Human Journey behind Food Is Medicine: A Participatory Study With a Lived Experience Advisory Group.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Poor diet is substantially associated with cardiometabolic diseases in the United States, yet systemic efforts to improve dietary behaviors remain limited. The American Heart Association's Health Care by FoodTM initiative seeks to advance Food Is Medicine interventions by integrating patient-centered insights into program design. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences of individuals managing diet-related chronic conditions to better understand the emotional, cultural, and systemic factors influencing dietary behavior change. METHODS: Using a participatory action research approach, a diverse Lived Experience Patient Advisory Group was convened. Fourteen participants engaged in a multiphase process including surveys, daily food diaries, individual interviews, and a 2-day in-person workshop. These activities were designed to elicit personal narratives, identify barriers and motivators to dietary change, and co-develop potential solutions. Thematic analysis was used to synthesize insights across all engagement activities. RESULTS: Fifteen subthemes emerged, grouped into 3 broader themes: facing change, understanding barriers, and acting. These themes highlighted the complex interplay between identity, social norms, access, and self-efficacy in shaping food choices. Participants also proposed a framework of opportunities for intervention, emphasizing the importance of support systems, culturally relevant education, and systemic alignment across health care, community, and policy sectors. CONCLUSIONS: Behavior change in food consumption is a deeply personal and socially embedded process. Centering lived experience in Food Is Medicine program design offers critical insights for creating more inclusive, effective, and sustainable interventions. This work underscores the need for coordinated, multilevel strategies to support dietary behavior change at scale.

recs.title: What constitutes healing after silent plaque rupture?
Impact of the 2026 Dyslipidemia Guideline on ASCVD Reclassification and Statin Recommendations in MESA.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2026 American College of Cardiology (ACC)/American Heart Association (AHA)/Multisociety Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia recommends the use of the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of cardiovascular disease EVENTs) equations to predict atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk while concurrently revising previous risk-category thresholds. The impact of these reclassifications is yet to be described. OBJECTIVES: The authors characterized ASCVD reclassification and statin recommendations under the 2026 guideline, evaluated clinical events under this reclassification, and examined risk enhancement with risk enhancers and coronary artery calcium (CAC) burden. METHODS: Adults (N = 6,098) from the MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) were assessed, comparing the Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE) and 2013 thresholds to PREVENT with 2026 thresholds. We evaluated the degree of directional reclassification, impact on statin recommendations, and risk enhancement with biomarkers and CAC burden. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 10 years, 6.0% of participants had an ASCVD event. PREVENT reclassified 16.4% to a lower and 13.1% to a higher risk category as compared to the PCE. The statin recommendation under PREVENT was 50.4% compared to 55.2% under PCE. Of those who were no longer recommended for statin use, 4.9% went on to have an event. Individuals who were reclassified downward but had elevated CAC or any risk-enhancing factors had a higher event rate. CONCLUSIONS: Adherence to the 2026 guideline may lead to a small net downward reclassification of predicted ASCVD risk. Statin recommendations will fall modestly, however, not accompanied by a substantial number of subsequent events. Risk enhancers and elevated CAC identify higher risk subgroups than their PREVENT risk would suggest, emphasizing their supporting role in risk prediction.

recs.title: Not all ultra-processed foods are equal: refining their role in cardiovascular risk.
Oral anticoagulation and cognitive outcomes in atrial fibrillation and Alzheimer's disease: considerations for longitudinal analyses.
Hyperuricemia From Early to Mid-Adulthood and Its Association With Cardiometabolic Diseases and Mortality.
Atrial Fibrillation and Risk of Late-Onset Dementia: A Danish Nationwide Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity, but its relationship with dementia remains incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to examine the association between AF and late-onset dementia in a nationwide Danish cohort. METHODS: In this Danish nationwide registry-based cohort study, individuals aged ≥50 years with first-time AF between 2005 and 2025 were matched 1:5 with controls from the general population on age, sex, and calendar year. Late onset dementia was defined as a first-time dementia diagnosis or antidementia medication initiation at age ≥65 years. Cumulative incidences were estimated at 1, 3, and 5 years, and associations were assessed using multivariable Cox regression. Secondary outcomes were thromboembolic events and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: A total of 326,687 AF patients and 1,633,435 matched controls were included (median age 75 years; 55% male). The median follow-up was 8.6 years. AF was associated with an increased hazard of late-onset dementia (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 1.12-1.17), which persisted after adjustment for cardiovascular comorbidity (HR: 1.17; 95% CI: 1.15-1.19) and exclusion of individuals with prior thromboembolic events (HR: 1.16; 95% CI: 1.13-1.18). The association remained stable across calendar periods, whereas the hazard of thromboembolic events attenuated over time. CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with late-onset dementia after adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors and exclusion of individuals with prior thromboembolic events. The stable association over 2 decades, despite attenuation of the association with thromboembolic events, suggests that dementia is an important long-term consequence of AF.

recs.title: Antenatal inflammation drives postpartum cardiac dysfunction in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
recs.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs), including preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, are strongly associated with maternal cardiac dysfunction during and after pregnancy. We hypothesized that maternal inflammation drives persistent postpartum cardiac maladaptation after HDPs. We conducted a prospective longitudinal study assessing cardiac function and circulating inflammatory profiles during pregnancy and 3-6 months postpartum, complemented by a preclinical mechanistic mouse model recapitulating key antenatal and postpartum immune and cardiac features of HDPs. Here we show that distinct antenatal inflammatory signatures, including elevated chemokines, correlated with adverse left ventricular structure and function 3-6 months postpartum, despite resolution of systemic inflammation. Mechanistically, our preclinical HDP mouse model demonstrates that reduced antenatal progesterone, also observed in patients with HDPs, drives inflammation and postpartum cardiac dysfunction. Antenatal (embryonic day 14.5), but not postpartum (postpartum day 28), progesterone treatment prevented postpartum cardiac dysfunction, identifying both a potential mechanistic and therapeutic strategy to reduce long-term maternal cardiovascular morbidity.

recs.title: Postoperative Inflammatory Response After Cardiac Surgery: Magnitude, Timing, and Prognosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery triggers a systemic inflammatory response. While this response is commonly interpreted as a marker of postoperative complications, its prognostic significance on short- and long-term death remains poorly characterized. We assessed the association between postoperative inflammation and short- and long-term all-cause death after cardiac surgery. METHODS: In a single-center retrospective cohort of patients undergoing cardiac surgery between 2011 and 2024, postoperative CRP (C-reactive protein) measurements and peak of postoperative CRP (CRPmax) and its timing were assessed. Association between CRPmax tertiles, delayed CRPmax (after postoperative day 3), and 30-day or 5-year all-cause death were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression models. RESULTS: A total of 7283 patients were included (mean age, 64.9 years; 72% men; 54% underwent coronary artery bypass grafting, 31% aortic valve replacement, and 94% on-pump surgery). Median CRPmax was 184 interquartile range, 134-246) mg/L. Median postoperative CRP peaked on postoperative day 3. Patients in the highest CRPmax tertile (tertile 3) more frequently presented with obesity, diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and chronic kidney disease. Compared with the lowest tertile, CRPmax tertile 3 was independently associated with higher 30-day (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.56 [95% CI, 1.78-3.68]; P<0.001) and 5-year all-cause death (adjusted HR, 1.41 [95% CI, 1.22-1.62]; P<0.001). A delayed CRPmax was independently associated with increased 30-day (adjusted HR, 2.61 [95% CI, 1.94-3.52]; P<0.001) and 5-year mortality rate (adjusted HR, 1.56 [95% CI, 1.37-1.77]; P<0.001). These associations persisted after adjustment for postoperative infection. CONCLUSIONS: Both the magnitude and timing of postoperative CRP peak were independently associated with short- and long-term death after cardiac surgery, irrespective of postoperative infection. These findings support close postoperative inflammatory monitoring after cardiac surgery.

recs.title: Building a Rural Cardiovascular Workforce Through Research Fellowship Immersion: Thad Waites Rural CVD Research Fellowship.
recs.abstract: Rural communities face significant challenges of access that disproportionately burden cardiovascular disease outcomes. Yet, cardiology training remains concentrated in urban tertiary. We describe the rationale, design, and prespecified evaluation framework of a launched 12-month rural cardiovascular research immersion fellowship. The program combines academic and community site-specific rotations in Washington, Mississippi, West Virginia, and Georgia with protected research time for a fellow-driven capstone project. The research activities are supported with educational modules of data and implementation science, leadership and policy, community immersion, and structured mentorship. The primary feasibility outcome is the proportion of 18 prespecified program deliverables completed by year-end. This pilot model is a transparent prospective evaluation of clinical research immersion in an expansive and diverse rural setting. This program will demonstrate the potential of nationally supported immersive research initiatives to produce measurable and more expansive competencies customized to training early-career cardiologists in the nuances of rural cardiovascular health.

recs.title: Right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling and long-term outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
Prognostic Value of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Artery Coupling in Mitral Valve Surgery and Impact of Concomitant Tricuspid Valve Repair.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling on clinical outcomes following mitral valve surgery with specific consideration of concomitant tricuspid valve repair remains uncertain. METHODS: A total of 214 patients who underwent mitral valve surgery and presented with moderate tricuspid regurgitation at the index procedure were included. Patients were classified after baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling (impaired versus normal). The primary study end point was a composite outcome of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary study end points included all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. RESULTS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was observed in 112 patients (52%), while 102 patients (48%) had normal right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling. The rate of concomitant tricuspid valve repair was similar between study groups (50.0% versus 49.0%, P=0.886). Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was associated with a higher hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 2.60, 95% CI 1.32-5.14, P=0.006), heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio 3.29, 95% CI 1.27-8.54, P=0.014), and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 2.25, 95% CI 1.11-4.59, P=0.025) during follow-up. Additionally, concomitant tricuspid valve repair in patients with moderate tricuspid regurgitation was associated with a lower hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.26-0.80, P=0.007). CONCLUSIONS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling is a predictor of adverse outcomes after mitral valve surgery. Concomitant tricuspid valve repair for moderate tricuspid regurgitation seems to be associated with improved outcomes.

recs.title: Sex-specific mortality in ischaemic heart disease across Western Europe: 2023 Global Burden of Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Ischaemic heart disease (IHD) mortality has declined across Western Europe, but conventional mortality rates may obscure whether women and men experience comparable outcomes once IHD is present. This study examined sex-specific prevalence-adjusted IHD mortality and risk factor-attributable population case fatality across Western European countries. METHODS: Global Burden of Disease 2023 estimates for IHD mortality and prevalence across Western European countries from 2013 to 2023 were analysed. Population case fatality was calculated as age-standardized mortality divided by age-standardized prevalence (mortality-to-prevalence ratio [MPR]). Risk factor-attributable mortality was normalized to IHD prevalence to derive case-fatality indices (CFIs) for metabolic, behavioural, dietary, and environmental exposures. Sex differences were quantified using women-to-men ratios (WMRs). Substantive disparities were defined by WMR deviation ≥20% from unity with <50% overlap of sex-specific uncertainty intervals. RESULTS: Between 2013 and 2023, IHD age-standardized mortality declined by 15.9% in men and 23.5% in women. The pooled Western Europe MPR decreased, from 2.26% to 2.09% in men and from 2.56% to 2.21% in women. Despite these improvements, substantive female excess in MPR was observed in Austria, France, Greece, Israel, Italy, and Spain, whereas substantive male excess was observed only in Iceland. Risk-specific CFIs showed female excess mainly for metabolic risk, low physical activity, and low fibre intake, whereas male excess was most evident for smoking and sugar-sweetened beverages. CONCLUSIONS: Declining IHD mortality across Western Europe conceals persistent sex-specific differences in population case fatality. Sex-disaggregated MPR and risk-specific CFIs may complement conventional surveillance and identify ecological signals, where declining mortality appears disproportionate to the estimated IHD burden.

recs.title: Epigenetic DNA Methylation Patterns Stratify Heart Failure Phenotypes and Predict Clinical Outcome.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Environmental and lifestyle exposures contribute substantially to heart failure (HF) development and progression. DNA methylation integrates cumulative environmental exposures and may provide insight into biological pathways and risk stratification across HF phenotypes. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to identify phenotype-specific DNA methylation patterns across HF subtypes and evaluate their association with clinical outcomes. METHODS: Individuals with symptomatic HF (universal definition stage C or D; HF with preserved ejection fraction, HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction, and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction [HFrEF]) from the MyoVasc (An Epidemiological Cohort Study to Investigate the Development and Progression of Heart Failure and the Interaction With Vascular Disease) cohort (N = 3,289) and individuals without cardiovascular disease from the population-based GHS (Gutenberg Health Study) (N = 18,700) were analyzed. Genome-wide DNA methylation from whole blood was measured using the Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC array. Phenotype-specific DNA methylation scores were derived using penalized regression models adjusted for cardiovascular risk factors. RESULTS: Distinct and partially overlapping DNA methylation patterns were identified across HF phenotypes, with limited overlap at the CpG level but substantial convergence at the gene level. Phenotype-specific methylation scores discriminated patients with HF from control subjects with high accuracy (area under the curve: 0.97-0.98). Methylation signatures in HF with preserved ejection fraction were associated predominantly with metabolic and inflammatory markers, whereas HFrEF signatures were more strongly linked to markers of myocardial injury and vascular disease. All methylation scores were independently associated with composite of cardiac death or hospitalization for worsening HF and all-cause mortality, with the strongest association observed for the HFrEF score (HR: ∼1.7 per SD). CONCLUSIONS: Symptomatic HF phenotypes are characterized by distinct and shared DNA methylation signatures. These epigenetic profiles reflect relevant biological pathways and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes, supporting their potential utility in HF risk stratification and precision medicine.

Diagnostic value of absent infarct-pattern LGE in patients with LV systolic dysfunction.

Real-World Safety and Effectiveness of Evolocumab in Japanese Patients With Familial Hypercholesterolemia: Postmarketing Survey Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Evidence on the real-world use of PCSK9 (proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9) inhibitors in familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) remains limited. This postmarketing surveillance study (NCT02808403) evaluated Japanese patients with FH and the long-term real-world effectiveness of evolocumab. METHODS: This analysis included patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) and homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH). Diagnostic pathways, patient characteristics, background lipid-lowering therapy, evolocumab use, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction, long-term target achievement, and findings in pediatric HoFH were assessed. RESULTS: Of 2117 patients in the safety analysis set (HeFH, n=2009; HoFH, n=108), 1380 (HeFH, n=1296; HoFH, n=84) were included in the effectiveness analysis. Compared with patients with HeFH, patients with HoFH had higher genetic testing rates (40.7% versus 9.8%), higher mean baseline LDL-C levels (188.4±107.3 mg/dL versus 139.2±58.3 mg/dL), and higher lipoprotein apheresis use (26.9% versus 2.1%), but fewer total comorbidities (2.2±1.5 versus 2.7±1.5). Statin use was similarly high in patients with HeFH and HoFH (92.2% and 93.5%, respectively) with many patients receiving low- to moderate-intensity statins. Most patients received evolocumab biweekly. LDL-C reductions were evident at 4 weeks and sustained at 104 weeks. At 104 weeks, mean LDL-C changes from baseline were -54.0% in patients with HeFH and -48.9% in patients with HoFH. LDL-C<70 mg/dL was achieved by 63.0% of patients with HeFH and 43.9% of patients with HoFH, and LDL-C<55 mg/dL was achieved by 48.2% and 17.1%, respectively. CONCLUSION: Evolocumab was associated with sustained LDL-C reductions over 104 weeks in Japanese patients with HeFH and HoFH, with higher target achievement in HeFH. Gaps exist in genetic testing and treatment optimization in routine Japanese FH care.

Leaders in Cardiology: Charalambos Antoniades.
Response by Heil et al to Letter Regarding Article, "Artificial Intelligence-Derived Volumetric High-Risk Plaque Features Are Predominantly Located Proximal to Maximal Luminal Stenosis".
Multiview Integration for Robust Echocardiographic Embeddings: Accessible AI for Clinical Practice.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although recent artificial intelligence (AI) foundation models have shown superior performance in medical imaging, their high computational demands and reliance on large data sets limit accessibility. These issues are especially pronounced in echocardiography, where integrating complex multiview measurements for individual cases hinders AI development and clinical translation. Vector embedding approaches offer promising solutions by leveraging compact representations in AI applications. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to develop a transformer-based multiview encoder that integrates multiple echocardiographic videos into unified vector embeddings and uses adversarial learning to reduce reliance on demographic shortcuts. METHODS: Using the MIMIC-IV-ECHO (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV-Echocardiography) data set (7,169 studies), we trained a multiview encoder to produce study-level embeddings and evaluated them on 21 binary classification tasks covering echocardiographic measurements and clinical diagnoses. We varied adversarial weights to assess their impact on demographic shortcut reliance and overall performance. RESULTS: The multiview encoder raised the mean area under the curve (AUC) across clinical tasks from 0.742 to 0.831 compared with the foundation model embedding (ΔAUC +0.090; 95% CI: 0.078-0.100), with significant gains in 20 of 21 tasks. The embeddings remained robust with a limited number of views (mean ΔAUC +0.071; 95% CI: 0.043-0.113). Adversarial learning reduced sex and race predictability only at strong weights and at substantial cost to clinical performance. CONCLUSIONS: The multiview encoder framework integrates multiple echocardiographic views into unified study-level embeddings, enabling substantial diagnostic improvements across diverse cardiac tasks. By producing compact, informative embeddings without requiring extensive computational resources, this approach lowers the cost of building echocardiographic AI on an existing foundation model.

recs.title: Implementation Feasibility and Clinical Utility of Phenomapping in Dilated and Hypokinetic Non-dilated Non-ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Despite phenotypic heterogeneity, the management of idiopathic non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) remains generalized and dominantly guided by left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (EF) and NYHA class. We aimed to develop a point-of-service phenomapping pathway for dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and hypokinetic non-dilated cardiomyopathy (HNDC) at time of CMR imaging leveraging the integration of i) patient self-reported health status, ii) imaging phenotype, and the iii) electronic health record (EHR). METHODS AND RESULTS: 1,355 patients (752 DCM and 603 HNDC) were followed for the composite MACE outcome of mortality, heart failure hospitalization or ventricular arrhythmia. K-means clustering was independently applied to DCM and HNDC derivation cohorts using 55 routinely captured features (16 patient-reported health variables, 19 CMR-derived, 14 EHR-derived, and 6 combined features), identifying three phenogroups in each cohort. Over a median of 3.9 and 3.7 years, 145 DCM patients (22%) and 65 HNDC patients (13%), respectively, experienced MACE. Adjusting for age, sex, NYHA class, and LV EF, phenogroup membership was independently associated with future outcomes. In DCM, the adjusted HR (95% CI) of phenogroups 2 and 3 versus Phenogroup 1 were 2.8 (1.6-4.8) and 3.5 (1.9-6.5), respectively (p<0.001 for both). In HNDC, Phenogroup 3 demonstrated an adjusted HR of 4.2 (1.7-10.2; p=0.001) versus Phenogroup 1. Prospective phenogroup assignment was enabled by a decision tree-classifier and validated in a temporal hold-out cohort. CONCLUSION: Phenomapping delivers incremental value to LVEF and NYHA for identification of high-risk NICM patients. These findings support value from standardized, point-of-service data integration for the delivery of phenomics-driven personalized care.

recs.title: Reply: 2-Year Patency as a Lightning Rod? Biological Hypotheses Linking PCSK9-Inhibition to Favorable Vein Graft Remodeling.
Early Left Bundle Branch Pacing for Complete Left Bundle Branch Block and Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction of 36%-50%: The EARLY-RESYNC Randomized Trial.
recs.abstract: AIMS: To compare the effects of early resynchronization with left bundle branch pacing (early-LBBP) versus guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) alone on cardiac function in patients with complete left bundle branch block (CLBBB) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 36%-50%. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this prospective, randomized, multicenter trial, 37 patients (mean age 60.5 ± 12.3 years, male 40.5%, LVEF 42.6% ± 6.0%) were assigned to early-LBBP plus GDMT (n=19) or GDMT alone (n=18). The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in the change of LVEF from baseline to 6 months. Secondary endpoints included changes in echocardiographic parameters and clinical outcomes. Analyses were performed according to the intention-to-treat principle. At 6-month follow-up, the adjusted mean improvement in LVEF was greater in the early-LBBP group than in the GDMT group (mean difference: 7.4%, 95% CI: 1.9 to 12.9%; P =0.013), with consistent findings in the per-protocol analysis. Early-LBBP was also associated with a greater reduction in LV end-systolic volume (-23.6mL; 95% CI: -42.3 to -4.8ml) and a higher rate of final LVEF ≥50% (78.9% vs. 38.9%) at 6 months compared with GDMT alone. CONCLUSION: In patients with CLBBB and LVEF 36%-50%, LBBP combined with GDMT resulted in greater improvement in LVEF at 6 months than GDMT alone. Larger randomized trials are needed to establish its long-term clinical benefits and optimal timing.

recs.title: Molecular signatures associated with reduced renal function in aortic regurgitation and aortic stenosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) accelerates aortic valve (AV) disease, yet the molecular pathways linking declining renal function to aortic regurgitation (AR) and aortic stenosis (AS) remain poorly defined. We aimed to characterize AV phenotype-specific molecular signatures associated with reduced renal function. METHODS: We performed an observational cross-sectional study using targeted proteomic profiling (Olink) in human AV from patients with AR or AS, stratified by renal function (eGFR≥60 vs < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2). Pathway enrichment analyses were performed using exploratory candidate proteins. Candidate molecular signatures were subsequently examined in independent cohorts (AR: n = 215; AS: n = 325) across renal function categories using histology, immunohistochemistry, ELISA, and qPCR. RESULTS: Reduced renal function was associated with distinct molecular patterns in AR and AS. In AR, exploratory proteomic profiling suggested enrichment of neutrophil degranulation, chemotaxis/adhesion and thrombo-inflammatory signaling pathways. Tissue characterization showed progressive extracellular matrix remodeling, collagen maturation, increased neutrophil markers (NGAL, MPO) and upregulation of pro-inflammatory (IL6, IL-8, IL-32, IL-33, CCL-2, TNF-α, RANTES), pro-adhesive (ICAM-1) and pro-thrombotic mediators (PAI-1) across renal function categories. In AS, exploratory proteomics suggested matrix disassembly and osteogenic signatures, while tissue characterization showed greater valvular calcification (BMP-2, -4, -9), collagen degradation (COL1, MMP-1, -3, TIMP-1) and inflammatory infiltration with declining renal function. Shared candidate proteins showed opposite regulation in AR and AS. CONCLUSIONS: Reduced renal function is associated with distinct, phenotype-specific patterns of AV remodeling-predominantly thrombo-inflammatory in AR and osteogenic-matrix-disruptive in AS- indicating heterogeneous molecular responses across the two major forms of aortic valve disease.

recs.title: Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease in a Primary Care Population of Young Adults by Disaggregated Race and Ethnicity.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States, with well-documented racial and ethnic disparities. Data are limited on incidence among patients aged <50 years, particularly within disaggregated Asian and Hispanic subgroups and individuals identifying with multiple racial or ethnic groups. We estimated CVD incidence rates for these groups and assessed whether disparities are explained by other clinical and demographic risk factors. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Sutter Health Electronic Health Record data (2010-2024) for adults aged 18 to 49 years with at least 2 primary care visits and a 2-year observed baseline period free of CVD. Incident CVD was defined as myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. We estimated incidence rates, applied age and sex standardization, and fit Cox proportional hazards models adjusting for additional risk factors. RESULTS: In a cohort of 1 178 551 patients, incidence was 1.14 cases per 1000 person-years (95% CI, 1.12-1.17). After standardization, Pacific Islander individuals (hazard ratio [HR], 2.90 [95% CI, 2.29-3.52]) and non-Hispanic Black individuals (HR, 2.82 [95% CI, 2.58-3.06]) had the highest incidence. Within the Asian group, Filipino individuals had the highest incidence (HR, 1.60 [95% CI, 1.42-1.79]). Hispanic subgroups showed less heterogeneity. Elevated HRs persisted among some groups after adjustment with Cox models. CONCLUSIONS: Young adult CVD incidence varied across racial and ethnic subgroups. Elevated risk persisted in several groups after adjustment, consistent with the influence of unmeasured social drivers. These findings support collection of granular racial and ethnic data and validation of existing risk prediction tools in young adult subgroups.

recs.title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced electrocardiography for detection and prediction of dilated cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: A major challenge in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) care is the identification and management of individuals at risk before disease manifestation. An artificial intelligence (AI) model applied to electrocardiography (ECG) was developed to detect and predict the echocardiographic DCM phenotype (left ventricular dilatation with systolic dysfunction) and was evaluated for its ability to stratify the risk of incident DCM in familial cohorts. METHODS: A deep learning model was trained to detect the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and to predict its future onset, using more than 330 000 ECG-echocardiogram pairs from the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston. Model performance was validated in cohorts from the UK Biobank, Zhongshan Hospital, and Antwerp University Hospital, and compared with models based on traditional ECG features and echocardiographic traits. To assess performance in familial DCM, genetically predisposed individuals identified through cascade screening at the cardiogenetics clinics of Antwerp University Hospital (n = 166, 18% DCM positive) and Maastricht University Medical Center (n = 177, 18% DCM positive) were evaluated. RESULTS: The AI-ECG model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of .87-.97 for diagnosing the prevalent DCM phenotype, outperforming traditional ECG parameters. AI-ECG was comparable to echocardiography for predicting future DCM (C-index .80-.87 and .80-.90, respectively). In familial cohorts, 5-year negative predictive values were 95.5% (Antwerp) and 91.5% (Maastricht), with corresponding positive predictive values of 42.4% and 39.4%, while high-risk scores were associated with a 5.1-6.4-fold increased risk of incident DCM. CONCLUSIONS: The explainable AI-ECG model detects the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and predicts future disease, and supports the exclusion of short- to mid-term disease in genetically at-risk individuals. This low-cost tool could help reduce surveillance burden and facilitate earlier intervention.

recs.title: Author Correction: Prospective validation of imaging and serum diagnostic biomarkers of steatohepatitis and fibrosis in MASLD: the LITMUS Imaging Study.
Nocturnal Respiratory Rate and Variability Predict Long-Term Mortality in Stable Outpatients With Cardiovascular Risk Factors.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory rate predicts short-term mortality in acute care settings, yet its prognostic significance in clinically stable outpatients remains poorly defined. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to determine whether the median and variability of nocturnal respiratory rate (NRR) are independently associated with long-term cardiovascular and all-cause mortality in outpatients with cardiovascular risk factors. METHODS: We analyzed overnight chest belt waveforms from elective polysomnography in 5,679 adults with cardiovascular risk enrolled in the Sleep Heart Health Study. NRR was quantified at 30-second resolution, and per-subject median NRR and within-night variability (interdecile range) were derived. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate associations with cardiovascular and all-cause mortality over 3-year and 15-year follow-up periods, adjusting for demographic characteristics, cardiopulmonary comorbidities, and sleep apnea severity. RESULTS: Higher median NRR and greater interdecile range of NRR were each associated with increased cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Combining these metrics stratified participants into low-, mid-, and high-risk groups with graded 3-year all-cause mortality; relative to the low-risk group, mortality risk increased stepwise in the mid-risk group (unadjusted HR: 1.91; 95% CI: 1.39-2.64; P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.09-2.10; P = 0.012) and the high-risk group (unadjusted HR: 4.17; 95% CI: 2.85-6.10; P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 2.80; 95% CI: 1.88-4.15; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Both the baseline level and variability of NRR independently predict mortality in clinically stable adults with cardiovascular risk. Densely profiled NRR represents a promising, underutilized biomarker for long-term risk stratification.

Once-Weekly Ribupatide for Weight Loss in Adults in China With Overweight or Obesity: The GEMINI-1 Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Obesity is a major health problem in China; more pharmacotherapy choices for long-term weight management are needed. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, for weight loss in adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial was conducted at 55 sites in China. From May to June 2024, adults without diabetes who had a body mass index of 28 or greater or 24 or greater with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity were enrolled, with final follow-up on June 20, 2025. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to receive once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide (target doses of 2 mg, 4 mg, or 6 mg) or matching placebo for 48 weeks, with dose escalation for up to 20 weeks and concomitant lifestyle intervention. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was change in body weight from baseline to week 48, including percent change in body weight and the percentage of participants achieving at least 5% body weight reduction, analyzed under the treatment policy estimand. RESULTS: Among 567 randomized participants (309 [54.5%] female; mean [SD] age was 34.4 [8.4] years, body weight was 93.0 [17.3] kg, and body mass index was 33.3 [4.5]), 514 (90.7%) completed the 48-week treatment period. Least-squares mean percentage changes in body weight at week 48 were -10.7%, -16.4%, and -17.7% with ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg, respectively, vs -1.4% with placebo. At week 48, the placebo-adjusted differences in percentage change in body weight were -9.3 (95% CI, -11.4 to -7.3) percentage points with ribupatide 2 mg, -15.0 (95% CI, -17.1 to -12.9) percentage points with ribupatide 4 mg, and -16.3 (95% CI, -18.4 to -14.2) percentage points with ribupatide 6 mg (P < .001 for all). For at least 5% body weight reduction at week 48, the multiply imputed response rates were 68.1% (95% CI, 59.9% to 75.3%) for ribupatide 2 mg (97 of 142), 88.0% (95% CI, 81.3% to 92.6%) for ribupatide 4 mg (124 of 141), 85.7% (95% CI, 78.6% to 90.7%) with ribupatide 6 mg (121 of 141), and 16.0% (95% CI, 10.8% to 23.1%) with placebo (23 of 143). Placebo-adjusted differences for ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg were 52.0 (95% CI, 42.2 to 61.9), 72.0 (95% CI, 63.7 to 80.2), and 69.7 (95% CI, 61.1 to 78.3) percentage points, respectively (all P < .001). The most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events with ribupatide were gastrointestinal events, occurring in 47.9%, 58.2%, and 63.1% of participants receiving ribupatide 2 mg, 4 mg, and 6 mg, respectively, compared with 23.1% receiving placebo; most were mild to moderate in severity and few participants (0.7%) permanently discontinued study treatment because of adverse events. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes, once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide resulted in significantly greater weight loss at 48 weeks. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent tolerability findings. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06396429.

recs.title: Residual Structural, Behavioral, and Social Barriers to Blood Pressure Control in an EHR-Integrated Remote Hypertension Program.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Remote hypertension programs improve blood pressure (BP) control, but which patient-level barriers matter once a program supplies education, monitoring, and pharmacist titration is unclear. OBJECTIVES: To quantify BP improvement in a pharmacist-led, electronic health record-integrated remote program and identify barriers independently associated with control. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study included 1,948 adults with uncontrolled hypertension (baseline BP >140/90 mm Hg) enrolled at least 6 months (median observation: 9.7 months). Health literacy and medication-affordability concerns were recorded at enrollment, with engagement measures and the ADI (Area Deprivation Index). Linear (systolic change) and logistic (control) models were adjusted for both barriers and clinical covariates (n = 1,744). RESULTS: Mean systolic reduction was 24.1 mm Hg (95% CI: 23.5-24.7); HEDIS (Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set) (<140/90 mm Hg) and clinical (<130/80 mm Hg) control reached 90.5% and 66.4%. Limited health literacy was associated with lower control (clinical OR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.50-0.88; HEDIS OR: 0.66) in a graded, linear fashion (per-level OR: 0.81; P < 0.001). Medication-affordability concern (HEDIS OR: 0.48; 95% CI: 0.29-0.78) and loss of a marital partner (HEDIS OR: 0.53) were likewise associated with lower control, with concordant linear estimates. Educational uptake, but not measurement frequency, was associated with control; no barrier acted through engagement, and associations survived ADI adjustment. CONCLUSIONS: A digital hypertension program achieved large BP reductions, yet limited literacy, medication affordability, and loss of a partner persisted as residual, overlapping barriers not explained by engagement or neighborhood deprivation. Screening for these barriers may extend program benefit through targeted support.

recs.title: Exploring the upper spectrum of physiological cardiac remodelling in Olympic athletes: insights from a CMR study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is essential for distinguishing physiological from pathological remodelling in athletes. However, cardiovascular screening protocols vary across studies, leaving uncertainty regarding the true upper limits of physiological adaptation. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to characterise the full spectrum of cardiac remodelling in Olympic athletes and to describe CMR-derived upper limits of cardiac remodelling according to sport category and sex. METHODS: Olympic athletes with negative comprehensive cardiovascular evaluation underwent voluntary non-contrast CMR. Left and right ventricular volumes, mass, and ejection fraction (EF) were quantified. Cardiac parameters were analysed according to the ESC sport classification and sex. Cluster analysis was performed to identify patterns of cardiac remodelling independently of sport category. RESULTS: A total of 320 athletes (age 26±5 years, 57% male; 13% skill sports, 19% power, 28% mixed, 40% endurance, 97% Caucasians) were included. Endurance athletes had the largest biventricular volumes and LV mass (all p-values <0.001), with no differences in EF across sport categories. Maximal interventricular septal thickness did not exceed 13 mm in males or 11 mm in females. Only 1% and 2% of athletes had LV or RV EF <50%, respectively, predominantly cyclists. Cluster analysis identified two phenotypes reflecting lower and higher degrees of remodelling, with substantial overlap across sport categories. The sex and sport categories were independently associated with the high-remodelling phenotype. CONCLUSION: CMR-derived cardiac adaptation in predominantly Caucasian, Olympic athletes varies according to sport category, with endurance athletes demonstrating the most pronounced remodelling. Maximal physiological LV wall thickness was 13 mm in males and 11 mm in females in this cohort, whereas LV EF <50% was uncommon despite marked cardiac remodelling. Finally, the overlap across sport categories and the identification of distinct remodelling phenotypes suggest that cardiac adaptation reflects a continuum rather than discrete sport-specific patterns.

recs.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Cardiovascular and Microvascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Analysis of the UK Biobank.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its associations across cardiovascular and microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 893 UK Biobank participants with type 2 diabetes, whole-exome sequencing, and no prevalent cardiovascular or microvascular complications. CHIP was defined from the curated UK Biobank call set by ≥1 driver variant with a variant allele fraction ≥2%. Associations with incident outcomes were evaluated using Fine-Gray models with multiple imputation for missing covariates. Driver-gene, clone-size, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: CHIP was present in 670 participants (3.7%) over a median follow-up of 14.6 years. CHIP was associated with the composite cardiovascular outcome (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR], 1.19 [95% CI, 1.00-1.42]), with heart failure showing the clearest component association (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.13-1.81]); acute coronary syndrome and stroke were not significantly associated. CHIP was also associated with the composite microvascular outcome (SHR, 1.34 [95% CI, 1.15-1.56]), broad chronic kidney disease (SHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.05-1.57]), and retinopathy (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.15-1.77]) but not neuropathy or strict diabetes-specific nephropathy. Ten-year adjusted risk differences were 1.94% and 3.46% for the cardiovascular and microvascular composites, respectively. Among 2919 proteins, ZBP1 (Z-DNA-binding protein 1) was the only protein retained after false-discovery-rate correction; no metabolite module was associated with CHIP after correction, whereas selected lipoprotein and amino acid/lactate modules were associated with cardiovascular outcomes, particularly heart failure. CONCLUSIONS: In adults with type 2 diabetes, CHIP was associated with a higher risk of incident microvascular complications and, among cardiovascular outcomes, most consistently with heart failure. Exploratory multiomic findings, including a protein-wide ZBP1 signal and selected metabolic associations with cardiovascular outcomes, provided additional biological context but require independent validation.

recs.title: Beyond Short-Term Relief: From External Dependence to Sustainable Pediatric Cardiac Surgery in Africa.
Anemia and Iron Deficiency Across Renal Function in Hospitalized Heart Failure: Insights From OPPORTUNITIES Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are highly prevalent among patients hospitalized for heart failure (HHF). Their prognostic contributions in the acute setting, particularly across kidney function, remain incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: We investigated the association of anemia, transferrin saturation (TSAT), and ID according to kidney function, with postdischarge outcomes in HHF patients. METHODS: Consecutive HHF patients enrolled in the OPPORTUNITIES registry with available hemoglobin and TSAT at discharge. The primary endpoint was HF-free survival, a composite of all-cause death, urgent heart transplantation, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and urgent emergency department referral for HF worsening at 12 months. Adjusted Cox regression models were applied. RESULTS: A total of 454 HHF patients were included. The median age was 77 (69-83); 37.9% were women, and 55% of patients were anemic. Anemic patients were older and exhibited a greater burden of comorbidities. Hemoglobin and TSAT showed a modest positive correlation overall (rho = 0.276, P < 0.001), which disappeared in patients with estimated glomerular filtration rate <30 mL/min/1.73 m2. Lower hemoglobin was independently associated with a higher risk (adjusted HR: 0.82; 95% CI: 0.75-0.91; P < 0.001), whereas TSAT was not independently predictive. A significant interaction between hemoglobin and renal function was observed (P = 0.025), indicating that the hemoglobin effect varied according to kidney function. Among ID definitions, only TSAT <20% independently identified patients at an increased risk (HR: 1.44; 95% CI: 1.03-2.03; P = 0.035). CONCLUSIONS: In HHF patients, the prognostic relevance of anemia varies according to renal function. TSAT <20% was the only ID definition independently associated with adverse outcomes.

recs.title: Deep Learning With Longitudinal Electrocardiograms Predicts Atrial Fibrillation Better Than a Single Electrocardiogram.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is often paroxysmal and asymptomatic, yet early identification could enable targeted surveillance. Deep learning can predict future AF from a single 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), but AF develops through progressive atrial remodeling. OBJECTIVES: We hypothesized that modeling each patient's longitudinal ECG history would improve 1-year AF prediction over a matched single-ECG model. METHODS: We developed a transformer-based model that accepts variable-length sequences of prior 12-lead ECGs with time-aware encoding of irregular intervals. We compared it with a single-ECG model sharing the same encoder, covariates, preprocessing, outcome definition, and splits. Models were developed at Weill Cornell Medicine/NewYork-Presbyterian and evaluated on MIMIC-IV-ECG without and with fine-tuning. The outcome was AF documented more than 1 and within 365 days after an index ECG. Discrimination used patient-cluster bootstrapping with 1 random index ECG per patient. RESULTS: Cohorts included 107,811 institutional and 55,307 MIMIC-IV-ECG patients. The fine-tuned longitudinal model with age and sex discriminated best (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: 0.85; C-index 0.84), exceeding the single-ECG model with age and sex (paired area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: +0.007; 95% CI: 0.003-0.012; +0.014 with ≥1 prior ECG). Without retraining on MIMIC-IV-ECG, the ECG-only advantage was confined to patients with ≥1 prior ECG (+0.014; 95% CI: 0.004-0.024). After external-domain adaptation, the matched advantage was +0.007 (95% CI: 0.002-0.012). High-risk patients had lower AF-free survival (HR: 8.8; 95% CI: 7.8-10.0). CONCLUSIONS: A longitudinal deep learning model using serial 12-lead ECGs improved 1-year AF prediction over a matched single-ECG model. Longitudinal ECG modeling may provide a scalable approach to identify patients warranting enhanced AF surveillance.

recs.title: Acute Kidney Injury Disrupts Cardiac Remodeling via SerpinA3N.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiorenal syndrome type 3 describes cardiac injury triggered by acute kidney injury (AKI). AKI caused by ischemia reperfusion injury represents a model for kidney injury during kidney transplant. It is well known that kidney transplant recipients are at increased risk to develop cardiac fibrosis; however, the molecular mechanisms linking renal injury to myocardial remodeling or cardiac fibrosis remain unclear. METHODS: Using a C57BL/6J mouse model of ischemia reperfusion injury-AKI, we combined proteomics and RNA seqencing transcriptomics to define early cardiac responses. We validated the proteomics and RNA sequencing data with quantitative polymerase chain reaction, ELISA, cytokine array, and western blotting for profibrotic and injury markers. We assessed SerpinA3N function using a granzyme B activity assay kit and XAV939, an inhibitor of SerpinA3N. Ingenuity pathway analysis further confirmed serine protease activity inhibition and increased expression of cardiac fibrosis-related genes after AKI. RESULTS: Successful establishment of renal ischemia reperfusion injury causing AKI, followed by significant induction of cardiac injury. AKI significantly upregulated SerpinA3N in the heart while suppressing serine protease (granzyme B) activity. Concomitantly, AKI hearts displayed elevated profibrotic genes (FN1, COL1A1, TGF-β1), mitochondrial dysfunction, and heightened inflammatory signaling. In vitro, inhibition of SerpinA3N with XAV939 restored granzyme B activity, confirming direct suppression by SerpinA3N. CONCLUSIONS: We conclude that SerpinA3N serves as a key mediator of cardiorenal syndrome type 3 pathogenesis, by inhibiting granzyme B, which promotes profibrotic remodeling in the heart following AKI. Targeting SerpinA3N could be a potential therapeutic approach that restores balanced extracellular matrix turnover and mitigates cardiac fibrosis.

recs.title: NNMT Safeguards Vascular Aging by Modulating an Endothelial LMNA-HSP Stress-Response Axis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: NNMT (nicotinamide N-methyltransferase) is a pivotal metabolic-epigenetic integrator that regulates cellular methylation balance. Although its expression and function exhibit profound, context-dependent heterogeneity in metabolic diseases and cancer, its role within the vascular system, particularly in aging endothelial cells, remains elusive. METHODS: We examined NNMT expression in a small, pathological, male-only cohort of older versus younger plaque-adjacent human carotid intimal donors, primary mouse aortic endothelial cells, and senescent human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Using endothelial-targeted adeno-associated virus-Tie systems, we assessed the effects of NNMT restoration and knockdown on vasodilation and arterial stiffness in aged mice. Mechanistic insights were obtained through exploratory multiomics integration. RESULTS: We established that NNMT expression exhibits an exploratory inverse association in a small, pathological, male-only cohort of older versus younger plaque-adjacent human carotid intimal donors, a pattern mirrored by declines observed in primary mouse aortic endothelial cells and senescent human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Functional assays demonstrated that NNMT restoration improves vasodilation and arterial stiffness in aged mice, whereas knockdown exacerbates these deficits. Mechanistically, exploratory multiomics integration, including Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation and transcriptomic analyses, suggests that NNMT-associated reduction in histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation occupancy at the LMNA (lamin A/C) promoter correlates with its transcriptional maintenance, a process influenced by S-adenosylmethionine supplementation. Downstream, we identified that NNMT-induced LMNA stabilization operates in concert with HSF1 (heat shock transcription factor 1) activation and nuclear translocation, a process accompanied by enhanced binding to HSP90 and HSP70 promoters to drive their transcription. Furthermore, we demonstrated that the vascular protective effects of the natural compound Heterophyllin B are mediated, at least in part, by NNMT, as these benefits were partially attenuated after endothelial NNMT knockdown in vivo. CONCLUSIONS: We identify a protective, age-dependent role for NNMT in vascular endothelium. Our findings reveal that NNMT maintains endothelial homeostasis through coordinated regulation of nuclear LMNA and the downstream HSP (heat shock protein) stress response, highlighting the therapeutic potential of this pathway for addressing age-related endothelial dysfunction.

recs.title: To Close or Not to Close, That Is the Question: A Neurological Perspective on Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion in High-Risk Atrial Fibrillation Patients.
Lipoprotein(a) and incident peripheral artery disease in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an atherogenic, prothrombotic lipoprotein linked to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but prospective data on its association with peripheral artery disease (PAD) in large, diverse U.S. cohorts are limited. We characterized the association of Lp(a) with long-term incident PAD risk in a diverse, community-based U.S. METHODS: We included Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study participants attending Visit 4 (1996-98) with measured Lp(a) and no prevalent PAD. Lp(a) was natural logarithm (ln)-transformed and categorized as <30, 30-50, and >50 mg/dL. Incident PAD was identified from hospitalization and procedure codes through 2019. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox models adjusted for confounders; Fine-Gray models and cumulative incidence functions accounted for competing mortality. RESULTS: Among 9727 participants (mean age 63.1 years, 53.9% women, 20.4% Black), 825 incident PAD events occurred over a median 22.5 years of follow-up. Lp(a) was <30 mg/dL in 69.7%, 30-50 in 11.7%, and >50 in 18.6%. Fully adjusted HRs were 1.27 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03-1.57) for 30-50 mg/dL and 1.32 (95% CI, 1.11-1.57) for >50 mg/dL versus <30 mg/dL; each unit increase in ln(Lp(a)) was associated with an HR of 1.14 (95% CI, 1.07-1.20). Estimates were similar accounting for competing mortality, and cumulative incidence differed across categories (p < 0.001). The association did not differ by baseline statin use. CONCLUSIONS: Higher Lp(a) was independently associated with greater long-term PAD risk in a community-based cohort, supporting Lp(a) as a risk factor for lower-extremity atherosclerotic disease and its value for risk stratification.

recs.title: Keeping Up Appearances-Or Measuring What Matters?
Safety and Efficacy of Topical Nitroglycerin for Radial Artery Dilation (The RADial Trial): A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transradial coronary catheterization is associated with a reduced risk of bleeding and vascular complications. Prior studies have evaluated nitroglycerin to improve transradial access by vasodilating the radial artery, but the optimal route of administration for preprocedural arterial dilation remains unclear. METHODS: In the RADial Trial (Radial Artery Dilatation Trial) patients undergoing transradial coronary catheterization were randomized in a double-blind fashion to receive either a placebo or topical nitroglycerin ointment (nitropaste). The primary outcome was the mean change in radial artery dimensions, assessed using paired t tests. Categorical outcomes were analyzed using odds ratio (OR) with 95% CI. RESULTS: A total of 260 patients (130 placebo, 130 nitroglycerin) were enrolled. Nitropaste significantly increased the mean diameter (2.65±0.6 versus 2.48±0.6 mm), circumference (8.37±1.63 versus 7.77±1.66) and cross-sectional area (5.63±2.28 versus 4.94±2.0 mm) of the radial artery, whereas no significant difference was observed in the placebo arm. Nitropaste was associated with a significant reduction in the number of skin punctures and risk of vasospasm (OR 0.34 [95% CI, 0.13-0.91], P=0.04). There was no significant difference between nitropaste and placebo groups in the odds of hematoma (OR, 0.32 [95% CI, 0.03-3.1], P=0.61), crossover to femoral access (OR, 2.29 [95% CI, 0.9-5.8], P=0.12), need for ultrasound-guided access (OR, 0.39 [95% CI, 0.13-1.15], P=0.13), and hypotension or headache (OR, 1.5 [95% CI, 0.24-9.2], P=1.0). CONCLUSION: Preprocedural administration of nitropaste significantly increases radial artery size and reduces the risk of vasospasm without causing headache or hypotension. REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05239013.

recs.title: One to move, one to clip: double transcatheter edge-to-edge repair technique for mitral regurgitation after annuloplasty ring dehiscence.
Lipid-Lowering Strategies in the Era of Early Atherosclerosis Detection: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
recs.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) begins early in life, driven in large part by cumulative exposure to low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and other atherogenic lipoproteins. Contemporary evidence from epidemiologic cohorts, genetic studies, imaging studies, and lipid-lowering trials supports a paradigm of earlier identification and more sustained treatment of individuals at increased ASCVD risk. This American College of Cardiology Scientific Statement reviews the rationale for early adoption of lipid-lowering strategies, with emphasis on lifetime lipid burden, inherited and acquired risk enhancers, and the role of subclinical atherosclerosis assessment. Available clinical trial data suggest that greater absolute low-density lipoprotein cholesterol reduction and longer treatment duration can reduce ASCVD events, even though direct evidence remains limited in younger populations at low short-term risk. Atherosclerosis detected by imaging may identify individuals whose ASCVD risk is underestimated by traditional calculators, but optimal strategies for screening, treatment thresholds, safety, adherence, cost-effectiveness, and value require further study. Clinicians should integrate estimated short- and long-term risk, lipid burden, risk enhancers, imaging findings when appropriate, and patient preferences to guide individualized, shared decision making to reduce lifetime ASCVD risk.

recs.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Super-High-Pressure Noncompliant Balloons for Treatment of Calcified Coronary Lesions: The VICTORY Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although calcified coronary lesions are associated with poor outcomes after percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI), randomized data guiding lesion preparation are limited. Small studies suggest potential benefits of super-high-pressure noncompliant balloons (SH-NCB); however, they have not been directly compared with intravascular lithotripsy (IVL). OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to conduct a randomized comparison of SH-NCBs vs IVL in calcified lesions. METHODS: In this open-label, randomized controlled, noninferiority trial with blinded outcomes assessment (ie, the PROBE design), patients aged ≥18 years with calcified coronary lesions were randomly assigned (1:1) to undergo lesion preparation with SH-NCBs or IVL before PCI with drug-eluting stents. All patients were required to undergo optical coherence tomography (OCT). The primary endpoint was final stent expansion (%) according to OCT. Secondary endpoints included procedural success, strategy success, target vessel failure, stent expansion <80%, and safety outcomes (eg, coronary perforation). RESULTS: Between December 21, 2022, and August 11, 2025, a total of 278 patients underwent the randomly assigned study procedure using plaque modification with SH-NCBs or IVL before stent implantation. The majority of patients (68%) had severe calcium based on an OCT Fujino score ≥4. Study procedures involving IVL tended to be longer and require more auxiliary devices compared with SH-NCBs. The median pressure applied with SH-NCBs compared with IVL was 40 atmospheres vs 6 atmospheres. Regarding the primary endpoint of stent expansion, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL (85% vs 84%; Pnoninferiority < 0.0001). The results were consistent across all subgroups, including calcium severity. Use of SH-NCBs, compared with IVL, resulted in similar rates of procedural and strategy success. Safety outcomes, specifically coronary perforations, did not differ between the 2 groups. At 30 days' follow-up, target vessel failure events (including cardiac death, target vessel revascularization, or myocardial infarction) occurred in 4 (2.8%) patients in the SH-NCB group and in 8 (5.7%) patients in the IVL group (HR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.15 to 1.66; P = 0.26). CONCLUSIONS: In calcified coronary lesions, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL for stent expansion and exhibited a comparable safety profile in experienced operators using intravascular imaging. (Value of IVL Compared To OPN Non-Compliant Balloons for Treatment of Refractory Coronary Lesions [VICTORY]; NCT05346068).

recs.title: Risk Stratification and Outcomes of Right Atrial Phasic Function in Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy: A Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Advanced arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy is associated with a high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (MVA) and end-stage heart failure (HF). However, the prognostic role of right atrial (RA) mechanics, as quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), remains largely unexplored. METHODS: Consecutive patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy undergoing CMR between 2014 and 2021 were retrospectively included. Demographics, clinical history, and strain parameters were collected. The primary clinical end points were end-stage HF and MVA. RESULTS: A total of 316 patients (mean age 38±15 years; 66.1% men) were included. Over a median follow-up of 5.3 years, 49 developed end-stage HF and 103 experienced MVA outcomes. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Gray models showed that impaired RA reservoir strain was an independent predictor of end-stage HF (hazard ratio [HR] 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, P<0.001) and MVA outcomes (subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99, P=0.025), with added prognostic value beyond clinical and imaging variables, improving the C-statistic to 0.84 and 0.70, respectively. Kaplan-Meier survival curves indicated that RA reservoir strain <18.6% was associated with higher end-stage HF risk, consistent across subgroups regardless of left ventricular involvement (both log-rank P<0.05). The association between RA reservoir strain <23.0% and MVA was significant in the overall cohort (P<0.001) and in patients without left ventricular involvement (P=0.002), but not in those with left ventricular involvement (P=0.08). CONCLUSIONS: Lower cardiac magnetic resonance-derived RA reservoir strain was independently associated with end-stage HF and MVA in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional risk markers. These findings support RA mechanics as a potential complementary component of multichamber CMR risk assessment, pending external validation.

recs.title: Patient-Reported Symptoms and Arrhythmias During Continuous ECG Monitoring After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Wearable ECG patches after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) enable continuous rhythm monitoring and allow symptoms reporting via trigger buttons and diary entries. However, the reliability of triggered events to identify clinically relevant arrhythmias after TAVI is uncertain. OBJECTIVES: We systematically analyzed patient-triggered events and their corresponding rhythm findings during 14-day ECG patch monitoring after TAVI. METHODS: Adult patients undergoing TAVI at a Swiss tertiary centre were prospectively enrolled and monitored with a 14-day ECG patch before discharge. Patients recorded any cardiac-related symptoms using the patch trigger button and/or diary function. RESULTS: Among 315 patients (median age 82 years [78-87], 43% female), median analyzable duration was 14 days [13-14]. At least one patient-triggered event was recorded in 94 patients (30%), with a median of 2 events per patient [1-4]. Atrial fibrillation (AF) was detected in 85 patients (27%), including 17 patients (5.4%) with new AF; however, only 20 patients with AF (24%) reported symptoms during AF episodes. Pauses occurred in 58 patients (18%) and high-grade atrioventricular block in 32 patients (10%), with no associated patient-triggered events. Ventricular tachycardia (≥4 beats) occurred in 165 patients (52%) and was entirely asymptomatic. Of 348 evaluable symptom-triggered events, 153 (44%) occurred without associated arrhythmia. The most frequent arrhythmias associated with symptom-triggered events were premature atrial contractions (21%), AF (14%), and premature ventricular contractions (11%). CONCLUSIONS: After TAVI, patient-triggered events during ECG patch monitoring poorly reflect objectively documented arrhythmias and fail to identify many clinically relevant rhythm disturbances. These findings support systematic continuous ECG surveillance beyond symptom-driven monitoring strategies after TAVI.

Cardiovascular risk, evaluation and management in patients with hypertriglyceridaemia: a Consensus Statement from the International Atherosclerosis Society.
recs.abstract: The prevalence of hypertriglyceridaemia is increasing globally owing to high rates of obesity and diabetes mellitus. Hypertriglyceridaemia is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, mediated through the cholesterol content of triglyceride-rich lipoprotein remnant particles rather than through triglycerides per se. Although plasma levels of triglycerides can be measured with a simple blood test, hypertriglyceridaemia remains underdiagnosed and undertreated. Hypertriglyceridaemia can result from various primary or secondary aetiologies, the identification and management of which is an important first step. Hypertriglyceridaemia can be managed with lifestyle measures, lipid-lowering therapy with statins in indicated patients to reduce cholesterol levels and, in refractory situations, with the addition of triglyceride-specific pharmacological therapies. Emerging therapies with considerable promise for the management of hypertriglyceridaemia include those targeting apolipoprotein C-III, angiopoietin-related protein 3 or fibroblast growth factor 21. However, so far, there is no evidence from randomized clinical trials that pharmacotherapies targeting triglycerides can reduce the occurrence of cardiovascular events, suggesting that elevated levels of triglycerides serve as a marker of atherosclerotic risk that should prompt optimization of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. In this Consensus Statement, we provide clinical context and evidence for the evaluation, diagnosis and management of hypertriglyceridaemia.

Tirofiban Prevents Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After Subarachnoid Hemorrhage in Aged Mice.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Microthrombi formation in the cerebral microvasculature has been demonstrated in animal models of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) as well as autopsy studies of patients with aneurysmal SAH, and microthrombi are thought to contribute to delayed cerebral ischemia and poor neurological outcomes. Our hypothesis was that treatment with tirofiban, an antiplatelet drug that inhibits glycoprotein IIb/IIIa, would reduce microthrombi formation and the subsequent sequalae, delayed cerebral ischemia, in aged mice. METHODS: SAH was induced via endovascular perforation in male mice, and blood injection in female mice, followed by treatment with either tirofiban or saline. Mice underwent daily neurological assessment for 6 days and then were euthanized. Magnetic resonance imaging scans were obtained on days 2, 4, and 6 after SAH to identify infarcted tissue. Magnetic resonance imaging perfusion and laser speckle contrast imaging were performed to evaluate cerebral perfusion. Postmortem microthrombi formation in the cerebral microvascular was quantified. RESULTS: Tirofiban treatment in male mice, compared with saline, led to reduced microthrombi formation, and prevented delayed infarct growth and neurological decline. In female mice, significant neurobehavioral improvements were observed, which corresponded with fewer brain microthrombi. No female mice had infarction, nor was delayed cerebral ischemia detected in any female mouse. CONCLUSIONS: After SAH in mice, treatment with tirofiban reduces both cerebral microthrombi formation and delayed infarct growth leading to a subsequent improvement in neurological outcomes.

Pulmonary Artery Pressures Predict Heart Failure Events Following Heart Failure and Non-Heart Failure Events.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: It is uncertain whether pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) within the first week after either hospitalization for a non-heart failure event (HFE) or hospitalization or urgent visit for a HFE predicts the risk of recurring events. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to determine if PAP following a non-HFE or HFE predicts subsequent events within 90 days. METHODS: The authors examined non-HFE and HFE in patients with heart failure (HF) treated with remote hemodynamic-guided management using a wireless PAP sensor in the GUIDE-HF study. They compared PAP trends before and after a non-HFE or HFE and stratified the admitting and discharge PAP during the index event into groups with a subsequent HFE, non-HFE, or no further events within 90 days. RESULTS: Following index non-HFE (615 events, n = 425), post-discharge diastolic PAP was significantly higher in patients with a subsequent HFE (23.3 ± 7.9 mm Hg) (n = 97) vs patients with a subsequent non-HFE (20.4 ± 7.3 mm Hg; P = 0.0046) (n = 189) or no further events (20.9 ± 7.4 mm Hg; P = 0.015) (n = 329). Following index HFE (539 events, n = 358), post-discharge diastolic PAP was numerically higher in patients with a subsequent HFE (23.9 ± 6.9 mm Hg) (n = 199) than in patients with a subsequent non-HFE (22.0 ± 7.1 mm Hg; P = 0.078 (n = 102) and in those with no further events (22.0 ± 7.6 mm Hg; P = 0.021) (n = 238). Similar trends were observed for HF with reduced ejection fraction and HF with preserved ejection fraction subgroups and with systolic and mean PAP. CONCLUSIONS: Persistently elevated PAP early after discharge following either an index non-HFE or an HFE is associated with the risk of a subsequent HFE. (Hemodynamic-GUIDEd Management of Heart Failure [GUIDE-HF]; NCT03387813).

recs.title: Ventricular Morphology and Atrioventricular Valve Regurgitation in Adults Post-Fontan: Associations With Exercise Hemodynamics.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) dominance and atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR) are associated with adverse outcomes post-Fontan palliation, but their underlying hemodynamic correlates, particularly during exercise, remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: In this cross-sectional cohort, exercise hemodynamics by ventricular morphology and AVVR severity were assessed invasively (supine exercise catheterization) in 108 individuals and semi-invasively (semisupine exercise with echocardiography and peripheral venous pressure) in 108. RESULTS: Age of the invasive cohort was 32.1 (25.6-37.2) years; 41 had RV dominance, 19 had moderate or severe AVVR, and 16 had both. Resting and peak mean pulmonary artery pressure and pulmonary artery wedge pressure were similar across ventricular morphologies and AVVR severity. However, RV dominance was associated with lower systemic (systemic blood flow, 67% [22-93] versus 86% [63-105] predicted; P=0.006) and pulmonary (pulmonary blood flow, 57% [33-75] versus 72% [61-89] predicted; P<0.001) cardiac output responses to exercise and steeper Δpulmonary artery pressure/Δpulmonary blood flow, (4.3 [2.6-10.6] versus 3.0 [1.7-4.8] mm Hg/L per minute; P=0.004). Patients with moderate or severe AVVR showed a similar pattern, with lower systemic blood flow (64% [19-92] versus 77% [57-101], P=0.10) and pulmonary blood flow (57% [36-74] versus 70% [55-88] predicted, P=0.03) responses. Findings were replicated in the semi-invasive cohort, where RV dominance and moderate or severe AVVR were associated with lower peak systemic blood flow and higher Δperipheral venous pressure/Δ systemic blood flow, despite similar peak peripheral venous pressure. CONCLUSIONS: Resting and exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure, pulmonary artery pressure, and peripheral venous pressure are unrelated to ventricular morphology and AVVR severity. Conversely, impaired flow augmentation and steeper pressure-flow relationships during exercise were associated with RV dominance and moderate or severe AVVR, emphasizing the role of dynamic provocation to unmask occult cardiovascular reserve limitations.

Liver radiomics on routine cardiac CT identifies hepatic stress states that predict heart failure.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Heart failure (HF) prevention remains limited because early multisystem cardiometabolic dysfunction is not captured by conventional risk tools. We evaluated whether liver radiomic phenotypes derived opportunistically from coronary artery calcium computed tomography (CAC-CT) identify imaging-defined hepatic stress states associated with incident HF. METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 59 237 individuals undergoing CAC-CT (CLARIFY: 46 028; Houston Methodist: 13 209). Liver regions were segmented and radiomic features extracted to derive a Liver Radiomics Score (LRS). The model was trained in a CLARIFY derivation cohort (Dtr, n = 9205), validated in a hold-out cohort (Dts, n = 36 823), and externally evaluated in Houston Methodist (Dext, n = 13 209). The mean follow-up was 1411 days (SD 760.1) in the pooled Dtr and Dts cohorts (1144 HF events) and 470 days (SD 596) in Dext (212 HF events). Continuous LRS was associated with incident HF [Dts: hazard ratio (HR) 1.63, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-1.74; P < 0.001; Dext: HR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.07; P = 0.004] and remained significant after multivariable adjustment in Dts. Increasing LRS quartiles showed progressively adverse hepatic, haemodynamic, and cardiometabolic profiles and higher HF risk. Among 17 806 Dts participants with PREVENT data, adding LRS modestly improved discrimination across CAC- and PREVENT-based models (P < 0.001) and improved reclassification metrics (7-year net reclassification improvement up to 0.25; including integrated discrimination improvement up to 0.015). High LRS identified elevated risk in low-risk groups: among participants with CAC=0, high LRS conferred ∼2.5-fold higher 5-year HF incidence, and ∼2.9-fold in PREVENT-low individuals. CONCLUSION: In this large multicentre cohort, liver radiomics from CAC-CT captured hepatic stress states linked to HF risk and modestly improved risk stratification beyond CAC and PREVENT scores.

Associations of Cumulative Wrist Accelerometer-Derived Physical Activity and Proxies of Sedentary Behavior With Early Cardiac Remodeling in Healthy Adolescents.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Physical inactivity and sedentary behavior are associated with adverse cardiac remodeling in adults, but evidence in adolescence remains limited. This study examined associations of cumulative accelerometer-derived physical activity and proxies of sedentary behavior during adolescence with early subclinical cardiac features assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance. METHODS: A total of 111 adolescents (55.9% girls) wore a wrist-worn triaxial accelerometer at ages 12, 14, and 16 years to measure physical activity and sedentary behavior proxies. A 3-Tesla cardiovascular magnetic resonance scan was performed at final follow-up to assess cardiac structure and function. Multivariable linear regression models examined associations between cumulative physical activity and sedentary behavior proxies and cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived metrics. RESULTS: Daily step counts were positively associated with indexed end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes of the left ventricle (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 0.90 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.42-1.37]; 0.36 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.10-0.63], respectively) and the right ventricle (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 1.03 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.44-1.61]; 0.44 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.05-0.82], respectively), and with reduced right ventricular longitudinal strain (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 0.53% [95% CI, 0.16-0.91]). Greater time spent in sedentary bouts and a higher number of sedentary bouts were associated with increased left atrial active emptying fraction (adjusted β per 100 min/d, 8.21% [95% CI, 0.09-16.34]; adjusted β per 1 bout/d, 1.76% [95% CI, 0.17-3.35], respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Physical inactivity and sedentary behavior proxies during adolescence were independently associated with early markers of ventricular and atrial remodeling. These findings highlight early cardiac adaptations related to lifestyle behaviors and underscore the importance of promoting active lifestyles from a young age.

Exercise Test Findings in the Long-Term Outcomes After Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MUSIC) Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) commonly presents with cardiovascular involvement, but the frequency of exercise-related arrhythmias and exercise capacity are poorly defined. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to describe exercise stress testing (EST) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) after MIS-C. METHODS: We summarized EST and CPET results from the MUSIC (Long-terM OUtcomes after the Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome In Children) study (1,204 participants, 32 North American sites). Demographics and details of hospitalization from participants undergoing clinical EST were compared to participants ≥5 years who did not undergo EST. Site reported results of EST and CPET were described. RESULTS: EST was performed in 22% (208/932) at a mean of 150 ± 110 days after hospitalization. Compared with those who did not undergo EST (n = 724), the EST cohort was older (12.2 vs 10.5 years) and had higher rates of intensive care unit admission (77.4% vs 63.8%), vasoactive infusions (57.2% vs 46.1%), troponin elevation (64.4% vs 51.0%), and coronary artery aneurysm (22.7% vs 0.4%) (all P ≤ 0.01). During EST, only 1% (2/208; 95% CI: 0.1%-3.4%) exhibited premature ventricular contractions and no sustained ectopy. Among 160 participants undergoing CPET, 75.6% (121/160; 95% CI: 68.2%-82.1%) achieved oxygen consumption/kg ≥ 80% predicted, and 83.8% (134/160; 95% CI: 77.1%-89.1%) achieved an oxygen pulse ≥80% predicted. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing exercise testing after MIS-C, most had normal exercise capacity, no sustained arrhythmias occurred, and premature ventricular contractions were rare.
