Blood pressure and arterial stiffness in the pathway between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular risk: exploratory mediation analysis in middle-aged and older adult men.
recs.abstract: AIMS: The extent to which blood pressure (BP) and arterial stiffness mediate the association between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular risk, and whether individuals with metabolic impairment are more susceptible, remain unclear. METHODS: Within the "Risk of Cardiovascular diseases and abdominal aortic Aneurysms in Varese" (RoCAV) cohort, we retained 2119 men aged 50-75 and free of coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke at baseline; carotid-femoral Pulse Wave Velocity (cfPWV) was measured in a subset of 1015 using an automated oscillometer. Exposure was the 12-month mean PM2.5 concentration before baseline (EXPANSE models); outcome was incident major acute CHD or stroke (MACE), fatal or non-fatal. We estimated the mediating contribution of BP and cfPWV through Marginal Structural Models and Aalen survival models, with individual- and area-level confounders. RESULTS: In a median follow-up of 7.6 years, 178 MACE events occurred (rate=1155 per 100,000 person-years), and 76 (1086/100,000 p-y) in the cfPWV subset. Systolic BP, mean BP, brachial pulse pressure and cfPWV were highest in the most exposed. Each 1-µg/m3 increase in PM2.5 was associated with 151 (95%CI:21-282) additional MACE events per 100,000 p-y, of which 48 (95%CI:17-79) were mediated by cfPWV (mediated proportion: 32%). Systolic BP and brachial pulse pressure each mediated about 16% of the PM2.5-associated risk. The cfPWV-mediated effect was enhanced in men with impaired glucose (96;95%CI:38-155) and elevated LDL-cholesterol (88;95%CI:28-147). CONCLUSIONS: Large-artery stiffness substantially contributes to the MACE burden associated with chronic PM2.5 exposure, especially in men with metabolic impairment. Monitoring cfPWV may help incorporate environmental risk into cardiovascular prevention.

Modified Posterior Wall Ablation in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: the BOX-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: AIMS: The efficacy of left atrial posterior wall isolation (PWI) for persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) is controversial. We propose a modified left atrial posterior wall ablation strategy. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of modified posterior wall ablation in patients with persistent AF who underwent first-time radiofrequency catheter ablation. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this multicenter, single-blind randomized trial, 276 patients with persistent AF were assigned 1:1 to pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) with (BOX+) or without modified posterior wall ablation (BOX-). Seven participants withdrew, leaving 269 (BOX+, n=139; BOX-, n=130) for primary endpoint analysis. The primary endpoint was freedom from any documented atrial arrhythmia lasting > 30 seconds without antiarrhythmic drugs after a 3 -month blanking period. At 12-month follow-up, the primary endpoint occurred in 120 of 139 patients (86.3%) in the BOX+ group and 113 of 130 (86.9%) in the BOX- group (hazard ratio 1.046, 95% CI, 0.54 - 2.01; P = 0.894). The BOX+ group exhibited longer procedure time and ablation time. Acute successful PWI was achieved in 91 (65.5%) patients assigned to BOX+. In a nonprespecified, post-randomization analysis, arrhythmia-free survival was 93.4% in patients with acute successful PWI, 72.9% in those with attempted but unsuccessful PWI, and 86.9% in controls without attempted PWI (overall log-rank P=0.002). Adverse events were similar between groups. CONCLUSION: Routine addition of modified posterior wall ablation did not improve overall outcomes of first-time ablation in persistent AF. However, achieving successful PWI was associated with significantly lower recurrence.

recs.title: Diet-Driven Modulation of the Gut Microbiome to Enhance Neuroplasticity and Cognitive Recovery After Ischemic Stroke.
recs.abstract: Cognitive impairment and limited neuroplastic recovery remain major contributors to long-term disability following ischemic stroke. Increasing evidence suggests that stroke-induced disruption of the gut-brain axis, characterized by microbiome dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolite signaling, may influence post-stroke inflammation, synaptic remodeling, and cognitive outcomes. Diet is a key modifiable determinant of gut microbiome composition and metabolic output, yet its role in post-stroke neuroplasticity has not been comprehensively synthesized. This narrative review examines dietary interventions with mechanistic or translational relevance to ischemic stroke recovery, including Mediterranean dietary patterns, ketogenic diets, high-fiber and prebiotic-enriched diets, probiotic and synbiotic supplementation, and intermittent fasting or caloric restriction. We summarize evidence linking diet-induced microbiome modulation to neuroinflammatory regulation, short-chain fatty acid signaling, microglial activity, mitochondrial function, and synaptic plasticity. Shared and diet-specific pathways are discussed, along with current limitations of the evidence base and barriers to clinical translation. Collectively, available data support a biologically plausible role for targeted dietary modulation of the gut microbiome as an adjunctive strategy to enhance cognitive recovery and neuroplasticity after ischemic stroke. Further well-designed clinical studies integrating microbiome profiling, neuroimaging, and cognitive outcomes are needed to define therapeutic potential and guide implementation in stroke rehabilitation. Among these dietary interventions, Mediterranean, high-fiber, and prebiotic-enriched diets currently have the strongest available evidence, while ketogenic and intermittent fasting approaches remain the least supported based on existing clinical and translational evidence.

recs.title: Discontinuation of Anticoagulation in Patients at Relatively High Risk of Stroke After Successful Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulant (OAC) discontinuation after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation may be feasible in selected patients; however, outcomes in those at high stroke risk remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate associations between OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after ablation and thromboembolic or bleeding events across CHA2DS2-VA risk strata. METHODS: Patients without AF recurrence within 12 months of catheter ablation and with CHA2DS2-VA scores ≥2 were identified from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database and classified as OAC continuers or discontinuers based on prescription coverage at the 12-month landmark. The primary outcome was a composite of stroke or systemic embolism and major bleeding. Doubly robust estimation combined overlap weighting with covariate-adjusted Cox regression, stratified by CHA2DS2-VA score (2-4 and ≥5). RESULTS: Among 3,637 patients (mean age: 60.8 ± 9.7 years, 27.1% female, mean CHA2DS2-VA 3.2 ± 1.3), discontinuation in those with scores of 2-4 (n = 3,054) was associated with lower risks of the composite event (HR: 0.61; 95% CI: 0.38-0.96) and major bleeding (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.29-0.90), without increased stroke or systemic embolism (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.34-1.58). In those with scores ≥5 (n = 583), discontinuation was not significantly associated with any outcome, and tests for interaction were not significant (all P > 0.46). CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after AF ablation was associated with decreased bleeding risk without a corresponding increase in thromboembolic events among patients with CHA2DS2-VA score 2 to 4.

recs.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Atrial Fibrillation Patients With High Risk of Stroke and Bleeding: An Individual Participant Data Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is increasingly used as an alternative to oral anticoagulation for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation. Its comparative effectiveness and safety in patients at a high risk of both stroke and bleeding remain uncertain. OBJECTIVES: We evaluated the efficacy and safety of LAAC vs contemporary medical therapy in a high-risk population using individual participant data from randomized trials. METHODS: Bibliographic databases and trial registries through August 5, 2026, were searched for randomized trials comparing percutaneous LAAC with contemporary medical therapy in populations with a trial-level mean CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥4. A 1-stage common-effect analysis used Cox models stratified by trial and adjusted for age, sex, CHA2DS2-VASc score, and HAS-BLED score. Both primary outcomes were time to first stroke, systemic embolism, or cardiovascular/unknown death (efficacy) and time to first major bleeding (safety). A flexible time-varying Cox model was used for major bleeding. The protocol was submitted to PROSPERO (CRD420261335972). RESULTS: CLOSURE-AF (Left Atrial Appendage CLOSURE in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Compared to Medical Therapy) and PRAGUE-17 (Left Atrial Appendage Closure vs. Novel Anticoagulation Agents in Atrial Fibrillation) contributed 1,290 participants (647 assigned to LAAC and 643 to control). Median age was 77.3 years (Q1-Q3: 71.4-81.9 years), and 809 participants (62.7%) were men. The primary efficacy outcome occurred in 142 LAAC participants (21.9%) and 133 control subjects (20.7%) (adjusted HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.77-1.24; P = 0.842). Major bleeding occurred in 86 LAAC participants (13.3%) and 80 control subjects (12.4%) (adjusted HR: 1.03; 95% CI: 0.75-1.39; P = 0.874). The treatment effect on major bleeding varied over time (P for treatment-by-time interaction < 0.001), with a cumulative major bleeding incidence of 9.4% with LAAC vs 6.0% with control (absolute risk difference, 3.4 percentage points; 95% CI: 0.4-6.3 percentage points) at 1 year and 13.2% vs 12.1% (absolute risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI: -2.8 to 5.0 percentage points) at 3 years. CONCLUSIONS: In high-risk patients with atrial fibrillation, no statistically significant difference was detected between LAAC and contemporary medical therapy for the primary efficacy outcome or major bleeding. The major bleeding hazard varied over time, with higher early and lower later conditional hazard estimates; however, a cumulative bleeding benefit was not demonstrated by 3 years. Long-term randomized data are needed to improve the precision of later treatment-effect estimates.

recs.title: Anterior mitral leaflet modification to prevent left ventricular outflow tract obstruction during transcatheter mitral valve replacement: the PROTECT-LVOT registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains the major limitation of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates. METHODS: We established a multicentre retrospective registry of consecutive patients undergoing TMVR with AML modification between 2017 and 2025. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, and major bleeding. RESULTS: A total of 55 patients were included (67% females). The median age was 78 years (interquartile range [IQR] 73-81); the median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality was 6.7% (IQR 4.8-9.5). AML modification was performed in 65.5% of cases with the Laceration of the Anterior Mitral leaflet to Prevent Outflow ObstructioN technique and in 34.5% with the Balloon-Assisted Translocation of the Mitral Anterior Leaflet technique. AML modification was successful in 96.4% of cases. Despite successful AML modification, haemodynamically significant LVOT obstruction occurred in 12.7% of cases. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint occurred in 20.0% of patients, driven by cardiovascular death in 14.5% of patients. Overall in-hospital mortality was 16.4%. The ViMAC substrate was associated with the numerically highest LVOT obstruction rate (ViMAC 20.7%, ViR 0.0%, ViV 8.3%, odds ratio [OR] 4.72, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.89-47.86; p=0.070). The aortomitral angle showed a borderline association with LVOT obstruction (OR 1.22 per degree, 95% CI: 0.99-1.48; p=0.059). CONCLUSIONS: AML modification enables TMVR in high-risk anatomies with high feasibility but does not eliminate LVOT obstruction. ViMAC represents the most challenging substrate.

recs.title: Temporal Changes in Lipoprotein(a) Following Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined cardiovascular risk factor generally considered stable over an individual's lifetime. Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) may transiently alter Lp(a) concentrations, complicating interpretation. We systematically evaluated temporal changes in Lp(a) following ACS. METHODS: This PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review searched MEDLINE and Embase from database inception to February 2026. Eligible studies reported serial Lp(a) measurements at two or more time points after index ACS event. Exploratory random-effects meta-analysis of percent change in mean Lp(a) was performed. RESULTS: Of 3,811 records, 16 studies comprising 1,396 patients met inclusion criteria. Lp(a) demonstrated a dynamic post-ACS trajectory. Using initial post-ACS measurements as the reference, pooled percent change in mean Lp(a) was non-significant at 24 hours post-ACS (+2.5%, 95% CI -6.8 to 11.7; p=0.602). Lp(a) was significantly higher at 7-14 days (+44.0%, 95% CI 4.0-84.1; p=0.031), 1 month (+28.3%, 95% CI 2.7-54.0; p=0.030), and 3-6 months (+22.2%, 95% CI 2.4-42.0; p=0.028). Across two studies, absolute Lp(a) increases >25 nmol/L occurred in 17% and 22% of patients by 3 and 6 months, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Lp(a) is not static post-ACS. Early post-ACS measurements may underestimate long-term concentrations and risk. Repeat measurement weeks to months later is most informative when initial post-ACS Lp(a) values are near clinical decision thresholds or would influence eligibility for emerging Lp(a)-lowering therapies.

Early Implementation of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy and Outcomes in Cardiogenic Shock Supported by Micro-Axial Flow Pumps.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) supported by mechanical circulatory support remains poorly defined. The feasibility and potential benefits of early GDMT initiation during Impella support are uncertain. METHODS: We analyzed a multicenter prospective registry of consecutive patients with CS treated with Impella between 2020 and 2024. GDMT exposure was defined as the number of heart failure therapies administered at device explantation. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinical severity and early shock trajectory. Landmark analysis excluded patients dying within 5 days, while mixed-effects models accounted for center-level clustering. RESULTS: Among 140 patients (mean age 61 years; 20% female), 40% received concomitant ECMO (ECPella). In-hospital mortality was 38%. At explantation, 43% received at least one GDMT agent. Greater GDMT exposure was independently associated with lower mortality (OR 0.28 per additional therapy; 95% CI 0.14-0.58; p<0.001). This association remained consistent in landmark analysis (adjusted OR 0.31; 95% CI 0.16-0.66; p<0.001) and after excluding patients with cardiac arrest (adjusted OR 0.48; 95% CI 0.23-0.88; p=0.002). A graded relationship between GDMT intensity and survival was observed. Center-level variability was negligible (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CS supported by Impella, early GDMT implementation was feasible in a substantial proportion of patients. Greater GDMT exposure at device explantation was associated with lower in-hospital mortality. Ventricular unloading may provide an opportunity to initiate outcome-modifying therapies during the acute phase of CS.

Biological Aging Associates With Preeclampsia and Gestational Hypertension.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Biological aging is a fundamental driver of chronic disease, yet its role in the cause of preeclampsia and gestational hypertension remains poorly defined. METHODS: We used a multimodal framework that triangulated genetic, epidemiological, and experimental approaches to assess the associations of biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension. Publicly available human and mouse transcriptomic data were analyzed to identify shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures, while the potential of nicotinic acid to alleviate aging- and preeclampsia-related features was further evaluated in experimental models. RESULTS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization demonstrated that biological age acceleration was associated with higher odds of preeclampsia (odds ratio, 1.55 [95% CI, 1.22-1.96]; P=2.67×10-4) and gestational hypertension (odds ratio, 1.56 [95% CI, 1.12-2.19]; P=0.009), while positive genetic correlations were also observed for both outcomes. In the nested case-control study, higher early pregnancy biological age acceleration was consistently associated with preeclampsia risk in both primary (odds ratio, 1.16 [95% CI, 1.01-1.35]; P=0.047) and sensitivity (odds ratio, 1.14 [95% CI, 1.03-1.29]; P=0.042) analyses, with the associations persisting after covariate adjustment and exclusion of systolic blood pressure from biological age acceleration calculation. Mouse models exhibited preeclampsia-like features accompanied by concordant alterations in biological age-related biomarkers and telomere dysfunction. These changes were partially attenuated by nicotinic acid treatment, whereas placental organoids showed limited growth responses to nicotinic acid. Complementing these phenotypic observations, transcriptomic analyses identified shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures across human and mouse data sets. CONCLUSIONS: Convergent evidence links biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, particularly biological age acceleration with preeclampsia. Experimental findings provide complementary context but do not establish a specific mechanism or therapeutic role for nicotinic acid.

Side Effects of Low-Dose Colchicine in Chronic Coronary Disease: A Post Hoc Analysis of the LoDoCo2 Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-dose colchicine reduces cardiovascular events in patients with chronic coronary disease. However, side effects may compromise compliance and lead to discontinuation of treatment. Therefore, we aimed to assess the incidence of side effects leading to discontinuation of treatment in the LoDoCo2 (Low-Dose Colchicine 2) trial. METHODS: The LoDoCo2 trial was a randomized controlled trial evaluating colchicine versus placebo in patients with chronic coronary disease. Participants entered a 30-day open-label run-in phase during which all participants received colchicine 0.5 mg once daily, followed by randomization to colchicine or placebo. Tolerability-related side effects leading to treatment discontinuation were evaluated at the end of the 30-day run-in phase and during the randomized phase (median follow-up, 29.5 [interquartile range, 21.6-47.4] months). Cumulative incidence of side effects was presented using Kaplan-Meier curves and compared by treatment arm using Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: During the 30-day run-in phase, 618 of 6519 (9.5%) participants reported side effects. Women had a higher risk of side effects than men during the 30-day run-in phase (odds ratio, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.23-1.89]). After randomization, 114 participants (4.2%) in the colchicine group and 120 (4.4%) in the placebo group discontinued treatment due to side effects (hazard ratio [HR], 0.95 [95% CI, 0.73-1.22]). Gastrointestinal symptoms were most common (colchicine 2.0% versus placebo 1.7%) followed by myalgia (colchicine 1.2% versus placebo 1.6%). No differences in the risk of side effects between colchicine and placebo were seen for any of the subgroups. Women did have a higher risk of reporting side effects compared with men, regardless of assigned treatment (HR, 1.66 [95% CI, 1.22-2.25]). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with chronic coronary disease that tolerated initial treatment with low-dose colchicine, long-term discontinuation due to side effects was uncommon and did not differ between colchicine and placebo. recs.title: Standards Defining Echocardiography Core Laboratory (ECL) in Clinical Practice and Research.
recs.abstract: Echocardiography is extensively utilized in both clinical practice and research due to its accessibility. Echocardiography core laboratories (ECLs) adhering to societal guidelines offer superior readings and interpretations compared with the on-site assessments by reducing measurement variability and enhancing study precision. In the present work, we aim to define minimum standards for clinical echocardiography laboratories and research ECLs based on recommendations from the American Society of Echocardiography and the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging, as well as on expert opinion and our experience in European countries. Accurate acquisition of high-quality images is crucial for ensuring reproducibility, repeatability and reliability of the echocardiographic measurements. In addition to the commonly used workstations, an academic ECL must also possess the necessary capacities and skilled personnel to conduct sophisticated research projects. Personnel should hold advanced certification in echocardiography, indicating postgraduate training and experience beyond the basic cardiovascular ultrasound education. They should be capable of designing, performing, and interpreting complex echocardiography studies. Reproducibility of the ECL should be validated using a small, randomly selected sample, preferably in the early analytic phase. ECL readings and interpretations are superior to site-reported measurements and serve as the gold standard in observational studies and clinical trials. To ensure internal validity, an academic ECL should continuously evaluate/report reproducibility, repeatability and reliability. ECL should be formally acknowledged and accredited by an international scientific imaging society.

recs.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neonates with complex congenital heart disease are at increased risk for perioperative brain injury and seizures. Electroencephalography (EEG) detects clinical and subclinical seizures, but national utilization patterns remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Pediatric Health Information System (2016-2025) of neonates ≤28 days with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation. Mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect identified predictors of EEG utilization. RESULTS: Among 13 202 neonates, 1654 (12.5%) underwent EEG monitoring. EEG monitoring was performed in only 10.8% of neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, 16% of those with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, and 13% of those with non- hypoplastic left heart syndrome single-ventricle lesions. EEG utilization increased from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025, while seizure detection among EEG-monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26% (both P-trend<0.01). Utilization varied substantially across hospitals (0% to >40%), persisting after adjustment for surgical volume. EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection (21.8% versus 5.2%), longer length of stay (33 versus 24 days), and higher hospitalization costs ($344 719 versus $174 865; all P<0.01). In multivariable analysis, EEG utilization was independently associated with seizures (OR ~4), dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome, but not with cardiac arrest, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. CONCLUSIONS: EEG utilization in neonates with complex congenital heart disease is increasing but remains low and highly variable across US centers. The association of EEG use with higher mortality and costs may reflect confounding by indication or illness severity. Standardized protocols are needed to optimize neurologic monitoring and improve long-term outcomes.

Association of Clonal Hematopoiesis Mutations With Incident Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) has been linked to cardiovascular disease through inflammation-related pathways, but its association with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to systematically review and meta-analyze evidence on the association between CH mutations and AF, with planned analyses by hematologic cancer status, variant allele frequency (VAF), mutations, and sex. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to May 6, 2026, for studies reporting adjusted quantitative associations between CH and incident AF. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Study quality was assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies-of Exposures tool. RESULTS: Five studies comprising 7 cohorts and 299,215 participants were included. In populations without cancer, CH defined by VAF ≥2% was not significantly associated with AF (HR: 1.02; 95% CI: 0.97-1.07; I2 = 0%). Large CH clones (VAF ≥10%) were associated with a modestly higher AF risk (HR: 1.11; 95% CI: 1.01-1.22; I2 = 0%). Mutation-specific analyses did not show statistically significant associations for DNMT3A, TET2, or ASXL1 individually, and no sex-based effect modification was observed. In hematologic cancer populations, CH mutations were significantly associated with higher AF risk (HR: 3.22; 95% CI: 1.02-10.13; I2 = 0%). Sensitivity analyses and wide prediction intervals warrant cautious interpretation, particularly for the VAF ≥10% and hematologic cancer analyses. CONCLUSIONS: The association between CH and AF may vary by clonal burden and hematologic cancer status. However, evidence remains limited and observational. Larger studies with standardized CH and AF definitions are needed to clarify clinical relevance.

recs.title: Association of Site Volume and MitraClip Outcomes in Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: The COAPT PAS Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The number of sites performing transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) for secondary mitral regurgitation (SMR) has increased. Despite concerns that low-volume sites may have worse outcomes, data are limited on the association between site volume and TEER outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the association between site volume and mitral TEER outcomes in SMR. METHODS: The COAPT PAS (COAPT Post-Approval Study) included patients with SMR who underwent TEER with the MitraClip device from March 2019 to September 2020 following Food and Drug Administration approval. Sites were categorized by number of patients treated: low (≤25), medium (25-50), and high (>50). RESULTS: Of 5,000 patients, 2,632 were from low-, 1,527 from medium-, and 841 from high-volume sites. High-volume sites treated sicker patients with higher Society of Thoracic Surgeons scores and prior heart failure hospitalization rates. Procedures at low-volume sites had similar device implant rates (low: 97%, medium: 99%, high: 98%), used fewer number of clips (low: 1.4 ± 0.6, medium: 1.5 ± 0.6, high: 1.6 ± 0.7 clips, P < 0.001), and had longer device (low: 68 ± 55, medium: 56 ± 53, high: 57 ± 42 min, P < 0.001) and procedure times (low: 153 ± 67, medium: 131 ± 59, high: 128 ± 56 min, P < 0.001). Technical success was comparable (low: 93%, medium: 94%, high: 95%, P = 0.92). MR reduction to ≤2+ and ≤1+ was also similar. There was no difference in heart failure hospitalization (low: 19%, medium: 18%, high: 20%, P = 0.50) or all-cause mortality (low: 23%, medium: 21%, high: 20%, P = 0.27). CONCLUSIONS: Technical success, MR reduction, and 1-year clinical outcomes were comparable across volume strata during the early adoption phase, without significant differences between low- and high-volume centers.

Multiple Traumas Accelerate the Transition From Cardiovascular Disease to Depression: A Multistate Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Traumas are risk factors for both cardiovascular disease (CVD) and depression. However, the specific impacts of trauma on the critical transition from incident CVD to subsequent depression and mortality remain scarce. METHODS: Using data from the UK Biobank cohort (N=138 036), we constructed multistate models to investigate the associations of childhood trauma, adult trauma, and lifetime trauma with the transitions between health states. Specifically, we modeled transitions from a healthy state to incident CVD, further to subsequent depression, and ultimately to death. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 13.65 years, 14 278 participants developed incident CVD, with 679 developed subsequent depression and 4144 dying. Trauma was positively associated with the dynamic disease progression: the transition from baseline to incident CVD showed significantly elevated hazards for multiple childhood traumas (hazard ratio [HR], 1.294 [95% CI, 1.170-1.432]), adult traumas (HR, 1.145 [95% CI, 1.071-1.225]), and lifetime traumas (HR, 1.632 [95% CI, 1.528-1.742]) compared with no trauma exposure. Similarly, the transition from incident CVD to subsequent depression demonstrated increased risks for multiple childhood traumas (HR, 2.260 [95% CI, 1.661-3.075]), adult traumas (HR, 1.950 [95% CI, 1.510-2.518]), and lifetime traumas (HR, 1.608 [95% CI, 1.245-2.078]) versus no trauma exposure. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that exposure to multiple traumas significantly increases the risk of developing depression following an incident CVD diagnosis. This underscores the urgent need for clinical and public health interventions targeting multiple traumas to mitigate the risk of CVD and depression progression, thereby improving outcomes.

recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrioventricular block with normal cardiac function is common with right ventricular pacing, which raises risks of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and symptomatic heart failure in some patients with high pacing burden. Left bundle-branch area pacing demonstrates protective potential to reduce the risk of heart failure on the basis of observational studies. Evidence from a large multicenter randomized controlled trial remains limited. METHODS: The LEAP-Block (Impact of Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Atrioventricular Block) study is a prospective multicenter, investigator-initiated randomized controlled trial aiming to verify the hypothesis that left bundle-branch area pacing might have superior impact to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of cardiovascular events in patients with atrioventricular block requiring high burden of ventricular pacing and left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%. A total of 484 patients will be randomized to either left bundle-branch area pacing or right ventricular pacing (1:1). The primary end point is the composite events of all-cause death, heart failure events, and upgrade to biventricular pacing-delivered cardiac resynchronization therapy during at least 24 months of follow-up. Secondary end points include changes in echocardiographic, electrocardiographic, and pacing parameters and device-related complications. CONCLUSIONS: The LEAP-Block study aims to compare the impact of left bundle-branch area pacing versus conventional right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved cardiac function with respect to midterm clinical outcomes. This trial will provide high-quality evidence for the selection of optimal pacing strategies in clinical practice. REGISTRATION INFORMATION: clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT04730921.

Universal ECG Screening for School-Age Children: A Pediatric Cardiology and Public Health Perspective.
recs.abstract: Sudden cardiac death in the young remains an important public health concern extending beyond competitive athletes. Recent advances, including the 2025 AHA/ACC (American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology) Scientific Statement, the 2024 CSRC (Cardiac Safety Research Consortium) Think Tank Report, pediatric electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation, disease-specific risk stratification and treatment, shared decision-making, and implementation strategies, provide a timely opportunity to reconsider the potential role of universal ECG screening in school-age children. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes contemporary evidence on the epidemiology, diagnostic value, ethics, implementation, and international experience of ECG-inclusive screening. The available evidence supports a contemporary framework for evaluating its value not only in preventing sudden cardiac death but also in facilitating earlier detection and management of childhood-onset cardiovascular diseases, with possible downstream benefits in mortality, morbidity, and health care burden. Future research should determine how universal ECG screening can be effectively implemented and evaluated across diverse health care systems.

Atrial fibrillation begets atrial fibrillation revisited: Early entrenchment of AF episodes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The 7-day threshold defining persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) is clinically entrenched but biologically arbitrary. Whether episode termination follows scale-free dynamics or time-dependent entrenchment remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To quantify the probability of spontaneous termination and assess its dependence on episode duration using large-scale pacemaker monitoring. METHODS: Continuous pacemaker monitoring data from the ACaSA study were analyzed. Device-detected AF episodes were reconstructed from daily burden using predefined continuity rules. Termination was modelled as the conditional probability that an ongoing episode would terminate within the subsequent 24 hours. Duration dependence was assessed using a shared frailty Weibull survival model, and episode duration distributions were compared using the Vuong likelihood-ratio test. RESULTS: After excluding patients with single-chamber devices or 100% baseline AF burden, 251 of 281 pacemaker recipients contributed 204,775 patient-days. Device-detected AF occurred in 154 patients, who contributed 7002 reconstructed episodes. Termination probability declined from 91.1% at 1 hour to 72.1% at 12 hours, 33.3% at 24 hours, and 4.3% at 7 days. Episode durations were better described by a lognormal distribution than by a scale-free power-law model. CONCLUSION: Device-detected AF episodes show marked early entrenchment, with spontaneous termination becoming progressively less likely as episode duration increases. These findings support the concept that "AF begets AF" even at short timescales and suggest that persistence beyond 24 hours identifies a state with a substantially reduced likelihood of near-term spontaneous termination. recs.title: Therapeutically Targetable Th17-Derived miR-721 Drives Autoimmune Myocarditis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myocarditis is an inflammatory cardiac disease in which T helper 17 (Th17) cell-driven immune responses contribute to progression toward dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure. Current therapies mainly rely on corticosteroids but lack specificity, while the role of miR-721, synthesized by Th17 cells, remains largely unexplored in disease pathogenesis. METHODS: We characterized the presence of mmu-miR-721 and its human homolog hsa-RNA-Chr8:96 in extracellular vesicles secreted by Th17 cells from IL-17 (interleukin-17) eGFP mice with experimental autoimmune myocarditis and from patients with myocarditis. MxCre±Ppargfl/fl mice and luciferase reporter assays were used to validate the target genes of miR-721 and hsa-RNA-Chr8:96, respectively. The functional role of miR-721 in experimental autoimmune myocarditis was investigated using lentiviral vectors overexpression and miRNA sponge molecules for inhibition. Th17 responses and heart inflammation were assessed, and echocardiography was performed after in vivo blockade of mmu-miR-721 in experimental autoimmune myocarditis mice. RESULTS: Both mmu-miR-721 and hsa-RNA-Chr8:96 were encapsulated in extracellular vesicles and secreted by Th17 cells of mice and patients with myocarditis. Overexpression of mmu-miR-721 in draining lymph node cells from experimental autoimmune myocarditis mice promoted Th17 differentiation via Pparg inhibition and increased RORγt and IL-17 expression. In contrast, no differences in RORγt expression were observed in the absence of Pparg, a target of miR-721, indicating that miR-721 promotes Th17 responses through Pparg repression. In addition, human PPARG was validated as a target gene of hsa-RNA-Chr8:96, as its overexpression in peripheral blood leukocytes downregulated PPARG mRNA levels, suggesting that similar pathways are involved in human pathology. Finally, in vivo blockade of mmu-miR-721 increased Pparg expression, reducing RORγt and IL-17 activation in T cells, leading to decreased leukocyte infiltration in the heart and improved cardiac function thereby ameliorating disease progression. CONCLUSIONS: miR-721 is released by Th17 cells in extracellular vesicles and promotes Th17 responses during myocarditis through repression of PPARγ, identifying this miRNA as both a mechanistic driver of disease and a potential therapeutic target.

recs.title: Acute right ventricular response to transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Changes in right ventricular (RV) function are frequent after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR), yet their mechanisms and prognostic implications remain incompletely defined. AIMS: We sought to characterise acute RV functional changes following TTVR and evaluate their prognostic impact. METHODS: This multicentre study included consecutive patients treated with TTVR between 2019 and 2025 with complete imaging data. RV function was assessed by echocardiography at baseline, intraprocedurally, and before discharge. RV end-systolic elastance (Ees), effective arterial elastance (Ea), and RV-pulmonary artery coupling (Ees/Ea) were derived from non-invasive single-beat pressure-volume loop analysis. Changes over time were assessed using paired tests, and associations with mortality were investigated using Cox regression analysis with Firth's penalised likelihood. RESULTS: Sixty-seven patients (median age 78 years; 72% female; EVOQUE n=49; LuX-Valve Plus n=18) were included. At discharge, both cohorts showed declines in absolute RV free-wall longitudinal strain (aRV-FWLS; -10.4%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -10.4%; p=0.001 for LuX-Valve Plus) and fractional area change (FAC; -18.0%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -13.5%; p=0.005 for LuX-Valve Plus). Overall, 58% of patients met the criteria for severe RV dysfunction after TTVR. Over a median follow-up of 19 months, 15 patients died. Device type, acute RV functional changes, Ees, and Ees/Ea were not associated with mortality (allp>0.05). In contrast, computed tomography-derived RV coupling (hazard ratio [HR] 0.02, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.01-0.89) and the coexistence of baseline longitudinal (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion <17 mm and/or aRV-FWLS <23%) and circumferential (RV-FAC ≤35%) RV dysfunction (HR 3.93, 95% CI: 1.10-14.47) were associated with mortality. CONCLUSIONS: TTVR is associated with an acute decline in RV systolic function. Although common, early postprocedural RV dysfunction was not associated with midterm mortality.

recs.title: Preferential Conduction Along the Epicardial Ventricular Septum During Idiopathic Ventricular Arrhythmias Originating From the Basal LV Summit: A Pitfall for Anatomical Ablation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: An anatomical ablation of idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) originating from the left ventricular summit (LVS) is delivered from endocardial sites across the myocardium adjacent to the site of the VA origin with the guidance of transvenous epicardial mapping. Therefore, electrophysiological information obtained by transvenous epicardial mapping should be carefully interpreted. OBJECTIVES: This study investigated ventricular activation patterns within the great cardiac vein (GCV) during idiopathic LVS VAs. METHODS: We studied 38 consecutive patients who underwent a successful endocardial ablation of idiopathic LVS VAs at the left ostial process, left coronary sinus, and commissure between the left and right coronary cusps. RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients exhibited a radial activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded around the junction between the GCV and anterior interventricular vein (AIVV). The remaining 9 patients exhibited a septal activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded within the AIVV, with the activation sequence being from the AIVV to GCV. The septal group mainly exhibited left bundle branch block pattern, whereas the radial group exhibited right bundle branch block pattern (P < 0.0001). The distance between the earliest ventricular activation site within the GCV or AIVV and the successful ablation site was significantly larger for LVS VAs with a septal activation pattern than those with a radial activation pattern. CONCLUSIONS: During idiopathic basal LVS VAs, activation from those VA origins often preferentially conducted along the ventricular septum. It should be kept in mind that this unusual activation pattern may mislead the mapping and catheter ablation of LVS VAs.

recs.title: 2025 Harriet Dustan Lecture: Sex Differences in Immune-Mediated Hypertension: Why Menopause Matters.
recs.abstract: Hypertension is an inflammatory disease with the immune system playing a key role in mediating hypertensive outcomes and end-organ damage. The risk of hypertension is greater in men than in women before women enter menopause. After menopause, a woman's risk for developing hypertension increases and accelerates beyond that of age-matched men. Moreover, after menopause, the rate of hypertension control in women is lower than in men. Indeed, cardiovascular drug efficacy in women is different from that in men, with recent studies highlighting serious side effects of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and β-blockers in postmenopausal women. Despite these sex differences, sex-specific clinical practice guidelines are still sparse, as is the consideration of a woman's hormonal status. In addition, preclinical models of immune-mediated hypertension are still mainly performed in male animals. The goal of this review is to highlight recent advancements in the field of sex differences in immune-mediated hypertension and to identify the major gaps in understanding immune mechanisms that lead to hypertension development in males and females, and as menopause progresses.

Angiography-Derived vs Wire-Based Fractional Flow Reserve to Guide Revascularization: The Randomized LIPSIA-STRATEGY Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Wire-based physiological assessment is recommended to guide coronary revascularization but remains underused. Angiography-derived physiology offers a wire-free alternative; however, randomized comparisons with pressure wire fractional flow reserve (FFR) have yielded inconsistent findings. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to determine whether angiography-derived vessel fractional flow reserve (vFFR)-guided revascularization is noninferior to pressure wire FFR guidance for intermediate coronary stenoses. METHODS: The multicenter, investigator-initiated, randomized LIPSIA-STRATEGY trial included patients with acute or chronic coronary syndromes and at least 1 intermediate coronary stenosis at 8 German centers. Patients were randomized 1:1 to undergo revascularization based on vFFR or FFR. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiac events, defined as a composite of cardiac death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or unplanned clinically driven revascularization within 1 year, analyzed by modified intention to treat against a noninferiority margin of 3.5 percentage points. RESULTS: Between June 2020 and February 2025, 1,053 patients (median age: 69 years) underwent randomization (vFFR, n = 528; FFR, n = 525). At 1 year, major adverse cardiac events occurred in 15 of 493 patients (3.0%) in the vFFR group and in 20 of 493 (4.1%) in the FFR group (risk difference: -1.01 percentage points; P for noninferiority <0.001); the primary outcome was ascertainable in 986 of the 1,053 randomized patients. The upper boundary of the 1-sided 97.5% CI for the risk difference was 1.29 percentage points, below the prespecified margin (relative risk: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.39-1.45). Physiological values of 0.80 or less occurred in 43.1% vs 35.9% of patients, and the study lesion was revascularized in 41.2% vs 35.5%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with intermediate coronary stenoses requiring physiological assessment, a vFFR-guided revascularization strategy met the prespecified absolute criterion for noninferiority to wire-based FFR at 1 year. Because the observed event rate was lower than anticipated, the margin was less conservative on a relative scale than intended. In a post hoc sensitivity analysis using the relative margin of 1.44 implied by the original assumptions, noninferiority was not met in the primary modified intention-to-treat population. In the corresponding post hoc per-protocol sensitivity analysis, noninferiority was met using this relative margin. Whether that additional revascularization is beneficial is not answered by similar 1-year event rates. (Comparison of Vessel-FFR Versus FFR in Intermediate Coronary Stenoses; NCT03497637; Protocol ID HRC045277.).

Association Between Peripheral and Coronary Subclinical Atherosclerosis Burden in Midlife.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atherosclerosis, silent in its early stages, underlies most cardiovascular manifestations. The inter-relation between silent atherosclerosis across vascular territories remains insufficiently characterized. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the association between peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis in asymptomatic individuals. METHODS: A subgroup of individuals of the PESA (Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis) cohort underwent contrast-enhanced coronary computed tomography angiography in addition to peripheral (carotid and femoral) atherosclerosis assessment using 3-dimensional vascular ultrasound. Peripheral global plaque volume was calculated as the sum of bilateral carotid and femoral plaque burden using an artificial intelligence-based automated approach. Coronary computed tomographic angiographic images were qualitatively evaluated for the presence and severity of coronary atherosclerosis (percentage stenosis) and quantitatively for coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and global coronary plaque volume measurement. RESULTS: A total of 374 participants (mean age: 55 years, 34% women, 63% with CACS = 0) were included. Peripheral atherosclerosis was present in 75%. Peripheral global plaque volume was significantly associated with the presence, severity, and burden of coronary atherosclerosis (coronary plaque volume) (r = 0.69; P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, and conventional risk factor profile, individuals with peripheral atherosclerosis had nearly 3 times greater odds of having coronary atherosclerosis than those without (OR: 2.66; 95% CI: 1.50-4.72; P = 0.001). Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis remained significantly and independently associated with coronary plaque. Among participants with CACS = 0, noncalcified coronary plaque was detected in 12.0%, nearly all of whom (93%) had concomitant peripheral atherosclerosis. CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis were strongly correlated in asymptomatic persons. Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis were associated with coronary artery disease independently of each other.

recs.title: High on the Heart? Cannabis Use and Cardiovascular Disease: A Systematic Review.
recs.abstract: Cannabis use has increased substantially over the past 2 decades following shifts in public perception, legalization, and medical usage. Although neurological and psychiatric effects are well known, the cardiovascular effects of cannabis exposure are largely understudied. This review evaluates the cardiovascular effects of cannabis use by examining clinical evidence, epidemiological data, and underlying biochemical mechanisms. This review examines cannabis-related cardiovascular conditions, including atherosclerosis, arrhythmias, heart failure, and stroke. The analysis focused on cannabinoid composition, route of administration, frequency of use, and cardiovascular outcomes. Evidence indicates that acute and high Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol/cannabidiol ratio cannabis use is associated with increased risks of various cardiovascular outcomes, especially among younger individuals without cardiovascular risk factors. Given rising use and increasing Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol potency, clinicians must routinely assess cannabis exposure when evaluating cardiovascular disease, especially in younger patients. Future research must prioritize the development of standardized exposure metrics in cannabis-related cardiovascular disease research, thus allowing clinicians and patients to better understand the cardiovascular risks of cannabis use and initiate effective cessation strategies.

recs.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Patients Considered Unsuitable for Oral Anticoagulation: Randomized Outcomes Through 5 Years in ASAP-TOO.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) use in atrial fibrillation is suboptimal due to real or perceived bleeding risks. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an alternative to OAC, but pivotal trials used OAC comparators. OBJECTIVES: The study sought to assess the long-term safety and effectiveness of LAAC in patients deemed unsuitable for OAC. METHODS: The ASAP-TOO trial was a multinational randomized trial of patients with atrial fibrillation, CHA2DS2-VASc (congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 years, diabetes mellitus, prior stroke or transient ischemic attack or thromboembolism, vascular disease, age 65-74 years, sex category) score ≥2, and OAC unsuitability; target enrollment was 888 patients. Patients were assigned 2:1 to LAAC with a Watchman device or control treatment-single antiplatelet therapy or no therapy. Device patients received dual antiplatelet therapy for 3 months and aspirin through 12 months. The primary effectiveness endpoint was ischemic stroke or systemic embolism; the primary safety endpoint was death, ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, or 7-day device/procedure-related events requiring major intervention. RESULTS: Enrollment stopped early because of slow accrual, accentuated by the COVID-19 pandemic: only 481 patients were randomized (320 LAAC, 161 control treatment) and withdrawal was significant (7.8% LAAC, 24.2% control treatment), with disparate follow-up durations (median 876 days and 440.1 total patient-years of follow-up for control patients; median 1,768 days and 1,154.6 total patient-years of follow-up for LAAC patients), reducing statistical power. Patients were 75 ± 8 years of age, the CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.6 ± 1.7, and 34% had prior intracranial/subdural hemorrhage. Implantation success was 97.8%. Only 31 of the 101 planned primary effectiveness events occurred, fewer than the 34 events required to trigger the first planned interim analysis. The primary safety endpoint occurred in 1.0% of implant-attempted patients, meeting the prespecified performance goal (P < 0.0001); there were 3 pericardial effusions requiring intervention. At up to 5 years, ischemic stroke or systemic embolism occurred in 7.8% with LAAC and 11.4% with control treatment (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.35-1.52; P = 0.39). Major bleeding was 22.1% with LAAC and 15.7% with control treatment (HR: 1.64; 95% CI: 0.96-2.81; P = 0.067), concentrated during the first 3 months. In an exploratory analysis, disabling/fatal stroke was nominally less frequent with LAAC (2.2% vs 5.7%; HR: 0.32; 95% CI: 0.10-1.05). CONCLUSIONS: In this prematurely terminated and underpowered trial, LAAC implantation was successful, with acceptable safety. Long-term estimates with LAAC were numerically favorable for thromboembolism but imprecise, while early bleeding was increased with the mandated antiplatelet regimen. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory and integrated with contemporary evidence and shared decision making. (Assessment of the WATCHMAN Device in Patients Unsuitable for Oral Anticoagulation [ASAP-TOO]; NCT02928497).

Systematic Transesophageal Echocardiographic Identification of Tricuspid Valve Commissures and Subvalvular Apparatus.
recs.abstract: Transcatheter tricuspid valve (TV) intervention is rapidly evolving and several classes of therapeutic devices are currently in development. The anatomic knowledge of the TV is the cornerstone for transcatheter patient selection, and the successful implantation of the devices depends on imaging guidance. Anatomically, leaflets are separated by the commissures, which have peculiar findings: they are supported by fan-shaped chords and do not open directly into the annulus, but a few millimeters of the leaflet tissue remain, similar to small scallops. While a comprehensive echocardiographic assessment of TV has been extensively reported, few papers have focused on analyzing commissures and their impact on interventions. This paper aims to introduce a novel echocardiographic approach focusing on TV commissures, and provide a dedicated transesophageal imaging protocol and methodology for recognizing their anatomic landmarks. Multiple dedicated transesophageal views are comprehensively reported for each commissure, in order to ensure a guide for emerging transcatheter procedures.

recs.title: Defining silent plaque rupture healing in vivo: a structural approach by OCT.
AI-Enabled Echocardiography Identifies Prominent Epicardial Adipose Tissue Associated With an Adverse Cardiometabolic Profile.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Excess epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is associated with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic dysfunction, but its assessment has traditionally required advanced imaging. OBJECTIVES: We investigated whether artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled echocardiography could characterize epicardial adiposity and identify residual cardiometabolic risk. METHODS: We developed PanAdipo, a video-based deep learning model in 1,114,441 videos from 28,797 studies across the Yale-New Haven Health System (YNHHS) (2016-2022), using report-derived expert reader labels of prominent EAT (2.3% of studies). PanAdipo was evaluated in 5 testing cohorts: a temporally distinct YNHHS transthoracic echocardiography set (n = 4,588 patients contributing 5,130 studies), an emergency department point-of-care ultrasound cohort (n = 10,957), the geographically distinct MIMIC-IV (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care, version IV) data set (n = 4,549), the community-based MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) Exam 6 (n = 2,740), as well as in held-out YNHHS patients with paired coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography within 12 months (n = 5,167). Analyses examined discrimination of the report label and of CT-defined high indexed EAT volume, correlation with paired cardiac CT phenotypes, and body mass index (BMI)-adjusted associations with cardiometabolic biomarkers and newly documented metabolic disease. RESULTS: In the held-out health system test set, PanAdipo identified prominent EAT documented in clinical reports with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82-0.91) across views. Against paired CT-derived measurements, PanAdipo discriminated age- and sex-specific high EAT (EAT / heart volume ≥95th percentile) with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.90 (95% CI: 0.89-0.92) overall and of 0.91-0.95 within age-sex groups, and correlated more strongly with indexed EAT volume (Spearman ρ = 0.76) than with BMI (Spearman ρ = 0.41; all P < 0.001); PanAdipo alone explained 53% of indexed EAT volume variance vs 23% for age, sex, and BMI combined. In MESA, higher scores were associated with an adverse metabolic profile (higher homeostatic model assessment for insulin resistance [β = 0.17 per SD; 95% CI: 0.11-0.22; n = 950]) after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. In exploratory health system cohort analyses, higher scores were associated with newly documented steatotic liver disease (pooled BMI-adjusted HR: 1.33 [95% CI: 1.11-1.59] per SD of log[PanAdipo]) and hyperlipidemia (HR: 1.11; 95% CI: 1.04-1.18), with modest precision (Hartung-Knapp intervals crossed 1). CONCLUSIONS: AI-enabled echocardiography provides a scalable digital biomarker that characterizes prominent epicardial adiposity and is associated with an adverse cardiometabolic profile, highlighting a role for echocardiography in metabolic risk stratification.

Pulmonary hypertension: a rapidly developing field.
Current Patterns and Best Practices for Prescribing Novel Heart Failure Medications in Children: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association.
recs.abstract: Robust evidence from randomized controlled trials of novel heart failure medications in adults has demonstrated improved quality of life, reduced hospitalizations, and decreased mortality, informing current treatment guidelines. In contrast, data supporting the clinical benefits of newer heart failure therapies in children remain limited. To assess contemporary prescribing practices and clinician perspectives, we surveyed pediatric heart failure physicians across the United States and Canada regarding the use of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, and iron replacement therapy in children. We also reviewed the existing pediatric literature and summarized reported side effects, dosing experience, and practical guidance for the use of these therapies in the absence of rigorous evidence.

recs.title: Initial Experience with Bachmann Bundle Pacing Lead Implantation as a Rhythm Control Strategy in Atrial Fibrillation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Bachmann bundle pacing (BBP) is challenging during atrial fibrillation (AF) because ECG based endpoints cannot confirm lead positioning. We aimed to demonstrate the feasibility of a practical approach to BBP implantation during AF and propose a framework for comprehensive conduction system pacing with BBP and left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) for rhythm control in patients referred for pace-and-ablate therapy. METHODS AND RESULTS: Twenty-four consecutive patients with persistent or longstanding persistent AF and preserved ejection fraction underwent dual-chamber BBP and LBBP implantation with individually optimized pacing rate and AV interval. Twelve underwent BBP during AF (Group 1) and 12 during sinus (Group 2), including six cardioverted intraprocedurally. During AF, lead positioning was guided by anatomical landmarks, local electrograms, current of injury, and impedance changes. After sinus rhythm restoration, BBP was confirmed in 11/12 Group 1 patients. Reductions in P-wave duration and interatrial block were observed in both groups. Seventeen had been referred for pace-and-ablate therapy; three in Group 1 reverted spontaneously to sinus rhythm before cardioversion. Over a median 192 [139-212] days after sinus restoration, 12/17 maintained sinus rhythm; 2 underwent AV node ablation, 1 AF ablation, 1 repeat cardioversion, and 1 required rate-control medication for paroxysmal AF. No complications occurred. CONCLUSION: BBP implantation during AF is feasible using anatomical and electrophysiological markers, with Bachmann bundle capture confirmed after sinus rhythm restoration. Exploratory findings suggest that comprehensive conduction system pacing with BBP and LBBP may support a rhythm-control (pace-and-wait) strategy in persistent AF patients referred for pace-and-ablate therapy.

recs.title: Safer Stroke Prevention in Atrial Fibrillation: Factor XI/XIa Inhibitors, Left Atrial Appendage Closure, or Both?
Heart Failure Phenotyping and Prognosis by CMR-Derived Oxygen Delivery and Extraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure reflects impaired matching of systemic oxygen delivery to metabolic demand, yet resting oxygen transport is seldom measured. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to noninvasively derive resting oxygen delivery and extraction using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and relate these to clinical characteristics and outcomes. METHODS: In this retrospective study, in patients with heart failure referred for clinical CMR, cardiac output was assessed by cine imaging; basal blood-pool T2 mapping provided imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation; and measured hemoglobin enabled calculation of arterial oxygen content. Arterial oxygen saturation was fixed at 96%. We derived indexed systemic oxygen delivery (DO2i), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), and indexed systemic oxygen consumption (VO2i). The endpoint was all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization. RESULTS: A total of 429 patients were included (62 events). VO2i varied widely (tertile means 138.8, 207.9, and 293.8 mL/min/m2), while left ventricular ejection fraction did not differ (38.8%, 40.6%, and 40.3%; P = 0.42). Imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation decreased across increasing VO2i tertiles (61.5%, 54.3%, and 50.7%; P < 0.0001). In Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, ejection fraction, and late gadolinium enhancement, VO2i was associated with the endpoint (HR: 1.15 per 50 mL/min/m2, 95% CI: 1.00-1.32; P = 0.046), but discrimination of VO2i alone was poor (Harrell's C = 0.53). Delivery-extraction phenotypes differed in event risk (log-rank P = 0.026): event proportions were 8.6% (high DO2i/low OEF), 14.0% (low DO2i/low OEF), 16.8% (high DO2i/high OEF), and 18.3% (low DO2i/high OEF). The delivery-extraction phenotype remained associated with outcome after adjustment for age, sex, left ventricular ejection fraction, and CMR-derived filling pressure. CONCLUSIONS: In this hypothesis-generating study, CMR-based oxygen supply-demand assessment delineates resting delivery-extraction phenotypes associated with heart failure outcomes.

recs.title: Sex-Related Differences in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Primary Mitral Regurgitation: PRIME-MR Registry Insights.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sex-related differences have been previously explored in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR) undergoing surgery as well as those with secondary MR treated with transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate sex-related differences in baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TEER for primary MR. METHODS: Outcomes of Patients Treated with M-TEER for Primary MR (NCT05332782) is an international, retrospective registry including patients undergoing TEER for primary MR in 27 centers. The primary outcome was a composite of 2-year all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. RESULTS: A total of 2,078 patients, including 961 (46.3%) females, were analyzed. Females were older and had fewer comorbidities but presented with a different anatomy and more advanced symptoms. Compared with males, females were more frequently excluded from surgery because of advanced age and frailty. Optimal procedural results were lower in females, with a higher incidence of residual MR ≥2+ (38.5% vs 32.1%; P = 0.0037), and a significantly higher mean transmitral gradient (4.0 vs 3.6 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier curves showed significantly lower rates of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality in female patients. In contrast, the incidence of the primary composite endpoint, as well as heart failure hospitalization alone, did not differ significantly. After adjusting for comorbidities, females demonstrated lower primary composite endpoint (HR: 0.77; P = 0.009), lower all-cause mortality (HR: 0.62; P < 0.001), and lower cardiovascular mortality (subdistribution HR: 0.53; P = 0.011). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with primary MR, females were older and presented with a different clinical and anatomical profile compared with males. Although optimal procedural results were lower in females, higher survival rates in females vs males suggest that mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be a good option regardless of sex.

recs.title: Fluoroscopy-Only Versus TEE-Guided Left Atrial Appendage Closure: A Comparison of Disk-Type and Plug-Type Devices.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopy alone is emerging as a guidance modality for left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO). OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of fluoroscopy-only vs transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)-guided LAAO and compared the fluoroscopic views required for plug-type and disk-type devices. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, patients undergoing LAAO guided by fluoroscopy only or by TEE with fluoroscopy were divided into a fluoroscopy-only group (n = 603) and a TEE group (n = 156) and further into a fluoroscopy-only disk-type (FODT) (n = 382), fluoroscopy-only plug-type (n = 221), TEE disk-type (n = 76), and TEE plug-type (n = 80) subgroups. Follow-up included TEE at 3 to 6 months and clinical event monitoring. RESULTS: The fluoroscopy-only group exhibited comparable implantation success (99.8% vs 100%; P = 1.000), peridevice leak rates (≥3 mm: 1.0% vs 1.3%; P = 0.671) and clinical outcomes during follow-up to the TEE group, with significantly shorter LAAO procedure times (40.9 ± 21.7 vs 78.9 ± 35.0 min; P < 0.001). The FODT subgroup required more views under fluoroscopy (3 [3, 3] vs 2 [2, 3]; P < 0.001) despite comparable peridevice leak rates. The clinical outcomes were similar between the TEE and fluoroscopy-only groups and between the FODT and fluoroscopy-only plug-type subgroups. CONCLUSIONS: Whether a disk-type or plug-type device is employed, LAAO guided by fluoroscopy only appears to be as feasible and safe as guidance by TEE. However, disk-type device needed more fluoroscopy views for accurate implantation than plug-type device. In the absence of randomized data, these hypothesis-generating findings should not be extrapolated to less experienced operators or centers.

recs.title: Concerns about use of placebo control in clinical trials of Obinutuzumab β for aquaporin-4 antibody positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
Predictors and Long-term Prognosis of Silent Cerebral Embolism After Catheter Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation.
Identifying Plasma Proteins for Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Penetrance and Severity in Pathogenic Variant Carriers and Noncarriers.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a clinically variable disease in onset and progression. Pathogenic MYBPC3 variants account for a substantial proportion of HCM diagnoses. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to identify protein biomarkers associated with HCM penetrance and severity. METHODS: Olink-assayed plasma proteins of 144 pathogenic MYBPC3 variant carriers were evaluated for associations with HCM severity based on diagnostic criteria (unaffected, mildly, or severely affected). Identified proteins were replicated in the UK Biobank considering time to onset of HCM (67 cases), cardiomyopathy (156 cases), and associations with left ventricular maximum wall thickness (6,492 participants). After prioritizing proteins on cardiac tissue expression and druggability, we examined disease penetrance through associations with heart failure (HF) and arrhythmic outcomes in 272 UK Biobank participants with known pathogenic HCM variants free of cardiomyopathy at proteomics assessment. RESULTS: Among pathogenic MYBPC3 variant carriers, we identified 27 proteins associated with HCM severity, of which 22 replicated in the UK Biobank. Six proteins were prioritized (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP], growth/differentiation factor [GDF]-15, fibroblast growth factor [FGF]-23, adrenomedullin [ADM], renin [REN], and neural cell adhesion molecule 1 [NCAM1]), of which 5 associated with disease penetrance in pathogenic variant carriers: NT-proBNP and REN associated with increased HF and arrhythmic risk, GDF-15 and FGF-23 with HF risk, and NCAM1 with arrhythmic risk. CONCLUSIONS: Through the integration of proteomic analyses in both clinical and general population cohorts, we replicated and prioritized 6 proteins associated with HCM penetrance and severity. These findings highlight potential plasma-based markers for diagnosis and disease monitoring, as well as promising targets for future therapeutic development.

recs.title: PREVENT Risk Stratification for Intensive Blood Pressure Intervention and Life Expectancy in Rural China: A Post Hoc Analysis of the China Rural Hypertension Control Project.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology guideline adopted the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) equations to guide antihypertensive treatment, but whether PREVENT risk groups identify patients who benefit more from intensive blood pressure (BP) control is uncertain. We evaluated intensive BP control across PREVENT risk groups in the China Rural Hypertension Control Project. METHODS: We analyzed 21 872 hypertensive adults from 326 Chinese villages. Participants received intensive BP control (target <130/80 mm Hg) or usual care and were classified as low risk (<5%), borderline risk (5.0%-7.4%), intermediate risk (7.5%-19.9%), or high risk (≥20%). The primary outcome was a composite of major cardiovascular events (myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death). Safety, net benefit, and life expectancy were assessed. RESULTS: Over a median of 3.02 years, intensive BP control was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in the low-risk (hazard ratio, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.29-0.97]), intermediate-risk (hazard ratio, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.49-0.69]), and high-risk groups (hazard ratio, 0.60 [95% CI, 0.47-0.77]), but not the borderline-risk group (hazard ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.51-1.26]). No significant treatment-by-risk interaction was observed. Adverse events increased mainly in intermediate- and high-risk groups. Net benefit was favorable across all groups and greatest in the high-risk group. At 45 years of age, estimated life expectancy gains were 0.94 years overall, 0.71 years in the intermediate-risk group, and 1.26 years in the high-risk group. CONCLUSIONS: Intensive BP control was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in 3 PREVENT risk groups, with favorable net benefit across all groups. Absolute benefit and estimated life expectancy gains were greatest among high-risk participants. PREVENT risk stratification may inform intensive BP control in community-based hypertensive populations.
