When Risk Becomes a Diagnosis: Biomarker-Driven CKM Stage Migration in Chronic Kidney Disease.
Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Anticoagulation for Atrial Fibrillation: Navigating Heterogeneity in Clinical Evidence: JACC Evidence Review.
recs.abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative to long-term anticoagulation for preventing stroke or systemic embolism in selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) based on several randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that collectively enrolled >7,000 participants. In this JACC Evidence Review, we interpret the major RCTs as distinct experiments, clarify what each can and cannot establish, and offer a phenotype-based framework for interpreting the evidence. The most recent RCTs, OPTION, CLOSURE-AF, and CHAMPION-AF, have prompted efforts to pool the evidence into a single summary estimate. However, these trials are not one coherent evidence base; they are distinct clinical experiments that asked different questions. They differ in patient phenotype, comparator, device generation, postprocedure antithrombotic regimen, endpoint construction, and follow-up duration. Study-level meta-analysis of published reports remains methodologically valid for estimating the broad direction of effect of a device class, but when the component trials differ materially in patient phenotype, comparator, and outcome construction, the pooled estimate does not map to a common patient group or treatment decision. Patient eligibility as well as thromboembolic and bleeding risk varied markedly across trials. In addition, device technology has progressed, and comparators have evolved from warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. Heterogeneity and insufficient details also exist about the antithrombotic therapy regimen in LAAC arms and adjunct antiplatelet therapy in control arms. Methodological issues further complicate interpretation, including the use of bleeding events (ie, the putative ancillary benefit of LAAC compared with anticoagulation) within composite endpoints tested for noninferiority, varying noninferiority margins, analytical approaches that may undermine the interpretation of noninferiority, and exclusion of periprocedural bleeding from primary safety endpoints in some trials. Finally, the standard of care for anticoagulation in AF has evolved, obviating concomitant aspirin use in stable individuals on therapeutic anticoagulation, thereby reducing bleeding risk compared with that of the control arm of LAAC RCTs. For most anticoagulation-eligible patients, anticoagulation remains the preferred first-line strategy. LAAC is a reasonable option when long-term anticoagulation is unsafe or unsustainable provided that procedural risk, adjunct antithrombotic feasibility, surveillance needs, and competing mortality are carefully considered. RCT evidence in this latter population is limited, and RCTs in other populations have features that limit their support for LAAC as an alternative to anticoagulation. Because LAAC and anticoagulation offer different types of risk, aligning the most applicable evidence with patient values through shared decision-making is central to care.

recs.title: Feasibility and safety of leadless pacemaker implantation via the right internal jugular vein: primary results of the VAMPIRE multicenter prospective study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Leadless pacemakers (LPs) are usually implanted through the femoral vein. The right internal jugular vein (RIJV) approach has emerged as an alternative, but evidence remains limited to retrospective single-centre series. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, procedural success, and 30-day safety of a first-line RIJV approach for LP implantation. METHODS: The VAMPIRE study (NCT06455566) is a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter registry enrolling consecutive patients with a guideline-directed LP indication across 15 tertiary centres in France (May 2024-May 2026). The primary endpoint was major procedure- or system-related complications within 30 days. RESULTS: Of 294 screened patients, 272 (92.5%) underwent a first-line RIJV approach. The cohort was elderly (median age 79 [73-85] years), predominantly male (63.6%), with high comorbidity burden including atrial fibrillation in 51.5%, chronic kidney disease in 34.9%, and cancer in 22.4%. High-degree atrioventricular block was the primary indication in 84.9%; 65.8% of procedures were performed urgently. Successful LP implantation was achieved in 266 of 272 patients (97.8%; 95% CI 95.3-99.2%), with septal deployment in 94.3%. Median procedure time was 30 [25-40] minutes and median fluoroscopy time 2.5 [1.1-7.0] minutes. Major complications occurred in 6 of 272 patients (2.2%; 95% CI 0.8-4.7%; p<0.001). CONCLUSION: In this prospective multicenter registry of a first-line RIJV approach for LP implantation, feasibility and procedural success were high, and 30-day major complications rate low. These results support the RIJV route as a safe and broadly applicable access strategy for LP implantation. However, dedicated studies are needed to compare safety versus the femoral approach.

recs.title: Impact of age on implementation and tolerability of guideline-directed medical therapy in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Elderly patients constitute a growing proportion of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet remain underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. We evaluated the impact of age on the implementation of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in HFrEF. METHODS: TITRATE-HF is a prospective, multicentre registry (enrolment June 2022-February 2024) including patients with de novo, chronic, and worsening heart failure (HF). For the current analysis, HFrEF patients were categorized by age (<65, 65-74, and ≥75 years). We assessed GDMT implementation, tolerability, and clinical outcomes (composite endpoint: first HF hospitalization or all-cause death). RESULTS: The cohort included 980 patients aged <65 years (29%), 1120 patients aged 65-74 years (33%), and 1267 patients aged ≥75 years (38%). At 12-month follow-up, younger patients more frequently received GDMT, with quadruple therapy prescribed in 68% of those aged <65 years, 61% aged 65-74 years, and 51% aged ≥75 years (P < .001). In de novo HFrEF, age-related differences were observed within weeks after diagnosis, with faster and more extensive GDMT intensification in younger patients. Still, rates of treatment downgrades and the distribution of side effects were largely similar across age groups. Significant left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement was observed in all age groups (all P < .001). The use of quadruple therapy at 6 months was associated with a lower risk of the composite endpoint between 6 and 12 months (adjusted hazard ratio 0.65, 95% confidence interval 0.50-0.86, P = .002), with consistent associations across age groups (P for interaction = .46). CONCLUSIONS: Elderly patients with HFrEF received less intensive GDMT. Age-related differences emerged early after diagnosis, with fewer treatment intensifications in elderly patients but largely similar downgrade rates across age groups. These findings highlight the need for improved implementation strategies to optimize guideline-directed therapy and dosing levels in the ageing HFrEF population.

recs.title: Assessment of the optimal echocardiographic profile on left ventricular assist device support: an outcome-driven definition.
Comparison of Prosthetic Valve Deformation and Hemodynamic Performance Between Bicuspid and Tricuspid Aortic Valve Anatomy After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study compared prosthetic valve deformation and postprocedural hemodynamic performance between bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valve anatomy after transcatheter aortic valve replacement with the Venus-A prosthesis. METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement between 2012 and 2022 and underwent postoperative computed tomography within 1 year. Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak. Computed tomography measurements included expansion ratio, ellipticity, implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening. The leaflet inflow and valve waist were collectively defined as the functional valve portion. RESULTS: Among 212 patients (106 bicuspid and 106 tricuspid), the mean age was 74.2±7.6 years, and 43.9% were women. Patients with bicuspid anatomy had a significantly lower oversizing ratio and underwent balloon predilation and postdilation more frequently than those with tricuspid anatomy. Residual transvalvular gradients were higher with bicuspid than tricuspid anatomy (12.0 [interquartile range, 8.2-17.0] versus 10.0 [7.2-14.0] mm Hg; P=0.014), whereas moderate to severe paravalvular leak did not differ significantly. Prosthetic ellipticity was greater in bicuspid anatomy, but expansion ratios, including those within the functional valve portion, did not differ significantly. Implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening incidence also did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: Following Venus-A implantation, bicuspid anatomy was associated with greater prosthetic ellipticity and higher residual gradients, despite no significant difference in prosthetic expansion.

recs.title: Effect of Acoramidis on Heart Failure-Related Health Status-Reply.
Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair: Preference Versus Evidence: A Less Invasive Surgical Approach for Mitral Valve Disease.
Precise anatomical landmark annotation of the cardiac conduction system on cardiac computed tomography angiography.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: CTA-based estimation of the conduction system from anatomical landmarks underpins a visualization platform (CARA) used in structural heart interventions and conduction system pacing. OBJECTIVE: To quantify the precision and reliability of the annotation method and the bias of trained readers relative to an expert reference standard. METHODS: The expert who defined the method and 6 trained readers each annotated 8 landmarks representing the sinus and atrioventricular nodes, His bundle course (Point B), left bundle branch origin (Point C), and course of Bachmann's bundle (B2-B5), in addition to the three aortic leaflet nadirs on 50 CTA studies in 3 sessions. Repeatability and reproducibility were assessed, referenced to clinically accepted error margins (2-5 mm). Intraclass correlations (ICC) were computed on heights above the aortic annular plane. 3D bias relative to the expert was tested for equivalence within half the margin. RESULTS: Repeatability SD was 1.67-3.98 mm and reproducibility SD 2.03-5.60 mm; all mean deviations were within margin, with 88.6-97.4% of repeat reads and 71.4-94.9% of reader means within margin. Inter-observer ICC on annular heights was 0.76-0.82 for the atrioventricular and 0.79-0.98 for the atrial points. Shared bias relative to the expert was 0.14-3.24 mm, within margin for all landmarks and equivalent within half the margin for sinus node, Point B, B2 and B3; at B3 and B2, 95% and 83% of the apparent separation was repeatability noise. CONCLUSION: The method meets its clinically accepted margins with millimeter precision and good-to-excellent reliability, and transfers from expert to trained readers with bias within margin.

recs.title: Macrophage Gα Chaperone Protein Ric-8B Exacerbates Atherosclerosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Macrophage stimulatory G-protein (Gαs/olf)-cAMP signaling promotes cholesterol accumulation and inflammasome activation in atherosclerosis. How obesity-associated inflammation amplifies this pathway is unknown. METHODS: We studied human and murine macrophages, genetically modified low-density lipoprotein receptor-deficient (Ldlr-/-) bone marrow chimeras, and human carotid plaques using biochemical assays and a macrophage-targeted resistance to inhibitors of cholinesterase 8B (Ric-8B)-Gα interference peptide. RESULTS: oxLDL (oxidized low-density lipoprotein) activated Gαolf through OR6A2 (olfactory receptor 6A2) and Gαs through downregulation of phosphorylated Gα-interacting vesicle-associated protein (p-GIV [phosphorylated Gα-interacting vesicle-associated protein]); both required Ric-8B. Ric-8B bound nucleotide-free Gαolf and Gαs with high affinity (KD, 21 and 29 nmol/L) through Arg75 and promoted their folding, stability, membrane localization, and cAMP signaling. Disrupting this interface reduced macrophage inflammasome activation and cholesterol accumulation. In Ldlr-/- chimeras, the targeted interference peptide localized to plaque macrophages, suppressed lesional Gαs/olf activity, and reduced atherosclerosis; these effects were absent with a nonbinding control peptide or Ric-8BR75E. In male patients' carotid plaques, plasma IFN-γ (interferon-γ) correlated with macrophage-associated Ric-8B S468/T473 phosphorylation. IFN-γ activated a STAT1 (signal transducer and activator of transcription 1)-independent ERK2 (extracellular signal-regulated kinase 2)-casein kinase 2 α catalytic subunit pathway that phosphorylated Ric-8B at S468/T473, enhancing chaperone activity. Phosphomimetic substitution lowered the pooled fitted oxLDL EC50 for cAMP generation (11.5 versus 27.7 µg/mL in wild-type cells) without increasing basal cAMP; replicate-level EC50 estimates did not differ significantly (P=0.17). This substitution restored the atherogenic phenotype suppressed by Ifngr1 deficiency in obese, but not nonobese, chimeras. CONCLUSIONS: Ric-8B sustains macrophage Gαs/olf-cAMP signaling and atherogenesis. Obesity-associated IFN-γ enhances macrophage responses to oxLDL through STAT1-independent ERK2-casein kinase 2 α catalytic subunit-Ric-8B signaling, supporting a 2-hit mechanism and identifying the Ric-8B-Gα interface as a potential therapeutic target.

recs.title: Rivaroxaban Inhibits Platelet-Driven NOX2-Dependent Oxidative Injury to Endothelium.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Endothelial dysfunction is a hallmark of cardiovascular disease, driven by oxidative stress, inflammation, and platelet activation. We hypothesized that the FXa inhibitor rivaroxaban, alone or combined with clopidogrel, could counteract platelet-induced oxidative injury to the endothelium and preserve endothelial function. METHODS: We conducted a prospective multicenter cohort clinical study in patients on chronic antiplatelet therapy (mostly aspirin) who initiated rivaroxaban, measuring indices of oxidative stress, endothelial function (nitric oxide bioavailability, ICAM-1/VCAM-1 levels), and platelet activation before and after rivaroxaban. In parallel, human endothelial cells were exposed to convulxin-activated platelet supernatants from healthy donors with or without rivaroxaban±clopidogrel, and assessed for NOX2 expression/activity, adhesion molecules, nitric oxide (NO) production, and tube-forming capacity. An ex vivo mouse model of angiotensin II-induced endothelial dysfunction was used to evaluate vascular relaxation responses after incubation with rivaroxaban and/or clopidogrel. RESULTS: Rivaroxaban significantly improved endothelial function in patients and in vitro, as shown by reduced endothelial ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 expression and increased NO availability despite platelet-derived oxidative stress. Rivaroxaban also decreased H2O2 production, downregulated endothelial NOX2 expression and sNOX2-dp release, and restored angiogenic capacity in endothelial cells exposed to activated platelets. Clopidogrel alone had negligible effects on these parameters. Notably, adding clopidogrel to rivaroxaban provided no additional endothelial benefit beyond rivaroxaban monotherapy. In an ex vivo hypertensive vessel model, rivaroxaban (but not clopidogrel) markedly improved endothelium-dependent relaxation. CONCLUSIONS: Rivaroxaban effectively preserves endothelial function by inhibiting platelet-induced NOX2-mediated oxidative stress and inflammation. The lack of any additive benefit from clopidogrel suggests that rivaroxaban alone may be mechanistically sufficient to counteract platelet-driven endothelial dysfunction. These findings reveal a novel vasoprotective mechanism for rivaroxaban and underscore its potential clinical value in mitigating vascular injury beyond its established antithrombotic effects.

recs.title: Greenspace Exposure Reduces the Risk of Hypertension: A Large Prospective Cohort Study in Northwestern China.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The effects of greenspace on hypertension remain unconfirmed. This study aimed to validate this by performing a large prospective cohort study in China. METHODS: PEAHEN-China (Prospective Environment and Health Epidemiological Study in Northwestern China) recruited 5 484 119 adults in 2017 and followed them to 2021. Blood pressure levels and hypertension were measured and defined using recommended standards. Greenspace exposure was estimated using the normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index. Cox regression models and generalized estimating equation models were used to assess the associations of greenspace with hypertension incidence and blood pressure levels, respectively. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were also performed. RESULTS: During a median 3.21-year follow-up, 1 290 003 new hypertension cases occurred. Living in greener areas was significantly associated with a lower risk of hypertension and lower blood pressure levels. For example, in the adjusted models, compared with the first quartile of normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index within a 500-m buffer, the hazard ratios of incident hypertension in the fourth quartile of the 2 metrics were 0.871 (95% CI, 0.861-0.881) and 0.896 (95% CI, 0.885-0.906). In addition, stronger associations of greenspace exposure with hypertension risk and blood pressure levels were observed in younger, male, rural, and less educated participants than their counterparts. CONCLUSIONS: Our study indicates that neighborhood greenspace may reduce residents' odds of having hypertension, offering robust evidence for developing policies and strategies to mitigate the burden of hypertension.

recs.title: Intrapancreatic fat deposition: an emerging organ-specific dimension of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome?
Outcomes Among Patients Receiving Watchman LAAO vs Antiplatelet Therapy: A Report From the GWTG-AFIB Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although Watchman left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) was approved for patients with atrial fibrillation who can tolerate short term anticoagulation, many patients are poor candidates for any duration of anticoagulation. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to compare 1-year outcomes among patients receiving Watchman LAAO vs antiplatelet monotherapy. METHODS: We performed an overlap weighted observational comparative effectiveness analysis of postdischarge outcomes among Medicare beneficiaries in the Get With The Guidelines-AFIB Registry who received LAAO or antiplatelet therapy. Cox Regression was used for all-cause mortality and cause-specific hazard models were used for nonfatal outcomes. A win ratio was calculated with the following endpoint hierarchy: 1) all-cause death; 2) stroke, systemic embolism, or transient ischemic attack (TIA); 3) major bleeding (excluding gastrointestinal bleeding); and 4) gastrointestinal bleeding. RESULTS: A total of 1,427 patients who received LAAO and 2,284 patients who received antiplatelet therapy were studied (overall median age 77 years, 49.3% female, median CHA2DS2-VASC score 5). Through the first 45 days, the adjusted risk of stroke, TIA or systemic embolism, major bleeding, or death was lower among patients who received LAAO (HR: 0.26; CI: 0.17-0.41; P < 0.001). Between 46 days and 1 year, the risk for the composite outcome was lower among patients who received LAAO (HR: 0.61; CI: 0.48-0.78; P < 0.001). The win ratio at 1 year was 2.71 (95% CI: 1.92-3.83; P < 0.0001), indicating significantly better outcomes among LAAO patients. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atrial fibrillation, treatment with LAAO was associated with a lower risk of stroke, TIA or systemic embolism, major bleeding, or death compared to antiplatelet therapy.

recs.title: Longest atrial fibrillation episode and clinical outcomes in implantable cardioverter-defibrillator recipients.
Prognostic significance of incident microalbuminuria in a real-world population at increased cardiovascular risk: A report from a global federated research network.
recs.abstract: AIM: Despite growing interest in biomarker-based risk stratification for incident heart failure (HF), the prognostic value of newly detected microalbuminuria is poorly defined. This study evaluated its association with incident HF and cardiorenal outcomes in a large real-world cohort. METHODS: A total of 985,367 patients aged 40-80 years at increased cardiovascular (CV) risk but with no prior HF or chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage ≥3 was included from the TriNetX Global Research Network. Patients with persistent normoalbuminuria (UACR <30 mg/g) were compared to those with newly detected microalbuminuria (UACR 30-300 mg/g). The primary outcome was a composite of incident HF or all-cause mortality over a maximum 5-year follow-up. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: After matching, 150,250 patients were included in each group. Over a median follow-up of 2.5 [IQR range, 3.6] years, newly detected microalbuminuria was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite outcome (HR 1.29 [95% CI 1.25-1.34]), as well as higher incident HF (HR 1.31 [95% CI 1.26-1.36]), all-cause mortality (HR 1.43 [95% CI 1.35-1.51]), HFrEF (HR 1.61 [95% CI 1.51-1.71]), HFpEF (HR 1.37 [95% CI 1.29-1.45]), acute myocardial infarction (HR 1.33 [95% CI 1.25-1.41]), ischemic stroke (HR 1.27 [95% CI 1.20-1.35]) and increased risks of CKD progression to stage 3 (HR 2.80 [95% CI 2.67-2.93]) and stage 4 (HR 4.71 [95% CI 4.11-5.40]). In exploratory subgroup analyses, renal function showed the largest number of nominal interaction findings. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort of patients at increased CV risk, newly detected microalbuminuria was associated with higher cardiorenal risk, supporting further evaluation of UACR for early risk stratification.

recs.title: Beyond the coronary tree: can AI-derived myocardial radiomics from routine computed tomography angiography refine long-term prediction of myocardial infarction?
Bioprosthetic valve performance of transcatheter aortic valves.
recs.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation is used increasingly in younger patients with longer life expectancy, necessitating long-term effectiveness. Randomised clinical trials have demonstrated comparable or superior haemodynamic performance of transcatheter heart valves (THVs) to surgical aortic valve replacement over midterm follow-up. Within a lifetime management framework, haemodynamic performance and durability of THVs are central considerations in patients undergoing aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis. This review provides an overview of THV design and function along with contemporary clinical evidence, with a focus on current haemodynamic assessment considerations, challenges in cross-platform interpretation of valve performance, and limitations of randomised comparative evidence, as well as future directions in the evaluation of THV performance.

recs.title: Interpreting Pulsed-Field Ablation Durability: Lesion Sets, Operator Experience, and Procedural Workflow.
Sex-Stratified Outcomes in Balloon Angioplasty for Symptomatic Intracranial Artery Stenosis: The BASIS Subgroup Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The BASIS (Balloon Angioplasty for Symptomatic Intracranial Artery Stenosis) trial demonstrated that balloon angioplasty plus aggressive medical management was superior to aggressive medical management alone for symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis. However, whether sex modifies this treatment effect is unknown. METHODS: This prespecified secondary analysis of the BASIS randomized controlled trial included 501 patients with symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis from 31 Chinese centers (November 2018 to April 2022). Baseline characteristics and outcomes were compared between sexes and across treatment arms within each sex. The primary outcome was stroke or death within 30 days, or ischemic stroke in the qualifying artery territory or revascularization beyond 30 days through 12 months. RESULTS: Among 501 patients (mean age, 58 years), 158 (31.5%) were women. No significant sex-by-treatment interaction was observed for primary or key secondary outcomes (all P for interaction >0.05). In sex-stratified analyses, balloon angioplasty reduced primary outcome risk versus aggressive medical management in men (2.9% versus 11.1%; hazard ratio [HR]=0.21 [95% CI, 0.07-0.65]; P=0.01). In women, the effect favored balloon angioplasty but was not statistically significant (7.8% versus 18.5%; HR=0.37 [95% CI, 0.14-1.01]; P=0.051). CONCLUSIONS: No significant interaction between sex and treatment effect was found, suggesting balloon angioplasty's benefit relative to aggressive medical management does not clearly differ by sex. Sex-stratified results showed significant benefit in men and a nonsignificant trend in women, but the study lacked power for definitive interaction testing, so findings are exploratory. Further research is needed to confirm these findings in broader populations. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT03703635.

recs.title: The Electrocardiogram as a Preventive Biomarker: From Conventional Risk Markers to Actionable Artificial Intelligence - A Narrative Review.
recs.abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is an established tool in cardiovascular prevention, identifying silent arrhythmias, hypertrophy, prior myocardial infarction, conduction disease, and inherited electrical disorders. However, conventional interpretation captures only a fraction of the information embedded in the cardiac electrical signal. Because the ECG is inexpensive, non-invasive, standardized, and already acquired at scale, it provides an attractive substrate for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening and risk stratification. Deep-learning models can identify latent signatures of ventricular dysfunction, structural heart disease, atrial fibrillation, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, and mortality risk. Importantly, evidence is beginning to extend beyond retrospective validation: prospective implementation studies have increased disease detection, while randomized data suggest that AI-ECG-guided clinical alerts may improve outcomes in selected high-risk populations. Whether such benefits extend to preventive populations remains uncertain. This review examines the preventive role of conventional, ambulatory, and wearable ECGs and distinguishes AI applications for detection, prediction, prognostication, treatment selection, and longitudinal monitoring. We argue that performance metrics alone are insufficient. Preventive value requires a defined target population, calibrated and externally validated predictions, an appropriate confirmatory test, a feasible clinical workflow, and an intervention proven to improve outcomes. The most credible near-term applications are those that triage patients to established diagnostic pathways, such as echocardiography or prolonged rhythm monitoring. The central challenge is therefore to transform accurate AI-ECG predictions into actionable, affordable, scalable, safe, and equitable prevention.

recs.title: Impaired Orthostatic Preload Reserve in Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome-Associated Orthostatic Tachycardia.
Before Metabolic Syndrome: Moving Cardiovascular Prevention Earlier.
Exercise Dose during Cardiac Rehabilitation and Long-Term Mortality: Beyond Program Attendance.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Exercise dose in cardiac rehabilitation is commonly inferred from program attendance or changes in exercise capacity rather than quantified from achieved exercise exposure. This study examined the association between supervised exercise dose and long-term mortality and 12-month hospital readmission in patients attending outpatient cardiac rehabilitation. METHODS: This retrospective study included 1032 patients attending outpatient cardiac rehabilitation, with average follow-up of 6.9±1.7 years. Exercise dose was quantified from 10 959 supervised exercise sessions using metabolic equivalent based calculations derived from session intensity and duration, expressed as metabolic equivalent min week-1. Cox proportional hazards models examined associations between exercise dose and long-term mortality after adjustment for baseline demographics, comorbidities, and functional capacity (6-minute walk distance). Logistic regression examined 12-month readmission. Kaplan-Meier analysis examined survival across quartiles of weekly exercise dose. RESULTS: We observed separation in survival across quartiles of weekly exercise dose (log-rank χ2=20.23, P<0.001). Mortality events decreased across dose quartiles, from 48/258 (18.6%) in the lowest quartile to 13/258 (5.0%) in the highest quartile (208-367 metabolic equivalent min week-1). Higher achieved exercise dose was independently associated with lower mortality risk, although the association was attenuated after adjustment for baseline functional capacity. Baseline functional capacity was independently associated with mortality. Exercise dose was not associated with 12-month readmission. CONCLUSIONS: Achieved exercise dose during cardiac rehabilitation demonstrated a linear association with long-term mortality despite no relationship with short-term readmission. Exercise dose accrued during a relatively brief period of rehabilitation may therefore represent an important and measurable aspect of program participation associated with long-term survival.

recs.title: Simultaneous leaflet laceration and valve fracture or remodelling in valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve interventions: the "crack-LLAMACORN" technique.
Exercise Capacity and Mental Health in Adults With a Systemic Right Ventricle.
Environmental noise and cardiometabolic health: a transatlantic perspective.
recs.abstract: Environmental noise is a pervasive but under-recognized cardiovascular and metabolic risk factor. Drawing on prior expert reviews and large-scale epidemiologic and mechanistic studies, this review synthesizes evidence on the burden, major clinical associations, biological pathways, vulnerable populations, and mitigation strategies relevant to cardiovascular health. Road traffic noise is consistently and dose-dependently associated with higher risks of ischaemic heart disease, stroke, heart failure, diabetes, sleep disturbance, and adverse mental health outcomes, whereas for railway and aircraft noise, the evidence base is less consistent, although important associations are increasingly reported. Translational human imaging studies, controlled exposure experiments, and animal models converge on a common pathway in which chronic and intermittent noise exposure activates stress-responsive neural circuits, increases sympathetic and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity, promotes oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular inflammation, and may thereby accelerate cardiometabolic disease. Noise frequently co-occurs with air pollution, heat, and adverse social and built environments, particularly in socioeconomically disadvantaged communities, and these combined exposures may contribute additively to cardiovascular risk. These effects are especially relevant in urban populations with nighttime exposure and multiple co-exposures. Despite this growing evidence base, environmental noise remains largely absent from contemporary cardiovascular risk assessment tools, prevention guidelines, and routine patient counselling, representing a missed opportunity for risk reduction. Effective mitigation will require a hierarchical strategy combining source reduction, health-informed urban and transport planning, and targeted individual protection. Reducing environmental noise exposure should be recognized as an important opportunity to protect and advance cardiovascular and metabolic health in the 21st century.

recs.title: Growth of Improper Medicare Payments for Cardiac Procedures: 2018 to 2024.
Poorly Controlled Hypertension Alters Coronary Microvascular Contractile Response to Endothelin-1 Before and After Cardiac Surgery.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic hypertension have worse outcomes following on-pump (cardioplegia and cardiopulmonary bypass [CP/CPB]) cardiac surgery. Altered vasomotor function of the coronary microvasculature to ET-1 (endothelin-1) and other agonists may underlie these differences. METHODS: Heart samples were collected from 85 patients undergoing CP/CPB enrolled in this observational study. Ex vivo coronary microvascular responses to ET-1, adenosine diphosphate, and sodium nitroprusside were assessed using video microscopy. Immunoblotting, immunohistochemistry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and multiomics approaches were also used. RESULTS: Coronary microvascular contractile response to ET-1 in patients with uncontrolled hypertension was increased compared with the other 2 cohorts pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05 across ET-1 10-10 to 10-7 mmol/L). Adenosine diphosphate-induced coronary microvascular vasodilation was conversely decreased (P<0.05 for adenosine diphosphate 10-5 and 10-4 mmol/L). Post-CP/CPB microvascular responses to ET-1 and adenosine diphosphate were blunted overall (P<0.05). Antagonism of pro-vasoconstrictive endothelinA receptor diminished contractile response (P<0.05). Transcriptomics and proteomics showed wide regulation of pro-vasoconstrictive pathways. Regression showed that hypertension status and cardiac mass reliably approximated ET-1-induced coronary microvascular contraction (R2 0.95 pre-CP/CPB, R2 0.86 post-CP/CPB), which, in turn, estimated change in ejection fraction pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05). Patients with uncontrolled hypertension had -11% change in EF when compared with the other 2 groups pooled (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Altered coronary microvascular vasomotor function in patients with uncontrolled hypertension may jeopardize myocardial perfusion. Hypertension status and cardiac mass may be used to prognosticate this physiology, which, in turn, estimates change in ejection fraction postoperatively. Perioperative endothelin receptor blockers may benefit patients with uncontrolled hypertension and thus warrant further investigation.

recs.title: Shifting the Pressure-Natriuresis Curve: The Cellular Mechanisms of Female Renal Resilience.
recs.abstract: Female and male kidneys exhibit markedly different patterns of transporter abundance and activity along the nephron, yet the physiological significance of the differences remains incompletely understood. Recent experimental and computational studies suggest that many of these differences can be interpreted through the lens of pressure natriuresis, the kidney's primary mechanism for long-term regulation of extracellular volume and arterial pressure. We review evidence that the female nephron exhibits a transport architecture that may facilitate enhanced pressure natriuresis and greater flexibility in effective circulating volume regulation. This framework provides new insights into sex differences in acute and chronic blood pressure control and connects pressure-natriuretic mechanisms with renal adaptations during pregnancy and lactation, hypertension, and aging.

recs.title: Weekly Journal Scan: Can we detect and REACT early enough to change the trajectory of subclinical atherosclerosis?
Population Impact of the 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Dyslipidemia Guideline on Lipid-Lowering Therapy Eligibility Among US Adults.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association dyslipidemia guideline replaces the pooled cohort equations with the atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease component of the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events equations for primary prevention risk estimation and modifies lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) eligibility by lowering the risk-based treatment threshold and expanding diabetes and chronic kidney disease criteria. The population-level impact of this transition is uncertain. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2021 to 2023 participants aged 40 to 75 years without self-reported atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and with available low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Survey weights were used to generate national estimates. Guideline-supported LLT eligibility was assessed under the 2018 pooled cohort equations-based American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association cholesterol framework and the 2026 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association dyslipidemia framework. Current LLT use was assessed among guideline-supported adults. RESULTS: The analytic sample included 1662 participants, representing 115.05 million US adults. LLT was supported for 42.82 million adults under the 2018 framework and 42.17 million under the 2026 framework, a net decrease of 0.65 million. Reclassification was substantial: 37.42 million remained supported, 5.40 million lost support, 4.75 million newly gained support, and 67.48 million remained unsupported. Among supported adults, current LLT use was 39.4% under the 2018 framework and 40.5% under the 2026 framework. CONCLUSIONS: Transition to the 2026 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based framework produced little net change in LLT eligibility but meaningfully changed who was supported for therapy. Persistent undertreatment remains a major implementation gap.

recs.title: Peri-aortic fat imaging: a window to vascular ageing.
Nationwide transcatheter aortic valve implantation rollout and cardiac-origin out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in the elderly.
Immersive Reality in Cardiothoracic Surgical Education.
recs.abstract: Immersive reality technologies, including virtual reality, augmented reality, mixed reality, and related extended reality platforms, are reforming how surgeons learn complex anatomy, rehearse procedures, develop technical skills, and manage unexpected or rare intraoperative crises. Cardiothoracic surgery is particularly well suited to these tools because postgraduate training occurs in a high-stakes environment characterized by complex 3-dimensional anatomy, limited operative exposure, minimally invasive/robotic approaches, open communication, and the need for synchronized team performance. Immersive platforms facilitate anatomy education and procedural planning and enable deliberate practice and nontechnical skills training. Although most studies remain small, heterogeneous, and focused on surrogate outcomes rather than patient outcomes, evidence from surgical education and cardiothoracic surgery literature demonstrates that these tools impart improvement in knowledge, confidence, procedural accuracy, and simulator performance. This article defines immersive reality technologies, reviews their educational rationale and emerging applications in cardiothoracic surgery, proposes an implementation framework for training programs, and highlights limitations related to haptics, validation, privacy, equity, and regulatory oversight. The next phase should focus on validation of outcome-linked curricula that integrate immersive simulation into competency-based surgical education.

recs.title: Temporal Trends and Racial and Geographic Variation in Left Atrial Appendage Closure Among Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
Evaluating the Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Paradox in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypercholesterolemia is an established cardiovascular risk factor. However, studies in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) showed an association between low low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and increased mortality, termed the "LDL-C paradox." This study examined the impact of LDL-C on clinical outcomes in patients with HFrEF and identify distinct hypocholesterolemia subgroups using latent class analysis. METHODS: Consecutive patients with HFrEF (left ventricular EF <40%) from national registries (2016-2022) were stratified by LDL-C quartiles, with the lowest quartile ≤1.73 mmol/L. Latent class analysis was performed to identify subsets of patients in the lowest quartile. Outcomes included 1-year all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, readmission, and composite end points. RESULTS: Among 2188 patients, the lowest LDL-C quartile had higher 1-year all-cause mortality than Quartile 2 and 3 (P<0.05) but not Quartile 4, with no intergroup differences in cardiovascular mortality, readmissions, or composite outcomes between groups. Latent class analysis identified 2 hypocholesterolemia subgroups: pathological and nonpathological hypocholesterolemia. The pathological subgroup was older, lower weight, with higher comorbidity burden. Compared with patients with hypercholesterolemia, the pathological hypocholesterolemia subgroup had higher 1-year all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.14 [95% CI, 1.17-2.69], P<0.001), cardiovascular mortality (adjusted HR, 1.93 [95% CI, 1.46-2.54], P<0.001), and composite end points (adjusted HR, 1.15 [95% CI, 1.01-1.30], P=0.037), and the subgroup with nonpathological hypocholesterolemia showed comparable outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: A distinct subset of patients with HFrEF with low LDL-C demonstrates different clinical characteristics (older and higher comorbidity burden) and poorer outcomes, potentially elucidating the "LDL-C paradox" cause in patients with HFrEF.

recs.title: Clinical Safety Evaluation of a Large Language Model for Heart Failure Treatment Recommendations.
Author's reply to Letter to the Editor - A methodological note on PRAETORIAN score reporting.
Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Closure Device Utilization Among Medicare Beneficiaries.
What Counts in a Stroke-Prevention Strategy?: A Patient-Centered Framework for Cardiovascular Care in Atrial Fibrillation.
Impact of Smoking on Transfusion Outcomes in Anemia and Myocardial Infarction: A MINT Trial Analysis.
Clinical characteristics and prognosis of heart failure patients referred to cardiac rehabilitation: SEC-EXCELENTE-IC registry.
recs.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To assess the referral rate to cardiac rehabilitation (CR), the clinical profile of referred vs nonreferred patients, and the association between referral and clinical events in Spanish heart failure (HF) units. METHODS: The SEC-EXCELENTE-IC registry is a prospective, multicenter observational cohort of patients with HF in units accredited by the Spanish Society of Cardiology. Patients were classified according to CR referral and were followed up for up to 400 days for all-cause death, HF hospitalization or decompensation, and the combined endpoint of death or HF hospitalization, with outcomes analyzed using Cox regression. RESULTS: Of 2236 patients, 219 (9.8%) were referred to CR. Referred patients were younger (65.2  ±  11.7 vs 71.7  ±  12.2 years), more often male (73.5% vs 63.2%) and more frequently had an ischemic etiology (50.5% vs 28.8%), fewer comorbidities and more frequent use of quadruple therapy (59.4% vs 46.0%); 74.4% had HF with reduced ejection fraction (11.9% had HF with preserved ejection fraction, and 13.7% HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction). The lower crude rate of the combined endpoint (HR, 0.75; 95%CI, 0.56-1.01) was no longer observed after adjustment (HR, 0.99; 95%CI, 0.71-1.38), with consistent findings in sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: CR referral was infrequent and preferentially directed toward younger patients with ischemic HF with reduced ejection fraction, a lower comorbidity burden, and optimized therapy, whereas older patients, patients with multimorbidity, and those with HF with preserved ejection fraction remained underrepresented. The lower crude event rate was no longer observed after adjustment for measured baseline characteristics, and the observational design does not allow conclusions on the effect of CR itself.

recs.title: Habitual Coffee Consumption, Genetic Susceptibility, and Incident Stroke: A Prospective Cohort Study in the UK Biobank.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between habitual coffee consumption and incident stroke remains uncertain. METHODS: We analyzed 490 889 UK Biobank participants without prevalent stroke. Average self-reported coffee intake across available assessments was categorized as ≤0.5, 0.6 to 1.67, 1.68 to 3.0, and >3.0 cups/d. Incident stroke was ascertained through linkage to hospital and death registries and self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable Cox models and restricted cubic splines characterized associations. Analyses assessed effect modification by CYP1A2 genotype and stroke polygenic risk score and used multiple-imputation and competing-risk sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: During follow-up, 22 579 incident strokes occurred. Compared with ≤0.5 cups/d, adjusted hazard ratios were 0.86 (95% CI, 0.83-0.89) for 0.6 to 1.67 cups/d, 0.92 (95% CI, 0.89-0.96) for 1.68 to 3.0 cups/d, and 0.98 (95% CI, 0.94-1.02) for >3.0 cups/d. Splines showed a nonlinear J-shaped association, with the lowest estimated risk at ∼2 to 3 cups/d. Associations were broadly consistent across CYP1A2 and polygenic-risk strata, with no significant interaction. Moderate intake was associated with lower risk among participants reporting sugar addition, whereas high decaffeinated-coffee intake was associated with higher risk. CONCLUSIONS: Moderate habitual coffee consumption was associated with lower incident stroke risk, with the lowest observed risk at ∼2 to 3 cups/d. These observational findings should not be interpreted as evidence to prescribe coffee for stroke prevention.

recs.title: Safety and Efficacy of Transvenous Lead Extraction Using a Right-Sided Approach.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite extensive experience with transvenous lead extraction (TLE) overall, outcomes for systems implanted on the right chest remain underexplored, largely because of their low incidence. OBJECTIVES: The objective was to evaluate whether system laterality influences TLE outcomes. METHODS: Using our institutional, prospectively maintained ExTRACT registry, we analyzed all consecutive patients undergoing TLE procedures at the Cleveland Clinic between 1996 and 2022. Patients were categorized by system laterality. Baseline characteristics, procedural characteristics, and complications were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated the association between right-sided TLE and adverse events. RESULTS: Among 4,989 patients, 494 (9.9%) had right-sided and 4,495 (90.1%) had left-sided TLE. Compared with left-sided cases, right-sided cases had longer total lead dwell times (13.83 vs 9.26 years, P < 0.001) and were more likely to be extracted because of infection (47.57% vs 39.71%, P = 0.001). Fluoroscopy time was longer (15.95 vs 12.1 minutes; P < 0.001), and femoral workstation use more frequent (7.89% vs 4.05%, P < 0.001), yet complete extraction was lower (94.53% vs 96.44%, P = 0.034). Right-sided TLE had higher rates of sternotomy (2.83% vs 1.25%, P = 0.004) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (2.49% vs 1.10%, P = 0.009). Thirty-day mortality was low and comparable (0.61% vs 0.47%, P = 0.727). Multivariable regression showed that right-sided TLE was associated with higher odds of sternotomy (OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.01-3.46, P = 0.037) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (OR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.01-3.78, P = 0.037). CONCLUSIONS: Right-sided TLE is associated with a lower rate of complete extraction and increased procedural risk, particularly sternotomy and major vascular injury, compared with left-sided TLE. These findings should be carefully weighed when implanting or extracting right-sided systems.

recs.title: 2-Year Patency as a Lightning Rod? Biological Hypotheses Linking PCSK9-Inhibition to Favorable Vein Graft Remodeling.

recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve (TAV)-in-TAV compared with TAV-in-surgical aortic valve (SAV) implantation for failed bioprosthetic valves have been limited to short-term outcomes. AIMS: This study compared midterm outcomes between patients undergoing TAV-in-TAV and those undergoing TAV-in-SAV. METHODS: From June 2015 to June 2024, 543 consecutive patients undergoing valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) were identified at our centre. After exclusion of ineligible patients, 109 patients undergoing TAV-in-TAV and 349 undergoing TAV-in-SAV were included. Following propensity score matching, 214 patients (107 per group) were analysed. RESULTS: Three-year all-cause mortality did not differ between the TAV-in-TAV and TAV-in-SAV groups (hazard ratio 1.06, 95% confidence interval: 0.56-1.98; p=0.867). Similarly, no significant differences were detected in secondary outcomes. Over 3 years, the aortic valve mean pressure gradient was consistently lower and the aortic valve area was consistently larger in the TAV-in-TAV group compared with the TAV-in-SAV group. Concomitant percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and coronary obstruction were more frequent in the TAV-in-SAV group than in the TAV-in-TAV group (22.4% vs 8.4%; p=0.006; 10.3% vs 0.9%; p=0.018, respectively). Post-ViV-TAVI computed tomography analysis showed that the waist level was the least expanded segment in both groups. However, expansion at this level was significantly greater in the TAV-in-TAV group than in the TAV-in-SAV group. CONCLUSIONS: There was no significant difference in 3-year mortality between the TAV-in-TAV and TAV-in-SAV groups. However, TAV-in-SAV was associated with higher rates of concomitant PCI and coronary obstruction, as well as lower valve expansion.

The clinical relevance of lipoprotein(a) in the post-Lp(a)HORIZON era: A statement of the European Atherosclerosis Society.
recs.abstract: Considering the recent Lp(a)HORIZON trial results showing that pelacarsen with 78% lowering of lipoprotein(a) in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease did not further reduce such events, the European Atherosclerosis Society (EAS) underscores that high lipoprotein(a) remains a genetically determined risk modifier of cardiovascular disease independently of LDL cholesterol concentrations and other traditional risk factors. The EAS maintains its recommendation for one-time universal lipoprotein(a) testing to assess individual cardiovascular risk, to guide preventive strategies - especially optimal LDL cholesterol lowering - and to facilitate family screening. The EAS acknowledges key unresolved questions and advocates for sustained research and future clinical trials on lipoprotein(a) lowering to reduce the burden of cardiovascular disease.

recs.title: Acute pulmonary embolism: long-term cause-specific mortality in a Chinese nationwide registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Long-term cause-specific mortality after acute pulmonary embolism (PE) remains poorly characterized. This study investigated cumulative mortality, temporal changes in causes of death, and associated factors in a national registry. METHODS: This registry-based cohort study consecutively enrolled 66 192 acute PE patients from 3223 Chest Pain Centres across China (2018-2023) (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04014972). Mortality was ascertained through national registry linkage. Cumulative incidence functions estimated temporal mortality patterns, while Fine-Gray models exploratorily examined factors associated with cause-specific mortality. RESULTS: At 60 months, cumulative all-cause mortality was 22.41% (95% confidence interval [CI] 21.92-22.91), comprising cardiovascular (CV) (11.84%, 95% CI 11.46-12.23) and non-CV mortality (10.57%, 95% CI 10.22-10.92). Causes of death varied over time: acute PE and ischaemic heart disease (IHD) predominated initially, malignancy peaked at 1-3 months, and IHD was the largest named cause in each interval beyond 12 months. Among CV deaths, IHD was the predominant cause (35.7%); malignancy (43.3%) and chronic pulmonary disease (24.6%) predominated among non-CV deaths. Men had higher cumulative CV and non-CV mortality than women; while women only had a higher proportion of CV causes among deaths. All-cause mortality increased with age (from 11.52% at <55 to 38.51% at ≥75 years); acute PE/malignancy dominated in younger patients, while CV/pulmonary disease prevailed in older ones. Exploratory analyses identified age, Western China residence, and vital signs as factors associated with mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients hospitalised with acute PE, 5-year cumulative mortality was 22.4%, and nearly half of deaths were from non-CV causes. Shifting mortality patterns highlight the need to evaluate risk-adapted long-term follow-up strategies.

Effectiveness of Bariatric Surgery and Incretin-based Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Obesity: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies improve cardiometabolic risk factors. However, direct head-to-head comparisons assessing their impact on cardiovascular outcomes remain limited. We performed an exploratory meta-analysis to compare bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies on major clinical outcomes in adults with obesity. METHODS: A systematic literature search using PubMed and Scopus databases was conducted. Randomized and observational studies comparing bariatric surgery or incretin receptor agonists with controls were included in the analysis. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and MACE. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was conducted across three nodes. RESULTS: A total of 40 studies, comprising more than 1.9 million patients, were included in the meta-analysis. Compared with control, bariatric surgery was associated with a significant reduction in all evaluated outcomes, including all-cause mortality (HR:0.57, 95%CI:0.51-0.65), MACE (HR:0.54, 95%CI:0.45-0.64), cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, myocardial infarction, and stroke. Incretin receptor agonists were also associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR:0.62, 95%CI:0.52-0.74), lower MACE (HR:0.75, 95%CI:0.61-0.92) and reduced heart failure hospitalization. All-cause mortality-representing the most direct and clinically relevant endpoint-did not differ significantly between the two strategies in the exploratory network meta-analysis. Importantly, the network estimates should be cautiously interpreted, given the predominance of observational evidence, substantial heterogeneity, and very low confidence across all comparisons. CONCLUSION: Bariatric surgery and incretin receptor agonists are associated with substantial reductions in major cardiovascular outcomes in adults with obesity. In head-to-head comparisons, no significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality and stroke. Both strategies provide clinically meaningful benefits.

recs.title: Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement for Aortic Regurgitation in LVAD Patients: The JENA-VAD Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic regurgitation (AR) during left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support causes recurrent heart failure. Surgery is high risk and stenosis-designed valves anchor poorly in noncalcified anatomy. OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate early outcomes of the AR-specific Trilogy transcatheter heart valve for LVAD-associated AR. METHODS: JENA-VAD is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm investigational device exemption study. An independent committee adjudicated endpoints using VARC-3 (Valve Academic Research Consortium-3) definitions. The primary efficacy endpoint was the VARC-3 device success composite adapted for LVAD support, and the primary safety endpoint was the VARC-3 early safety composite. RESULTS: Fifty patients were treated (mean age 69.2 years; 40% female). Median follow-up was 105 days (range 27 to 577 days). Technical and device success were 96.0% (95% CI: 86.3-99.5). Freedom from any component event of the VARC-3 early safety composite was 90.0% (95% CI: 78.2-96.7). At 30 days, 7 VARC-3 safety events occurred in 5 patients: type 2 to 4 bleeding (n = 2), major vascular complications (n = 2), device-related peripheral interventions (n = 2), and new pacemaker (1 of 7 without prior pacing; 14.3%). There were no strokes or myocardial infarctions. Two transient ischemic attacks occurred in patients without valve abnormalities. Beyond 30 days, cardiovascular death occurred in 1 patient (day 86). Follow-up computed tomography (CT) imaging or transesophageal echocardiography was obtained in 12 patients, and 11 (including 3 within 30 days) had leaflet thickening or thrombosis, including all patients who underwent CT. The remaining 38 patients did not have postprocedure imaging. Two of these events were symptomatic: valve thrombosis and a transient ischemic attack (day 116), and prosthetic AR that required valve-in-valve implantation (day 146) and subsequent heart transplantation. In exploratory analyses, NYHA functional class at 30 days was I or II in 72.3% (34 of 47) and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score rose 11.5 ± 21.5 points (n = 44). CONCLUSIONS: Transcatheter valve replacement using a dedicated system in LVAD patients was feasible with high technical and device success and without early death, stroke, or moderate or severe residual AR. Leaflet thickening or thrombosis, detected on clinically indicated CT imaging, occurred in 22%, representing a lower bound. Follow-up is ongoing to inform longer-term safety and effectiveness. (Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Using the JenaValve Trilogy Heart Valve System for Clinically Significant Aortic Regurgitation in Patients With Left Ventricular Assist Devices [LVAD]; NCT06594705).

recs.title: Intrapancreatic fat as a window into the multiorgan adiposity landscape of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome?
Age-Related Differences in Physical Activity for Primary Prevention of Coronary Heart Disease: Insights From Wearable Accelerometers.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Current physical activity recommendations suggest at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity for primary prevention of coronary heart disease (CHD) across ages. However, age-related disparities exist in exercise capability, engagement, and guideline adherence, and their implications for CHD prevention remain underexplored. METHODS: We included wrist-worn accelerometer data from 80 243 UK Biobank participants (aged 61.54±7.84 years, 57.3% women), classified as older (≥65 years; n=31 663) or middle-aged (<65 years; n=48 580). Cox proportional hazards models were applied to examine age-specific associations between physical activity and incident CHD. Nonlinear and dose-response relationships were assessed using restricted cubic splines, and age-related differences were tested using likelihood ratio tests. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 7.88 years, 3764 CHD events occurred. A 20% lower CHD risk (hazard ratio [HR], 0.8) was observed at approximately 60 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity in older adults versus 330 minutes per week in middle-aged adults (Pinteraction=0.006). Guideline adherence was associated with stronger inverse associations in older than in middle-aged adults (HR, 0.72 versus 0.85; Pinteraction=0.029). Older weekend warriors exhibited a 28% lower CHD risk, comparable with regularly active individuals, whereas the association was weaker and nonsignificant in middle-aged adults (Pinteraction=0.005). At 150 minutes per week, a 10% lower CHD risk corresponded to an acceleration threshold of 100 milligravity in middle-aged adults but approximately 55 milligravity in older adults. A possible U-shaped relationship was observed in older adults. CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest potential age-related heterogeneity in wearable-measured physical activity for CHD prevention, and may help motivate activity engagement among older adults and enhance CHD prevention.

CTA-Guided Anatomical Targeting for Bachmann's Bundle Pacing: First-in-Human Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bachmann's bundle pacing (BBP) is an emerging physiological atrial pacing strategy, but implantation relies on fluoroscopic landmarks and iterative electrophysiological mapping. Whether patient-specific computed tomography angiography (CTA) can facilitate anatomical targeting of Bachmann's bundle has not been investigated. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, procedural performance, and anatomical impact of CTA-guided anatomical targeting for BBP. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, first-in-human study compared 49 consecutive patients undergoing CTA-guided BBP with 28 undergoing conventional electrogram- and fluoroscopy-guided implantation. RESULTS: Using predefined electrocardiographic criteria, successful BBP was achieved in 65 of 77 patients (84%) and was higher with CTA guidance (92% vs. 71%; P=0.024). CTA-guided implantation resulted in a different distribution of final lead positions, with more leads at the predefined B2-B3 target than with the conventional approach (76% vs. 42%; P=0.006; odds ratio 4.20; 95% CI, 1.52-11.60). CTA guidance reduced implantation time (median 2.0 [1.0-3.0] vs. 4.0 [3.0-7.0] minutes; P<0.001), fluoroscopy time (0.4 [0.2-0.6] vs. 1.6 [1.1-2.9] minutes; P<0.001), and lead deployment attempts (1.0 [1.0-2.0] vs. 2.0 [1.8-3.2]; P=0.001), and increased first-pass success (67% vs. 25%; P<0.001). In patients with successful BBP (n=65), BBP shortened P-wave duration in all cases (161±13 to 142±15 ms; relative reduction 11.6±4.4%; P<0.001), with similar reductions irrespective of implantation strategy. No acute lead-related complications occurred, and electrical performance remained stable during short-term follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: CTA-guided anatomical targeting for BBP is feasible and safe. Compared with conventional implantation, this anatomy-first strategy improves procedural efficiency, supporting anatomical guidance as a feasible approach to physiological atrial pacing.

recs.title: Impact of Coronary Sinus Reducer on the Extent of Ischemia in Functional Stress Tests.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The coronary sinus reducer is an established therapy for patients with refractory angina due to obstructive coronary artery disease who are not candidates for further revascularization. Although symptomatic benefits are well documented, its effect on objective measures of ischemia remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between coronary sinus reducer implantation and inducible myocardial ischemia assessed by functional stress testing. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained registry of consecutive patients undergoing coronary sinus reducer implantation between 2011 and 2024. Baseline assessment included Canadian Cardiovascular Society angina class, 6-minute walk test, stress echocardiography, and dipyridamole single-photon emission computed tomography imaging, repeated at 6 months. Coprimary outcomes were changes in stress wall motion score index and in the proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography. Clinical nonresponders were defined as no improvement in Canadian Cardiovascular Society class at 12 months. RESULTS: Among 153 treated patients, 118 had complete imaging data. Median stress wall motion score index improved from 1.38 to 1.23 (P<0.001), and stress left ventricular ejection fraction increased from 55% to 60% (P=0.019). The proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography decreased from 52% to 24% (P<0.001). The summed difference score, available in 45 patients, did not change significantly. Clinically, 86% improved by ≥1 Canadian Cardiovascular Society class at 6 months. CONCLUSIONS: Coronary sinus reducer implantation was associated with reduced inducible ischemia on stress echocardiography and with clinical improvement. The proportion of patients with moderate or severe ischemia on single-photon emission computed tomography decreased following Reducer implantation.

recs.title: Ischemic Mitral Regurgitation: A Changing Paradigm.
Evaluation of the ESC Guideline based risk stratification of syncope patients in the emergency department A post-hoc analysis of the SYNERGY-trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Syncope accounts for approximately 1% of all emergency department(ED) visits. With 1-year mortality rates reaching up to 33% in certain arrhythmogenic aetiologies, adequate assessment in the ED is imperative. The risk stratification as described in the 2018 European Society of Cardiology(ESC) guidelines on syncope is widely used in clinical practice, but has never been validated. We therefore aimed to determine the ability to identify cardiac syncope of the composite guideline-based RISC-score, and investigate the association of individual risk-features and cardiac aetiology. METHODS: 520 patients presenting with syncope to the ED of five Dutch hospitals were included. Adjudicated diagnoses were established by a multidisciplinary expert-panel following one-year of critical follow-up. ED-documentation was analyzed for the presence of guideline risk-features. Overall discriminative ability of the guideline-based RISC-score was evaluated using receiver-operating-characteristic(ROC) curve-analysis. Uni- and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the predictive ability of the individual risk-features. RESULTS: 50 patients(9.6%) were adjudicated with a cardiac aetiology of syncope. The RISC-score demonstrated excellent discriminative ability with an area-under-the-curve(AUC) of 0.928. The guideline based cut-off threshold of 2 points yielded a sensitivity of 96.0%, a specificity of 78.5%, a positive predictive value of 33.2% and a negative predictive value of 99.5%. Multivariate regression analysis identified age, no warning-symptoms, angina pectoris, unevaluated systolic murmur, atrial fibrillation, syncope during exertion and bifascicular-block as independent predictors of cardiac syncope. CONCLUSION: The ESC-guideline based RISC-score can be reliably and safely used for excluding a cardiac aetiology of syncope in patients in the ED.

recs.title: Deletion of Yes-Associated Protein in Vascular Smooth Muscle Cells Alleviates Atherosclerosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The migration and proliferation of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) are critical processes in the development of atherosclerosis. YAP (Yes-associated protein) regulates VSMC migration and proliferation. However, its specific role in atherosclerosis remains unclear. METHODS: Atherosclerosis models were generated in mice injected with adeno-associated virus 8-mPCSK9 (murine proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9) or ApoE-/- (apolipoprotein E knockout) mice by being fed a high-cholesterol diet. Primary VSMCs were used to elucidate its mechanism. RESULTS: YAP expression was elevated in VSMCs within mouse atherosclerotic plaques. Both tamoxifen-mediated YAPΔVSMC or adeno-associated virus-inducible VSMC-specific YAP knockout mice injected with adeno-associated virus 8-mPCSK9 and YAPΔVSMCApoE-/- mice exhibited alleviated atherosclerotic phenotype. Further study found that angiopoietin-2 overexpression induced VSMC phenotypic switching, migration, and proliferation in YAP knockout VSMCs stimulated with platelet-derived growth factor-BB in vitro. Furthermore, the VSMC-specific angiopoietin-2 overexpression could completely reverse VSMC YAP deficiency-alleviated atherosclerotic phenotype and the effect of YAP-mediated VSMC phenotypic switching. Mechanistically, YAP upregulated angiopoietin-2 via TEAD4 (murine TEA domain family member 4) in VSMCs. CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, our findings revealed that YAP promotes atherosclerosis by inducing angiopoietin-2-mediated VSMC phenotypic switching via TEAD4. Inhibition of VSMC YAP may be an effective therapeutic strategy for atherosclerosis.

recs.title: Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation: From Prolapse to Precision Therapy.
recs.abstract: Degenerative mitral valve regurgitation due to mitral valve prolapse affects ≈15 million people globally and is the commonest indication for mitral intervention in high-income countries, but its biology, natural history, and lifetime management are ill defined. This review summarizes current knowledge of the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, risk stratification, and lifetime management of degenerative mitral regurgitation, with a focus on areas of uncertainty, recent advances, and emerging research directions. These include translational research focused on determining genetic and cellular drivers of disease progression and mechanistic studies geared to improve detection and prevention of downstream myocardial dysfunction, particularly in high-risk phenotypes, including arrhythmic mitral prolapse. The current landscape of randomized trials and large registries comparing contemporary surgical and transcatheter treatment and strategies to improve patient access to care and outcomes across all patient risk profiles and populations are also discussed.

Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI. METHODS: We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved). RESULTS: Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P=0.445; C statistic=0.77). CONCLUSIONS: One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

recs.title: Cardiac and Metabolic Effects of Semaglutide in Obesity-Related HFpEF: Rationale and Design of CAMEO-SEMA.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Two-thirds of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) have obesity, and >90% have increased visceral adiposity. Adiposity-associated HFpEF is characterized by hemodynamic congestion driven by impaired cardiac reserve, volume overload and altered blood distribution, adverse cardiac remodeling, pericardial constraint, systemic vascular stiffening, myosteatosis, metabolic dysfunction, and altered adipokine signaling profiles. Recent clinical trials have demonstrated that glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists alleviate symptoms and improve exercise capacity in patients with obesity-related HFpEF, but the mechanisms underlying these benefits remain uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to elucidate the mechanisms by which semaglutide improves clinical status in patients with HFpEF and obesity. METHODS: The CAMEO-SEMA trial is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled mechanistic trial evaluating the effects of semaglutide in obesity-related HFpEF. RESULTS: Eighty-one participants have been randomized in a 2:1 ratio to semaglutide subcutaneously once weekly or matching placebo for 52 weeks. Comprehensive pathophysiological characterization is being performed at baseline and following treatment, including invasive exercise hemodynamic status, transcardiac (arterial and coronary sinus) blood sampling at rest and with exercise, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, submaximal and peak aerobic capacity through expired gas analysis, comprehensive rest and exercise echocardiography, body composition and visceral adiposity assessment, blood volume analysis, oral glucose testing, subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsy, and inflammatory-adipokine profiling. CONCLUSIONS: The CAMEO-SEMA trial will provide comprehensive, novel insights into the mechanisms by which the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists semaglutide affects the key pathophysiological factors causing symptoms, exercise limitation, and morbidity in patients with obesity-related HFpEF. (Cardiac and Metabolic Effects of Semaglutide [CAMEO-SEMA]; NCT05371496).

recs.title: Early outcomes of tricuspid valve replacement in patients with tricuspid regurgitation: the Trisol Early Feasibility Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) could lead to a paradigm shift in treating tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and improving patient quality of life. AIMS: We aimed to report the 30-day outcomes of the Trisol Early Feasibility Study (EFS). METHODS: The Trisol EFS was a single-arm, multicentre study that enrolled patients with symptomatic ≥severe TR despite optimal medical therapy to undergo TTVR with the Trisol system via transjugular access. The primary safety endpoint was the rate of device-related serious adverse events, including death, myocardial infarction, disabling stroke, life-threatening bleeding, renal failure requiring dialysis, and the need for surgery. The primary performance endpoints included technical and procedural success, while secondary endpoints included echocardiographic as well as functional and quality-of-life measures. RESULTS: A total of 19 patients, who were treated with a latest-generation Trisol 12-anchor valve, were included from August 2023 to September 2025. The mean age was 75.8 years (range 62 to 91), 78.9% were female, and 78.9% were in New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III or IV. TR was reduced to mild or less in 87.5% of the subjects and moderate or less in 100% of the subjects. The 30-day composite major adverse event rate was 10.5% (2/19) due to one cardiovascular death and one pacemaker implantation. No other complications were observed. NYHA Class significantly improved to Class I/II (87.5%), and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved by a mean of 13.6±34.6 points. CONCLUSIONS: In this early clinical experience, the Trisol TTVR system demonstrated technical feasibility, overall safety, significant TR reduction, and the ability to improve quality of life and functional status in TR patients.

recs.title: Losing "function" but gaining flow: reframing right ventricular assessment in transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement.

10-Year Outcomes of Initial CTO-PCI vs No CTO-PCI Strategies for Chronic Total Occlusion: The DECISION-CTO Randomized Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The long-term clinical effects of percutaneous coronary intervention for chronic total occlusion (CTO-PCI) remain uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare 10-year clinical outcomes between initial CTO-PCI and no CTO-PCI strategies in the extended follow-up of the DECISION-CTO trial. METHODS: The DECISION-CTO trial was an open-label, multicenter, randomized trial conducted at 19 centers in 5 Asian countries. Patients were randomly assigned to an initial strategy of CTO-PCI or no CTO-PCI, with guideline-directed medical therapy in both groups and PCI of obstructive non-CTO lesions encouraged in both groups. The primary endpoint was a composite of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, stroke, or any revascularization at 10 years, analyzed in the modified intention-to-treat group. RESULTS: Between March 2010 and October 2016, 834 patients were randomly assigned, and 804 of these patients were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis (413 CTO-PCI, 391 no CTO-PCI). Clinical follow-up at 10 years was complete in 688 patients (85.6%), without a significant between-group difference (P = 0.69). At 10 years, the primary endpoint had occurred in 134 patients in the CTO-PCI group and 138 patients in the no CTO-PCI group (Kaplan-Meier estimates: 33.9% vs 37.4%; risk difference: -3.5 percentage points; 95% CI: -10.4 to 3.3 percentage points; P = 0.32). Restricted mean event-free survival time at 10 years was also similar between groups (7.52 vs 7.53 years; difference: -0.01 years; 95% CI: -0.54 to 0.52 years; P = 0.97). Death from any cause did not differ significantly between groups (12.7% vs 16.5%; HR: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.52-1.12; P = 0.16). CONCLUSIONS: Over 10 years, an initial strategy of CTO-PCI was not associated with a significant difference in the primary endpoint or all-cause mortality compared with an initial strategy of no CTO-PCI. However, the wide CIs preclude definitive conclusions regarding the potential benefit or harm of an initial CTO-PCI strategy. (Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation Versus Optimal Medical Treatment in Patients With Chronic Total Occlusion [DECISION-CTO]; NCT01078051; extended follow-up, NCT06908499).
