Psychological Assets and Cardiovascular Health in Adulthood: A Mixed Methods Investigation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Psychological risk factors like depression increase risk for poor cardiovascular outcomes but psychological assets like purpose in life are protective and linked to reduced risk of cardiovascular events. However, most assets are investigated individually, and not all have been explored in relation to cardiovascular health (CVH). This study used mixed methods to assess multiple psychological assets and evaluate associations with CVH 12 years later. METHODS: Data came from 2092 participants in the National Child Development Study. At age 50 years, participants wrote open-ended responses describing their futures. Two trained researchers qualitatively coded each response by rating them for 7 commonly assessed psychological assets (1=not at all; 7=very): optimism, purpose, satisfaction, personal growth, agency, enjoyment, and overall positivity. At age 62, CVH behavioral factors (exercise, smoking status, sleep) were self-reported; CVH clinical factors (blood pressure, lipids, glucose, body weight) were measured during nurse visits. Following Life's Essential 8 guidelines, CVH components were combined into total CVH scores. Linear regressions examined associations between each age 50 asset and age 62 CVH scores, adjusting for age 50 confounders. RESULTS: All age 50 assets were positively associated with better CVH scores 12 years later, accounting for sociodemographic characteristics and word counts (p≤0.05). Purpose (b=0.81 [95% CI, 0.33-1.29]) and personal growth (b=0.82 [95% CI, 0.34-1.20]) showed the strongest associations with CVH in fully adjusted models. CONCLUSIONS: Higher levels of most midlife psychological assets were linked with better CVH over time, suggesting multiple paths to health protection. These findings highlight assets that could be prevention targets.

Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.
recs.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes. DESIGN: Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial. SETTING: 145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China. PARTICIPANTS: 12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume. RESULTS: 6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference -0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm3, 95% CI -0.15 to -0.02; P=0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03808311.

recs.title: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection: implications for women's health, clinical care, and future research.
recs.abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an increasingly recognised cause of acute coronary syndromes, characterised by spontaneous separation of the layers of the coronary arterial wall. It predominantly affects younger women, and recent registry and imaging studies indicate that SCAD is more common than previously appreciated, challenging its historical classification as a rare condition. Clinically, SCAD is associated with a substantial early risk of adverse events, particularly in the first weeks after the index dissection. Given the high frequency of spontaneous healing, conservative management is preferred for most patients, whereas revascularisation is generally reserved for ongoing ischaemia or haemodynamic compromise. However, evidence to guide both pharmacological and interventional management remains scarce. This Review summarises current evidence on SCAD epidemiology, underlying mechanisms including genetic susceptibility, diagnostic approaches, management principles, implications for reproductive and women's health, and research priorities to improve outcomes for affected patients.

Biatrial Versus Left Atrial Maze Ablation During Cardiac Valve Surgery for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The ABLATION Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend concomitant surgical ablation during cardiac surgery in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the optimal lesion set remains uncertain, with ongoing debate regarding the relative benefits and risks of biatrial versus left atrial (LA) maze ablation. METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, single-blind trial, patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF undergoing rheumatic mitral valve surgery, with or without concomitant cardiac surgical procedures, were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo biatrial or LA maze ablation. The biatrial group underwent a complete Cox-Maze IV procedure; the LA group received a left-sided maze lesion set. To ensure standardization and consistency of the ablation procedures, surgeons underwent pretrial training and certification, and all procedures were videorecorded and centrally reviewed. The primary outcome was freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias lasting >30 seconds without antiarrhythmic drugs within 12 months. The key secondary end point was freedom from permanent pacemaker implantation. RESULTS: All 323 randomized patients were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (mean age, 56.5 years; 72.1% women; mean LA diameter, 51.9 mm). At 12 months, 78.7% of patients (129 of 164) in the biatrial group and 68.6% (109 of 159) in the LA group were free from atrial tachyarrhythmias (adjusted difference, 10.7% [1-sided lower 95% CI, 3%]; P=0.01). Freedom from permanent pacemaker implantation was noted in 97.0% (159 of 164) of the biatrial group and 98.1% (156 of 159) of the LA group, meeting the predefined noninferiority criterion with a margin of -5% (adjusted difference, -1.1% [1-sided lower 95% CI, -3.9%]; Pnoninferiority=0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF undergoing rheumatic cardiac valve surgery, biatrial maze ablation was superior to LA maze ablation in reducing recurrent atrial tachyarrhythmias, while maintaining noninferiority with respect to permanent pacemaker implantation. These findings provide direct evidence to inform lesion-set selection for surgical ablation during cardiac surgery. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT05021601.

Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Initial Clinical Experience.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), defined as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, remains challenging to treat because of its heterogeneous pathophysiology. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of transapical beating-heart septal myectomy in patients with symptomatic nHCM. METHODS: Patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory nHCM were prospectively enrolled to undergo transapical beating-heart septal myectomy through a left minithoracotomy. Under real-time transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, septal myectomy was tailored to relieve systolic cavity obliteration and mid-to-apical ventricular obstruction and to enlarge the left ventricular cavity. The primary end point was procedural success at 6 to 12 months postoperatively, defined as fulfillment of all prespecified criteria compared with baseline: ≥1-class improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, ≥10-point increase in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, ≥10-mL increase in stroke volume, and normal or grade I diastolic function. RESULTS: Between January 2023 and January 2025, 97 consecutive eligible patients with nHCM underwent transapical beating-heart septal myectomy at Tongji Hospital. At postoperative 6 to 12 months, procedural success was achieved in 87.6%. Specifically, New York Heart Association functional class I increased from 0% at baseline to 93.8% at follow-up, the median Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved from 64 (interquartile range, 56-69) to 87 (interquartile range, 82-92; P<0.001), the stroke volume increased from 53.5 mL (interquartile range, 41.0-66.6 mL) to 70.8 mL (interquartile range, 61.3-82.3 mL; P<0.001), and normal or grade I diastolic function increased from 65.6% to 97.9%. Among patients who underwent paired cardiopulmonary exercise testing (n=58), peak oxygen uptake increased by 1.1±2.9 mL/kg/min (P=0.008). In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis of 12 patients with paired 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography, coronary flow reserve increased from 1.8±0.3 to 2.0±0.4 (P=0.034). Adverse events included mitral valve injury (n=1) and ventricular septal perforation (n=1), the latter resulting in 1 postoperative death. CONCLUSIONS: Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy was associated with favorable left ventricular geometric remodeling and meaningful improvements in symptoms, health status, and functional capacity in selected patients with symptomatic nHCM. Being a potential therapeutic option for a previously difficult-to-treat population, it warrants further evaluation in controlled, multicenter studies. Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Postarrest Cardiac Procedures for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective postarrest care facilitates optimal outcomes for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Relatively little research has evaluated whether there may be racial or ethnic disparities in the workup and management of the patient post arrest. METHODS: We retrospectively studied out-of-hospital cardiac arrests using the TriNetX research database. We defined out-of-hospital cardiac arrest as any emergency department visit (2013-2024) with a diagnosis of cardiac arrest and included patients who survived to admission. Multivariate adjusted logistic regression was used to compare rates of the following cardiac interventions across race or ethnicity: (1) echocardiography; (2) left heart catheterization; (3) percutaneous coronary intervention; (4) ventricular assist device placement; and (5) automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement. RESULTS: A total of 58 394 cases of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest met inclusion criteria. Compared with White patients (left heart catheterization: 13.9%, percutaneous coronary intervention: 7.1%, ventricular assist device: 3.0%, automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator: 0.9%), Black patients had lower odds of receiving left heart catheterization (7.2%, adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.60 [95% CI, 0.55-0.64]), percutaneous coronary intervention (2.6%, aOR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.42-0.53]), ventricular assist device placement (1.6%, aOR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.60-0.80]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.41-0.70]). Hispanic/Latino patients were also less likely to receive left heart catheterization (8.9%, aOR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.64-0.80]), percutaneous coronary intervention (3.7%, aOR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.53-0.74]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.33-0.81]). CONCLUSIONS: Our large multicenter analysis identifies racial or ethnic disparities in postarrest cardiac workup and management. Further research is needed to identify potential causes for these disparities with the hope of developing strategies to address them.

recs.title: Life Expectancy After Incident Ischemic Stroke in a Bi-Ethnic Population: Estimates Over 2005 to 2022.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study measured 5- and 10-year life expectancy after an incident ischemic stroke using a high-quality sample of Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White patients over a recent period. METHODS: Data were from the Brain Attack Surveillance in Corpus Christi Project. The sample included 2011 Mexican American and 1262 non-Hispanic White men and women who had an incident ischemic stroke during 2005 to 2022 and were aged 45 years or older at the time of stroke. Participants were followed up to 18 years. Primary outcome was 5- and 10-year life expectancy. Discrete-time logistic regression models were implemented. RESULTS: Mean age at incident stroke was 69 years. There was no difference in the odds of dying between Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White men and women after adjustment for age at stroke and sex. Among men, an incident stroke at age 70 years was associated with a 10-year life expectancy of 6.4 years (95% CI: 6.1-6.6) in Mexican Americans and 6.5 years (95% CI: 6.2-6.9) in non-Hispanic White adults. Among women, the analogous 10-year life expectancy was 6.7 years (95% CI: 6.3-6.8) in Mexican Americans and 6.8 years (95% CI: 6.4-7.0) in non-Hispanic White adults. Comparing these estimates to life expectancy at age 70 in the general US population indicates that stroke is associated with a life shortening effect of 2.1 to 2.4 years over 10 years. CONCLUSIONS: Life expectancy after an ischemic stroke did not differ between Mexican Americans and non-Hispanic White adults. Incident ischemic stroke remains associated with substantial life shortening effects in the recent period.

recs.title: Surgical Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation.
recs.abstract: Atrial fibrillation is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is associated with an increased risk of stroke, heart failure, mortality, and reduced quality of life. Although catheter ablation is the most widely used rhythm control strategy, its efficacy is limited in patients with non-paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and large left atria. To address this therapeutic gap, surgical approaches, including minimally invasive ablation, hybrid epicardial-endocardial strategies, and left atrial appendage exclusion, have continued to evolve. In this review, we focus on recent evidence to guide clinical decision-making on patient selection, advances in minimally invasive surgical and hybrid techniques, left atrial appendage exclusion, and postoperative anticoagulation management. Minimally invasive standalone Cox-Maze IV procedure and hybrid epicardial-endocardial ablation have demonstrated superior long-term freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias compared with thoracoscopic epicardial surgical ablation or catheter ablation alone. Five-year arrhythmia-free survival has approached 85% to 95% in experienced centers after the Cox-Maze IV procedure and approximately 60% to 70% after hybrid ablation, compared with 35% to 45% after thoracoscopic epicardial ablation and 30% to 35% after single catheter ablation alone. Surgical left atrial appendage exclusion performed at the time of ablation may further reduce thromboembolic risk, although the optimal strategy for postprocedural anticoagulation remains uncertain. Careful patient selection remains essential, with atrial fibrillation type, duration, left atrial size, and previous treatment failure known to be key predictors of procedural success. As surgical techniques and supporting evidence continue to grow, standalone surgical ablation may assume a more important role in the contemporary management of atrial fibrillation, particularly for patients with advanced disease who are unlikely to achieve durable rhythm control with catheter ablation alone.

recs.title: Congestion Assessed With Inferior Vena Cava Ultrasound Predicts Long-Term Outcomes in Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Inferior vena cava (IVC) parameters relate to clinical outcomes in retrospective acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) studies, but prospective data on long-term outcomes and quality of life are unavailable. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate the prognostic value of IVC parameters for clinical outcomes and their association with quality of life. METHODS: Patients admitted for ADHF were prospectively enrolled from January 2022 to May 2024. Point-of-care IVC ultrasound was performed at admission and discharge. The Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) was evaluated at baseline, 1, 6, and 12 months. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and ADHF rehospitalization at 12 months. RESULTS: A total of 100 patients (median age 67 years, 28% women, 45% NYHA functional class III/IV, 65% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction) were included. The primary endpoint occurred in 50 patients (9 deaths and 41 ADHF hospitalizations). In multivariable analysis, admission minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.6 cm (HR: 3.71; 95% CI: 1.97-7.01; P < 0.001), admission maximum IVC diameter >2.3 cm (HR: 2.70; 95% CI: 1.46-4.96; P = 0.001), discharge minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.3 cm (HR: 2.27; 95% CI: 1.24-4.14; P = 0.008), and discharge sniff IVC collapsibility index <36% (HR: 3.16; 95% CI: 1.64-6.06; P < 0.001) were independent predictors of the primary endpoint. KCCQ scores improved during follow-up (Ptime<0.001) but were not associated with the primary endpoint. Patients with admission minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.6 cm had lower KCCQ scores throughout the study period (Pgroup = 0.03). CONCLUSIONS: In ADHF patients, IVC parameters predict 12-month outcomes and may serve as objective markers to identify residual congestion and stratify risk.

Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
recs.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a common cause of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in patients with pneumonia, sepsis, aspiration of gastric contents, severe trauma, or other inciting triggers. Although the definition of the syndrome has evolved over the past several decades, the core elements (acute onset, hypoxemia, and bilateral radiographic opacities) remain consistent. Critical components of management include identification and treatment of the underlying cause of ARDS as well as avoidance of ventilator-induced lung injury and volume overload. Ongoing areas of controversy include the best strategy for supporting nonintubated patients, personalization of positive end-expiratory pressure, the role of innovative ventilatory strategies, and the use of glucocorticoids. New research suggests that precision medicine approaches to ARDS management that focus on discrete biologic, radiographic, or physiological subphenotypes may improve outcomes, and prospective trials of these approaches are ongoing.

recs.title: Renal Insufficiency and Clinical Outcomes in Acute Ischemic Stroke With Large Infarct: A Prospective Cohort Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate whether renal insufficiency (RI) modifies the effectiveness and safety of endovascular treatment (EVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke and large infarct in a real-world setting. METHODS: This study was a post hoc analysis of a prospective multicenter cohort study. RI was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate <90 mL/min per 1.73 m2 on admission. Patients were treated with EVT plus standard medical treatment or standard medical treatment alone and were stratified by RI status. The primary effectiveness outcome was favorable outcome (modified Rankin scale 0-3) at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and 90-day mortality. RESULTS: Among 745 patients with acute ischemic stroke and large infarct, 343 (46.0%) had RI and 490 (65.8%) underwent EVT. Compared with standard medical treatment, EVT was associated with improved functional outcomes (modified Rankin scale 0-3) in both the RI (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 2.55 [95% CI, 1.15-5.68], P=0.022) and the non-RI group (adjusted OR 2.65 [95% CI, 1.49-4.73], P=0.001). EVT was also associated with higher risks of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage in both groups (P=0.002 and 0.007, respectively), whereas no significant difference in mortality was observed. Results were consistent in the inverse probability-weighted analyses. No statistically significant interaction was observed between RI status and treatment effect for effectiveness or safety outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute ischemic stroke and large infarct, EVT was associated with improved functional outcomes but a higher risk of hemorrhagic complications. We did not find statistically significant evidence of interaction between EVT and RI status for 90-day outcomes.

The PELICANS Registry: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy Extended Longitudinal Investigation of Clinical Outcomes-Adverse Events, Nonrecovery, and Survival.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) disproportionately affects Black women, yet long-term outcome data in socially vulnerable, predominantly Black cohorts remain limited. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to characterize long-term outcomes and baseline predictors of survival, major adverse events (MAEs), and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) recovery in a U.S. PPCM cohort. METHODS: This retrospective-prospective registry included 159 women with PPCM (1982-2024). Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, MAEs, and LVEF recovery (≥50%). Multivariable and extended Cox models evaluated predictors, adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy. RESULTS: The cohort was 80.5% Black. Over a median 9.0-year follow-up (IQR: 3.4-15.5), 41 patients (25.8%) died and 64 (40.3%) had MAEs. Among 148 patients with echocardiographic follow-up, 69 (46.6%) had sustained LVEF recovery, though 23 (25.0% of initially recovered) declined to LVEF <50%. Independent mortality predictors included elevated creatinine (adjusted HR [aHR]: 2.86; 95% CI: 1.37-5.97), lower index LVEF (aHR: 0.94; 95% CI: 0.90-0.98), family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure (aHR: 3.27; 95% CI: 1.41-7.56), and non-O blood type (aHR: 2.36; 95% CI: 1.04-5.33), retaining significance after adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy (n = 62). Elevated creatinine increased MAE odds (adjusted OR: 7.09; 95% CI: 1.98-32.9), while higher LVEF, parity, and obesity reduced them. Baseline LV dilation (≥60 mm), Black race, older age, and family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure predicted lower LVEF recovery odds. CONCLUSIONS: This long-term predominantly Black PPCM cohort had high mortality, low LVEF recovery, and frequent late relapse. These findings highlight the importance of baseline risk stratification and sustained echocardiographic surveillance to guide clinical decision-making.

Effects of Exercise Preconditioning on Promoting Endogenous Recovery Responses After Ischemic Stroke in Late-Adult Mice.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes substantial neurological impairment, and although poststroke rehabilitation can support recovery, neurological deficits often limit the feasibility of exercise in clinical settings. Prestroke exercise has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance resilience to ischemic injury, but most preclinical studies have relied on young adult rodents, in which spontaneous recovery can sometimes obscure clinically meaningful functional effects. However, the impact of exercise preconditioning in later stages of adulthood remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated whether a treadmill exercise preconditioning regimen confers neuroprotection and improves recovery-related responses in late-adult mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion. METHODS: Eight-month-old male mice were assigned to sedentary or exercise groups. Following 5 weeks of treadmill running (5 days per week after 1 week of acclimatization), mice underwent 45 minutes of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion. Behavioral assessments and body-weight monitoring were performed before and after middle cerebral artery occlusion. Infarct volume and cellular responses were evaluated 14 days after stroke. RESULTS: Fourteen days after stroke, lesion volume was significantly reduced in the exercise group compared with sedentary controls. Exercise preconditioning enhanced neurogenesis, oligodendrogenesis, and CD31-positive vascular responses while suppressing reactive astrocyte activation. Functional improvements were consistently observed across multiple behavioral assays in late-adult mice. CONCLUSIONS: Preconditioning with treadmill exercise provides neuroprotection against ischemic stroke in late-adult mice by reducing infarct volume and promoting recovery-associated cellular responses. These findings demonstrate that the functional benefits of prestroke exercise extend beyond the young adult stage and support the potential value of regular physical activity as a strategy to mitigate ischemic brain injury later in adulthood.

recs.title: Long working hours and cardiometabolic multimorbidity progression: a prospective multistate analysis in the UK Biobank.
recs.abstract: AIMS: The association of long working hours with cardiometabolic disease accumulation remains unclear. Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) was defined as the coexistence of at least two of the following conditions: type 2 diabetes, ischaemic heart disease and stroke. METHODS: We studied 269,197 employed UK Biobank participants free of cardiometabolic disease (CMD) at baseline. Weekly working hours were analysed in five categories, with 35-40 h/week as reference. Cox models assessed incident first CMD (FCMD), CMM and all-cause mortality. Multistate models assessed progression from no CMD to FCMD and from FCMD to CMM, with death possible from each state. Models were adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, occupational and family-history factors. Estimates were pooled across 50 multiply imputed datasets. RESULTS: Within the disease observation window, 25,190 participants developed FCMD and 2,824 developed CMM. Working ≥55 h/week was associated with FCMD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.117, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.057-1.180). Incident CMM from baseline was associated with 41-48 h/week (1.128, 1.010-1.260) and 49-54 h/week (1.205, 1.042-1.393); the estimate for ≥55 h/week was 1.144 (0.973-1.346). For FCMD-to-CMM progression, the corresponding HR were 1.141 (1.021-1.274), 1.129 (0.976-1.306) and 1.093 (0.929-1.286). Spline analyses supported overall associations with FCMD and incident CMM from baseline (both P<0.001), but not a clear association with FCMD-to-CMM progression (P=0.083). CONCLUSION: Long working hours were associated with first CMD onset and incident CMM in some working-hour groups; FCMD-to-CMM progression showed no clear increasing gradient. These findings support considering working time in cardiometabolic risk assessment while distinguishing initial disease development from subsequent progression.

recs.title: Longitudinal Trends of Intact and Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repairs in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted access to elective procedures and routine care. Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes. METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database. We included 423 874 patients diagnosed with AAA from 2016 to 2024. Patients were categorized by clinical presentation-intact AAA and ruptured AAA-and stratified by surgical approach: endovascular aneurysm repair or open aneurysm repair. Annual trends in AAA repair rates were assessed using joinpoint regression to calculate annual percentage change. RESULTS: Among 19 330 AAA repairs, 3791 (19.6%) were open aneurysm repair, and 15 539 (80.4%) were endovascular aneurysm repair. From 2018 to 2024, 1623 repairs (9.9%) were for ruptured AAA and 14 835 (90.1%) were for intact AAA. The rate of intact AAA repairs initially remained stable from 2018 to 2022 but significantly decreased after the pandemic from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -2.87% [95% CI, -10.95 to -1.00]). In contrast, ruptured AAA repairs rates shifted sharply during the pandemic, with an established prepandemic decline in ruptured repairs from 2018 to 2020 (annual percentage change, -11.48%) reversed, with an increase from 2020 to 2022 (annual percentage change +12.01%), before declining from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -11.00%). CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, repairs for intact AAA declined, while repairs for ruptured AAA increased during the pandemic period. These trends suggest that potential delays in routine surveillance and elective surgery during the pandemic may have increased acute presentations.

Association Between Saturated Fat Intake and Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Across the Genetic Spectrum.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Guidelines recommend reducing saturated fat intake to lower LDL-C, but dietary effects are heterogeneous. OBJECTIVES: We examined whether genetic propensity for higher LDL-C modifies the association of saturated fat intake with LDL-C and incident ASCVD. METHODS: Among 20,940 genotyped Women's Health Initiative participants, we examined saturated fat intake from food frequency questionnaires and a polygenic score for LDL-C (PGSLDL). The primary outcome was LDL-C. The secondary outcome was incident ASCVD. Associations were assessed using multivariable linear and Cox regressions. Effect modification was evaluated using interaction terms and restricted cubic splines. Models included demographic, lifestyle, clinical, and genetic covariates. RESULTS: The association between saturated fat intake and LDL-C was modified by PGSLDL (P interaction for LDL-C = 0.01). Spline analysis revealed a nonlinear interaction, with increasing effect sizes across the upper end of the PGSLDL distribution. Among 16,835 participants without prevalent ASCVD, 1,582 experienced incident ASCVD (median follow-up: 10 years [Q1, Q3: 9.4, 10.0]). A 5% isocaloric increase in saturated fat intake was associated with a higher ASCVD risk among individuals in the top quartile of PGSLDL (HR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.08-1.47), but no association was observed among those in the bottom 3 quartiles (HR: 1.00; 95% CI: 0.89-1.12); P interaction for ASCVD = 0.006. CONCLUSIONS: The association between saturated fat intake and LDL-C and subsequent ASCVD risk may be stronger for individuals with a genetic propensity towards high LDL-C.

recs.title: Atrial Fibrillation Screening-to-Anticoagulation Pathways in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an important cause of preventable stroke in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where diagnostic and treatment gaps may limit screening effectiveness. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate AF screening in LMICs as a screening-to-anticoagulation pathway, focusing on reach, equity, diagnostic confirmation, anticoagulation uptake, and health-system capacity. METHODS: MEDLINE via PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to July 2026. LMIC studies reporting population-facing AF screening or screening-linked care were included. Logit-transformed proportions were pooled using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp CIs; binomial-normal generalized linear mixed models were used in sensitivity analyses. Pathway stages were synthesized from outcome-specific study subsets rather than a single longitudinal cohort. RESULTS: Thirty-seven reports from 13 LMICs and 1 multinational cohort were included. Across 22 community- or population-based studies, confirmed AF averaged 1.24% (95% CI: 0.79%-1.94%; I2 = 98.8%; 95% prediction interval: 0.16%-8.83%). Newly detected AF averaged 0.95% (95% CI: 0.43%-2.11%; I2 = 99.2%; prediction interval: 0.08%-9.97%). In separate study subsets, prior AF awareness was 50.7%, study-defined high stroke risk or oral anticoagulation indication was 78.9%, and oral anticoagulation coverage among study-defined eligible/high-risk participants was 22.8%. Reach ranged from 9.7% to 98.8%, and confirmation completion was 57.5% to 61.8% in 2 programs. CONCLUSIONS: AF screening in LMICs identifies substantial but highly variable detection and treatment gaps. Pooled proportions should be interpreted as cross-study summaries rather than expected rates for a specific setting. Effective programs require representative reach, timely confirmation, appropriate stroke-risk and valvular assessment, access to anticoagulation, and longitudinal follow-up.

recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Women sex is an established, nonmodifiable risk factor for adverse outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has been proposed as an alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in patients with AF; however, there are limited data on sex-based outcomes of LAAC following catheter ablation. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare outcomes of LAAC vs OAC after AF ablation in men and women. METHODS: Patients with AF and CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2 in men and ≥3 in women were randomized 1:1 to either ablation + LAAC or ablation + OAC. The primary safety endpoint was nonprocedural major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding at 36 months. The primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of all-cause death, stroke, or systemic embolism at 36 months. RESULTS: The study included 1,053 men and 546 women. LAAC and OAC demonstrated comparable primary efficacy events in men (HR: 0.96; 95% CI: 0.56-1.65; P = 0.88) and women (HR: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.41-1.62; P = 0.55), with no treatment-by-sex interaction (P interaction = 0.71). Procedural complication rates were similar at 2.3% in men and 3.7% in women with only 1 pericardial effusion in each group, not related to the index LAAC procedure. At 36 months, the primary safety endpoint was significantly lower in the device group among men (HR: 0.34; 95% CI: 0.23-0.50; P < 0.0001). In women, a similar but nonsignificant trend was observed (HR: 0.68; 95% CI: 0.42-1.09; P = 0.11), with a significant treatment-by-sex interaction (P interaction = 0.02). No significant difference was seen in the secondary safety endpoint across both treatment arms for either sex. CONCLUSIONS: In this prespecified analysis of the OPTION (Comparison of Anticoagulation With Left Atrial Appendage Closure After AF Ablation [OPTION]) trial, stroke, systemic embolism, and mortality outcomes were not significantly different between LAAC and OAC following AF ablation in either men or women. Compared with OAC, LAAC demonstrated a greater magnitude of major and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding reduction in men as compared with women. (Comparison of Anticoagulation With Left Atrial Appendage Closure After AF Ablation [OPTION]; NCT03795298).

recs.title: Thirty-Day All-Cause Readmissions After Pregnancy-Associated Hospitalizations With Heart Failure in the United States: Analysis of the Nationwide Readmissions Database.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of pregnancy-related morbidity and mortality in the United States. There is a paucity of data regarding pregnancy-associated heart failure readmissions. This study aims to characterize the 30-day heart failure readmission patterns in pregnancy-associated admissions. METHODS: The National Readmission Database from 2016 to 2021 was used to identify women aged 13 to 49 with an index hospitalization with heart failure as the primary or secondary diagnosis during a pregnancy-related admission, identified by diagnosis-related group codes and International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission. Survey-weighted descriptive analyses and hierarchical multivariable logistic regression were used to characterize readmission patterns and identify independently associated factors. RESULTS: Among 19 452 eligible index hospitalizations, 2659 were followed by a 30-day readmission; the survey-weighted readmission rate was 13.5%. In the fully adjusted model, Medicare and Medicaid coverage, residence in a small metropolitan area, greater All Patient Refined Diagnosis-Related Group severity, discharge with home health care, and discharge against medical advice were associated with higher odds of readmission. Deficiency anemia, chronic pulmonary disease, diabetes without chronic complications, renal failure, solid tumor without metastasis, and cardiovascular or respiratory disorders complicating pregnancy were also independently associated with increased readmission. CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 1 in 7 pregnancy-associated hospitalizations complicated by heart failure was followed by a 30-day all-cause readmission. Readmission risk reflected a combination of illness severity, discharge disposition, payer status, geographic location, and selected medical and pregnancy-related comorbidities. These findings support the development and evaluation of individualized, multidisciplinary transitional-care strategies for patients at highest risk.

recs.abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation can cure certain hematological disorders but has many complications. In retrospective studies, low gut microbiome diversity is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. In 2023, the Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1703 randomized phase 3 trial demonstrated the superiority of post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) and mycophenolate mofetil to tacrolimus and methotrexate (Tac/MTX) for graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis in participants with hematological malignancies undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. Here we report on the microbiome-focused companion study to 1703, Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1801, which coenrolled participants and shared trial registration. The primary endpoint was association between microbiome diversity at neutrophil engraftment and non-relapse mortality after 1 year; secondary endpoints included associations with other clinical outcomes and with baseline microbiome diversity. Based on 2575 longitudinally collected stool samples from 304 participants (Tac/MTX n = 147, PTCy n = 157), no association between engraftment microbiome diversity and non-relapse mortality was observed (P = 0.314), not meeting the primary endpoint. Lower baseline microbiome diversity was associated with shorter overall survival (P = 0.007). Safety data were reported in the original 1703 publication. In exploratory analyses, microbiome diversity and absolute microbial load were lower in PTCy compared to Tac/MTX on days 14-28 following HCT, independent of non-prophylaxis antibiotics exposure. Microbial domination events, when a single species exceeds 30% relative abundance, did not differ significantly between study arms and reflected both pathogen blooms and less severe disruptions of the microbial community. Clostridium scindens and secondary bile-acid metabolism pathways were less prevalent in PTCy than in Tac/MTX following HCT. In summary, we find prophylaxis regimens likely exert independent effects on both the microbiome and immune compartments and can also impact their interaction. Understanding whether and how microbiome-targeted interventions might improve transplant outcomes will therefore require careful disentangling of these effects within each specific treatment context. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03959241 .

Ultraprocessed Food Consumption and Incident Heart Failure: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) are associated with adverse cardiometabolic outcomes and increased atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. However, the relationship between UPF intake and incident heart failure (HF) remains incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: The aims of this study were to examine the relationship between UPF consumption and incident HF and to evaluate potential biological mediators. METHODS: A sample of 6,531 U.S. adults 45-84 years of age without cardiovascular disease at baseline from MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) was analyzed. UPF intake was classified according to the Nova system. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations between UPF intake and incident HF. Phenotypes were classified as heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (ejection fraction <50%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (ejection fraction ≥50%). Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate the potential mediating role of waist-to-height ratio as a surrogate measure for central adiposity. RESULTS: Higher UPF intake was significantly associated with increased risk of incident HF across sequentially adjusted models. In the primary model (model 2), each additional daily serving of UPF was associated with a 5% higher risk of incident HF (HR: 1.052; 95% CI: 1.002-1.103). When stratified by phenotype, UPF intake remained significantly associated with HFpEF (HR: 1.096; 95% CI: 1.016-1.183) but not HFrEF. Participants in the upper 80% of UPF intake had a >2-fold higher risk for HFpEF than those in the lowest 20% (HR: 2.234; 95% CI: 1.289-3.874). In mediation analyses, waist-to-height ratio statistically accounted for ∼51% of the association between UPF intake and total HF and 49% of the association between UPF intake and HFpEF. CONCLUSIONS: Higher UPF consumption was significantly associated with an increased risk for incident HF, with associations driven primarily by the HFpEF phenotype. Central adiposity, measured by waist-to-height ratio, demonstrated a potential mediating role, suggesting that obesity-related cardiometabolic pathways may represent an important pathway linking UPF consumption to HF risk.

Aortic Valve Stenosis Screening Using Deep Learning on Noninvasive Arterial Pressure Waveforms.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic stenosis (AS) presents a significant health burden. Early identification of significant AS, defined as at least moderate AS, may facilitate timely confirmatory testing, referral, and management. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop and externally validate a deep learning model applied to arterial pressure waveforms obtained from a noninvasive finger-cuff system to screen for significant AS, using transthoracic echocardiography as the reference standard. METHODS: This prospective international multicenter cohort study was conducted from December 2020 through July 2025. Participants underwent concurrent transthoracic echocardiography and noninvasive arterial pressure waveform acquisition. A 1-dimensional convolutional neural network was developed using the Cleveland Clinic development cohort and evaluated in a temporally distinct, multicenter validation cohort including sites in the United States, Spain, and the Netherlands. RESULTS: Significant AS was present in 307 of 3,634 (8.4%) patients in the development cohort and 241 of 1,336 (18.0%) in the validation cohort. In the validation cohort, the model demonstrated an area under the curve of 0.893 (95% CI: 0.876-0.910), with a sensitivity of 92.5% (223/241; 95% CI: 88.5%-95.2%), negative predictive value of 97.5% (706/724; 95% CI: 96.1%-98.4%), specificity of 64.5% (706/1,095; 95% CI: 61.6%-67.3%), and positive predictive value of 36.4% (223/612; 95% CI: 32.7%-40.3%). For severe AS, the area under the curve was 0.906 (95% CI: 0.890-0.922), with a sensitivity of 94.3% (183/194; 95% CI: 90.1%-96.8%), negative predictive value of 98.5% (706/717; 95% CI: 97.3%-99.1%), specificity of 64.5% (706/1,095; 95% CI: 61.6%-67.3%), and positive predictive value of 32% (183/572; 95% CI: 28.3%-35.9%). CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning applied to arterial pressure waveforms obtained from a finger-cuff system serves as a promising screening test for significant AS.

Comparative Accuracy of the European Society of Cardiology Rapid Rule-Out and Rule-In Protocols for Diagnosing Non-ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Network Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The European Society of Cardiology rapid rule-out and rule-in protocols using hs-cTns (high-sensitivity cardiac troponins) with blood collection at 0 and 1 hour (0/1 hour), 0 and 2 hours (0/2 hours), and 0 and 3 hours (0/3 hours) are accurate and widely used for evaluating non-ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction. This network meta-analysis aimed to identify the best performing hs-cTn assay. METHODS: We conducted database searches up to January 15, 2026, a dual screening and eligibility assessment, independent data extraction and risk of bias assessment, a network meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy, and assessment of the certainty of evidence. Only full-paired diagnostic accuracy studies conducted in the emergency department were included. RESULTS: Ten prospective studies (15 publications) comparing 10 assays using the 0-/1-hour algorithm (n=8769), 0-/2-hour algorithm (n=1881), and 0-/3-hour algorithm (n=1236) were included. Comparisons between newer and conventional assays largely stemmed from a single-source study. Across all assays, the European Society of Cardiology 0-/1-hour algorithm demonstrated high sensitivity (summary point estimate range: 97.8%-99.8%). Furthermore, it maintained high specificity (89.8%-98.1%), with no assay showing clear superiority. The summary sensitivity and specificity did not show significant differences across assays after adjusting for biases because of imperfect reference standards. Comparative data in the European Society of Cardiology 0-/2-hour and 0-/3-hour algorithms were limited. CONCLUSIONS: Evidence remains insufficient to establish the superiority of any specific hs-cTn assay within the European Society of Cardiology 0-/1-hour algorithm. Although practical considerations may currently guide selection, continued validation of newer assays remains necessary.

Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Direct Oral Anticoagulation in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion With Watchman FLX.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal antithrombotic therapy after left atrial appendage occlusion remains uncertain. METHODS: We studied 2817 patients undergoing left atrial appendage occlusion at 8 hospitals from 2016 to 2023 using registry data linked to Medicare claims. Among 2448 Watchman FLX recipients, the primary exposure was time-varying dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) versus pooled direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC)-based therapy. Outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), major bleeding, and device complications. The primary instrumental-variable analysis used operator FLX preference; overlap weighting was secondary and pairwise regimen comparisons exploratory. RESULTS: DAPT was associated with lower MACE (absolute risk difference [ARD], -1.5% [95% CI, -1.9% to -1.0%]; number needed to treat, 67) and major bleeding (ARD -1.6% [95% CI, -2.0% to -0.9%]; number needed to treat, 63) than pooled DOAC-based therapy, without increased device complications. Overlap-weighted associations with MACE and major bleeding were nonsignificant. In exploratory pairwise analyses, DAPT did not differ significantly from DOAC monotherapy for MACE or major bleeding; lower major bleeding was limited to DAPT versus DOAC plus single antiplatelet therapy (ARD, -0.6% [95% CI, -1.1% to -0.2%]; P=0.008). Most estimated benefit accrued within 6 months. CONCLUSIONS: DAPT was associated with lower MACE and major bleeding than pooled DOAC-based therapy after Watchman FLX implantation. The safety benefit was concentrated in the comparison with DOAC + single antiplatelet therapy, whereas DAPT and DOAC monotherapy did not clearly differ in either outcome. These findings support randomized trials comparing DAPT with DOAC monotherapy.

Sex-Specific Phenotypic Architecture in Cardiac Amyloidosis Identified by Explainable Machine Learning.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Females are under-represented in cardiac amyloidosis (CA), but whether this reflects sex-associated phenotypic heterogeneity or differences in disease prevalence remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to characterize sex-associated differences in presentation and prognosis across CA subtypes using unsupervised clustering. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 2,216 patients with confirmed CA enrolled between 2010 and 2022: light-chain amyloidosis (AL) (n = 583), variant transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) (n = 432), and wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRwt) (n = 1,201). Self-organizing maps with k-means partitioning were applied separately to each subtype, and conditional inference trees identified key phenotypic discriminators. RESULTS: Females represented 40.8%, 33.8%, and 15.9% of AL, ATTRv, and ATTRwt cohorts, respectively. Clustering identified 4 AL, 6 ATTRv, and 6 ATTRwt phenotypes. Across subtypes, female-predominant clusters generally showed preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, lower cardiac remodeling burden, and less pronounced biomarker elevation. Female-predominant AL clusters included preserved-function and multisystem profiles, whereas ATTRv clusters included neurologic-dominant and older cardiometabolic profiles. In ATTRwt, females were predominantly represented in a phenotype characterized by preserved systolic function and less structural remodeling. Conditional inference trees identified sex as the first discriminator in ATTRwt and a secondary discriminator in AL, whereas ATTRv clusters were primarily discriminated by cardiac variables and sex was not selected. CONCLUSIONS: Unsupervised clustering identified female-predominant phenotypes with less structural cardiac remodeling but distinct multisystem characteristics across CA subtypes. These findings support sex-associated phenotypic heterogeneity in CA and generate hypotheses regarding female underrepresentation in contemporary CA cohorts.

FGF13 Regulates Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via PGRN Glycosylation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Macrophage polarization and complement activation play a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury. FGF13 (fibroblast growth factor 13) is a critical regulator of cardiac homeostasis. However, the role and mechanism of FGF13 in myocardial I/R injury remain unclear. METHODS: FGF13 expression was detected in cardiomyocytes after hypoxia/reoxygenation and in hearts subjected to myocardial I/R. Cardiomyocyte-specific FGF13 knockout and adeno-associated virus serotype 9-mediated overexpression mice were generated. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses identified key downstream mechanisms. Immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation, and glycoproteomics identified PGRN (progranulin) as an FGF13-interacting protein and mapped its glycosylation site. Mechanistic studies were performed using Transwell cocultures of neonatal mouse cardiomyocytes and bone marrow-derived macrophages, together with molecular and biochemical approaches. Virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations identified a small-molecule FGF13 inhibitor. RESULTS: FGF13 was upregulated in cardiomyocytes after myocardial I/R. Cardiomyocyte-specific FGF13 knockout alleviated, whereas overexpression exacerbated, cardiac dysfunction and myocardial injury after I/R. Mechanistically, FGF13, through its asparagine 121 residue, competitively occupied the asparagine 263 glycosylation site of PGRN, sterically preventing STT3A (STT3 oligosaccharyltransferase complex catalytic subunit A)-mediated glycosylation of asparagine 263 and suppressing PGRN secretion. FGF13 depletion restored PGRN glycosylation and secretion, which activated macrophage TNFR2/PI3K/AKT (tumor necrosis factor receptor 2/phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B) signaling in a paracrine manner, promoted M2 polarization while suppressing M1 polarization, and inhibited complement activation and inflammation. The small-molecule FGF13 inhibitor CWD8 (1-[2-amino-2-methylpropyl]-5,5-dimethylpiperidin-3-ol) also attenuated myocardial I/R injury. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the critical role of FGF13 in myocardial I/R injury and reveal a competitive mechanism by which FGF13 hinders STT3A-mediated PGRN glycosylation. We identify the PGRN glycosylation-PI3K/AKT axis as the key downstream pathway mediating FGF13-regulated macrophage polarization and complement activation, suggesting that small-molecule FGF13 inhibitors may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for myocardial I/R injury.

Prediction of Stroke Outcome After Endovascular Thrombectomy From Clinical Characteristics: A Machine Learning Approach.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Predicting outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is challenging. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data. METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke. A total of 4353 patients who underwent EVT between 2016 and 2020 were included, with those from 2016 to 2019 assigned to the derivation cohort and those from 2020 to the validation cohort. The model was developed using 132 routinely collected clinical variables that can be rapidly obtained on patient arrival. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm, and the model was built using CatBoost. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 2 at discharge. RESULTS: Among 4353 patients treated with EVT, the derivation cohort included 2764 patients and the validation cohort, 1589 patients. In these cohorts, 973 (35.2%) and 547 (34.4%) achieved mRS 0 to 2, respectively. Boruta selected 47 predictors. CatBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.744 (95% CI, 0.710-0.776) in the derivation test set and 0.781 (95% CI, 0.755-0.803) in the validation cohort. Validation areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.792 (95% CI, 0.765-0.815) for mRS 0 to 1, 0.766 (95% CI, 0.744-0.787) for mRS 0 to 3, and 0.680 (95% CI, 0.631-0.729) for mRS 6. CONCLUSIONS: Our machine learning model predicted outcomes following EVT using only admission clinical data. This imaging-independent machine learning approach may support early prognostication and facilitate discussions of expected clinical courses.

recs.title: Incidence and predictors of de novo atrial fibrillation in patients with heart failure undergoing continuous rhythm monitoring.
recs.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with adverse clinical outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF). The true incidence of de novo AF in HF, however, remains uncertain. Moreover, the role of clinical variables and circulating biomarkers in AF risk stratification in this population is not well established. This study aimed to determine the incidence of AF in patients with HF using long-term continuous rhythm monitoring and to identify clinical, structural, and biomarker-based predictors. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective study included patients with HF and reduced or preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Long-term rhythm monitoring was performed using implantable loop recorders or single-chamber defibrillators without atrial leads and with ventricular pacing < 20%. Serial blood samples were obtained at baseline, during follow-up, and during HF decompensation, and analyzed using a multiplex panel of selected biomarkers. Multivariable analyses were performed using both baseline biomarker levels and laboratory values closest to AF onset or HF decompensation. RESULTS: A total of 345 patients were enrolled (79% male; median age 68 years; 53% with LVEF< 40%. During a median follow-up of 756 days, 86 patients (24.9%) developed AF episodes lasting > 6 minutes, and 64 patients (18.5%) died. Hypertension, left atrial volume, beta-blocker use, CA-125, NT-proBNP, COL4A1, and AT1-AA were independently associated with AF, whereas aldosterone receptor antagonist therapy was associated with a lower risk of HF (C-index, 0.74). Patients with persistent AF as the initial manifestation had significantly higher mortality than those with paroxysmal AF or no AF. NT-proBNP and COL4A1 were associated with mortality. Clinically relevant bradyarrhythmias and ventricular tachyarrhythmias were also detected. CONCLUSION: De novo AF is a common complication in patients with HF. Integrating clinical variables, structural parameters, and biomarkers improves the identification of patients at increased risk of developing AF. Continuous monitoring enables early detection of rhythm abnormalities that may influence therapeutic management.

recs.title: A novel small-molecule inhibitor of proteoglycan GAG-chain elongation that alone or in combination with rosuvastatin inhibits lipid deposition in the aortic walls of high-fat fed ApoE-/- mice.
recs.abstract: Subendothelial retention of atherogenic lipoproteins by vascular proteoglycans is a key initiating event in atherosclerosis. The elongation of glycosaminoglycan (GAG) chains on proteoglycans enhances lipid binding and retention. We have shown that the Smad2 transcription factor in the linker region is a common signalling intermediate that regulates GAG chain elongation in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). This study used a small molecule kinase inhibitor to investigate whether inhibition of the Smad2 transcription factor and GAG chain elongation in vitro correlates with a reduction in lipid deposition in vivo. We identified a potent new kinase inhibitor, Cyc12068, and tested its effects on PDGF-mediated GAG chain elongation in VSMCs by measuring mRNA expression of GAG biosynthesis genes and [35S]-sulfate incorporation into secreted proteoglycans. ApoE-/- mice were fed a high-fat diet for 12 weeks and treated with Cyc12068 alone or in combination with rosuvastatin. Aortic wall lipid deposition was quantified by en face Oil Red O staining. Plasma lipid parameters and aortic mRNA expression of GAG elongation genes were assessed. Cyc12068 dose-dependently inhibited PDGF-induced expression of GAG biosynthesis genes, [35S]-sulfate incorporation into secreted proteoglycans, and biglycan GAG chain elongation in VSMCs. Cyc12068 also suppressed PDGF-mediated Smad2 linker region phosphorylation. In high-fat diet-fed ApoE-/- mice, Cyc12068 reduced aortic wall lipid deposition both as monotherapy and in combination with rosuvastatin. Unlike rosuvastatin, Cyc12068 did not alter plasma lipid parameters, indicating that its anti-atherogenic effect was independent of systemic lipid lowering. Cyc12068 also reduced aortic expression of GAG elongation genes, whereas rosuvastatin no effect on this pathway. By demonstrating a reduction in aortic wall lipid deposition when Cyc12068 was administered alone or with rosuvastatin, these findings identify inhibition of proteoglycan GAG chain elongation as a potential vessel wall-directed strategy that is mechanistically distinct from lipid lowering therapy.

Fermentable dietary fiber controls blood pressure by lowering large intestinal pH and activating the proton-sensing receptor GPR65.
recs.abstract: High blood pressure (BP) is the most common cause of death globally due to increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Fermentable dietary fibers regulate BP through gut microbial production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), acidic metabolites. How SCFAs regulate BP remains unclear. Here we show that, in a phenome-wide association study, the proton-sensing G protein-coupled receptor GPR65 gene is associated with human hypertension and cardiorenal phenotypes. Fermentable dietary fibers, delivered as a type 2 resistant starch (RS2), regulated luminal and interstitial tissue pH in the large intestine through gut microbial SCFA production in mice. High RS2 intake reduced pH, increased cAMP production via GPR65 signaling and CREB phosphorylation, and restricted the release of pro-hypertensive inflammatory cytokines by CD8+ T cells. Gpr65-/- mice spontaneously developed hypertension, cardiac and renal hypertrophy, and fibrosis. The benefits of a high-RS2 diet, which prevented these effects, were reduced in Gpr65-/- mice. Adoptive transfers revealed that GPR65 deficiency in CD8+ T cells explained this phenotype.

recs.title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is a chronic, neurometabolic disease with limited options for medical treatments that are efficacious and durable. Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide is approved for the treatment of obesity in adolescents and adults, but data for its use in young children are lacking. METHODS: We conducted a phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity. Participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide or placebo for a period of 104 weeks, after which participants stopped taking semaglutide or placebo for a 7-week washout period. Both groups received counseling for lifestyle modification. The primary end point was the percent change in the body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) from baseline to week 68. The confirmatory secondary end point was a reduction in BMI category at week 68. RESULTS: Among 167 children who underwent randomization, 112 were assigned to receive semaglutide and 55 to receive placebo. At week 68, the mean percent change in BMI was -13.5% with semaglutide and 2.7% with placebo (estimated between-group difference, -16.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -19.4 to -12.9; P<0.001). The percent change in BMI at week 104 was -9.4% with semaglutide and 8.4% with placebo (between-group difference, -17.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -22.2 to -13.3). At week 68, a reduction in BMI category had occurred in 79% of the participants in the semaglutide group and in 23% of those in the placebo group (odds ratio, 7.8; 95% CI, 3.5 to 17.6; P<0.001), with the BMI below the threshold for obesity (the 95th percentile for age and sex) in 38% of the participants who received semaglutide and in 2% of those who received placebo. Adverse events occurred in 96% of the participants receiving semaglutide and in 93% of those receiving placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most common, occurred more frequently with semaglutide than with placebo, and led to discontinuation in 1 participant in the semaglutide group. CONCLUSIONS: Among children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity, treatment with semaglutide for 68 weeks resulted in a significantly greater mean percent reduction in BMI than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; STEP Young ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05726227.).
